nodes.title: ElevenLabs Agents public teardown (account-free): 56 graded claims from the 804-page docs index (258 page bodies saved as Markdown), the public OpenAPI (322 paths, 141 convai), pricing pages, 32 changelog entries, the incident.io status feed, 6 npm SDKs and the PyPI SDK, DNS/RDAP of 19 hostnames, passive captures of elevenlabs.io/agents and the signed-out app, one 25 s public demo call, 157 job posts, Trustpilot, GitHub issues and HN. Adversarially verified the same day: 37 claims re-checked, 2 downgraded to unknown (EL-21 Iowa media anchoring; EL-33 82-97% margin), 1 sub-claim refuted (EL-23 embeddings are intfloat open weights), 15 corrected or scoped. Grades now 44 observed, 7 inferred, 3 vendor-claimed, 2 unknown. sha256 manifest of 3,846 raw files.

ElevenLabs is building a lead-level outbound campaign product that is not public yet. The signed-out dashboard bundle carries a generated client for 16 unpublished /v1/convai/outbound-campaigns paths (18 operations): campaigns submit/pause/resume/stop/progress/calls/export, leads with useSuppressLead (DELETE a lead), an attention queue (resolve/retry), workspace config and pre-revoke-status, plus a dashboard page route /outbound-campaigns. Public conversation records already carry batch-call campaign metadata {campaign_id, campaign_lead_id, cold_attempt, conversation_type initial/retry/callback/redirect} (2026-08-31). The public product is still single-start batch calling with no calling window, retry policy or suppression. Of 335 unique convai/speech-engine paths in the bundle, 204 (243 operations) are absent from the public OpenAPI, including automations, task-agents, memories, templates and analytics queries. Counts re-done by the verifier with dedupe by normalised path; the lane first reported 23 and 326 of 568 because paths seen by both regexes were counted twice.

ElevenLabs has an India data-residency environment, but only on Enterprise. The 2026-10-17 parity row "no India region found" is wrong. in.residency.elevenlabs.io is a separate, blank workspace with limited migration; storage is in India, "processing may nevertheless occur outside", and Realtime v1 Max is not offered there. Observed: SIP signalling is regional. sip.rtc.elevenlabs.io is one GCP us-central1 IP and sip.rtc.in.residency.elevenlabs.io is asia-south1 (Mumbai). The answer is the same for Jio, Airtel and Azure Central India client subnets (ECS scope /0, no geo-DNS), and the static-IP SIP /24 (199.88.252.0/24) is registered to Eleven Labs Inc. Vendor-claimed: standard-workspace data and self-hosted LLMs are in the US, and residency "may" reduce latency. Unknown (verifier downgrade of EL-21): where RTP media and the agent runtime run for a standard Indian buyer, since the docs say SIP servers are distributed and RTP uses dynamic IPs, and so whether a ~200-250 ms India-US penalty per turn exists. EL-P08 measures it.

Exotel has been a first-class ElevenAgents telephony provider since 2026-06-01, alongside Twilio and SIP. Exotel's Voicebot applet streams 8 kHz PCM over a WebSocket to ElevenLabs; outbound uses Exotel Calls/connect with the buyer's own keys; the Mumbai and Singapore clusters are supported. Friction: Exotel support must first enable the gated Voicebot applet and provision channels (1-2 business days), and transfer needs a chained Connect applet. This is the self-serve route to a domestic Indian CLI that Vapi lacks. The India page also claims Ozonetel and Plivo integrations and Indian agent customers (Meesho, Cars24, TVS Motor; vendor-claimed).

ElevenAgents leaves Indian calling compliance to the buyer. The 258 saved docs pages never mention TRAI, DLT, NCPR/DND, the 140/160 series or Indian calling hours; the only telemarketing-law page is TCPA. The public batch API has no calling-window, DNC, consent or suppression field. AI disclosure and recording consent are contractual duties of the buyer. Twilio regional routing offers only us1/ie1/au1.

ElevenAgents all-in list price for an Indian outbound minute at FX 95: INR 8.17-8.92 via Exotel or Plivo, INR 15.8-16.5 in burst, INR 12.5-15.0 via Twilio. The platform fee is $0.08 = INR 7.60 on every plan, unchanged in USD since 2026-06-06, and alone is above the INR 3.5-7 Indian band (2.1-2.6x Sarvam all-in). The rest is LLM pass-through (INR 0.19-0.72, flash-lite rows; the default gemini-2.5-flash is not priced) and telephony (INR 0.38-0.60; Exotel is quote-gated and assumed equal to Plivo, and the Plivo route may be closed on a standard US-SIP workspace because Indian numbers need media anchored in India). The $0.08 fee is 3.3-3.9x the same ASR and TTS on ElevenLabs' own API list. A reconstructed-COGS margin (82-97%) is an analogue hypothesis that the verifier downgraded to unknown (EL-33).

nodes.title:
ElevenLabs v2 signals.
- Memory across calls has no feature docs. The only public mention is "user memories" under agent privacy settings in the versioning doc; the public PrivacyConfig has no memory field. The data model has memory entries (version, conversation/manual source, since 2026-04-27), and the dashboard calls /agents/{id}/memories and /agents/{id}/user-memory/preview.
- On widget traffic the default user_id is a FingerprintJS browser fingerprint (persisted in localStorage), so any per-user memory there is keyed to a device, not an authenticated person.
- Personalisation today is per call only: dynamic variables, overrides, user_id and initiation webhooks.
- The improvement loop is human-gated: Spotlight finds an issue, Architect proposes a branch with tests, a teammate merges, and experiments split traffic with manual promotion and no documented significance test.
- "Proactive proposals" and scheduled automations are announced; the bundle already calls /convai/automations and /triage-tickets/{id}/architect-dispatches.

nodes.rationale: Public evidence shows ElevenLabs owns the speech stack (ASR, TTS, turn model, S2S; embeddings are open weights), ships ~6 agent features a week, already offers domestic Indian telephony through Exotel (after a 1-2 business-day applet enablement), and has a leads/suppression/retries campaign product built but unpublished. Its margin is unknown: an analogue COGS estimate suggests room to cut price, but the verifier graded it unknown. Its public gaps for Indian outbound are India-region processing for self-serve buyers (the latency effect is unmeasured), Indian compliance controls, Hinglish handling on a configured agent (unmeasured; the public demo forces English) and India-specific failure reasons.
nodes.reverse_if: ElevenLabs makes outbound campaigns public with calling windows and suppression and offers India-region processing on self-serve plans; or the account phase measures handset p50 <= 1.5 s with >= 90% Hinglish language hold on the default configuration; or it prices Indian minutes at or below INR 4 all-in.

nodes.title: Within about one quarter, ElevenLabs could launch its hidden outbound-campaigns product (leads, retries, suppression) and cross-call memory, and cut its Indian price toward INR 4/min. Its margin is unknown (an analogue estimate of 82-97% was downgraded to unknown by the verifier), so how cheap a cut would be is unknown too. That would close the usability and price gaps VP is targeting, leaving India-resident latency (unmeasured), compliance and Hinglish quality.
nodes.mitigation: Re-run code/bundle_endpoints.py weekly against the signed-out app bundle and the public OpenAPI (radar watchlist), deduping by normalised path (code/verify_bundle_check.py), and diff the changelog. Build VP's Indian operator layer (DLT/140-160 declaration, NCPR scrub, consent ledger, IST windows, business-language outcomes) as the product, and keep India-resident processing on every plan.

Gupshup launched a self-serve console on 2026-09-04 with 100 free minutes, 'from INR 3.50/min', owned Indian numbers via Knowlarity and WhatsApp in the same agent, and sells to the Indian enterprises that already buy its messaging.

nodes.title: BFSI specialists funded in the window, one naming our beachhead: Desible.ai (INR 32 Cr seed-plus, 2026-10-07) lists a 'Policy Renewal Agent' and an 'Insurance Post-Sales & Onboarding Agent' on its homepage (observed); Navana (INR 40 Cr Series A, 2026-09-07) claims 100M+ BFSI minutes (vendor-claimed); Gnani publishes no price (observed) and claims 12M+ renewals. Inference: Indian sellers are packaging the operation rather than the tool. MyOperator withdrew its INR 5/min AI plan for a custom plan with a human 'AI Agent Manager' (observed); Samora escalates to trained human operators; Tata/TTBS and Caller.digital price per outcome (vendor-claimed). Pre-deployment simulation/evals ship at Gupshup, Cartesia, LiveKit, PolyAI, ThunderPhone and Ringg (often free) and are sold standalone by Coval and Hamming; voice plus WhatsApp in one agent is at 6+ radar vendors, extending l4a's 'only Ringg and ElevenLabs'.

AI layers are INR 3.02; support plus platform fee are about half the price. Contradicts ledger CMP-16 (INR 3-8 + 1-3 lakh/month).

Indian self-serve headline floor is INR 3.50/min from two vendors (Sarvam PAYG + INR 0.40 telephony; Gupshup 'from INR 3.50', telephony inclusion not stated); Ringg INR 6 all-in unchanged; global per-minute brains at 2 cents (PolyAI Dialog-RSN-1 API + tokens; ThunderPhone) and GPT-Live-1 at USD 0.05 flat.

nodes.title: Teardown lane regulation-segment: 60 graded claims (40 observed, 17 inferred, 3 vendor-claimed) and a 10-job compliance matrix. Built from re-fetched primary texts (TCCCPR 2018 plus all three amendments, the 1600/1601 directions, the DPDP Act and Rules from eGazette, RBI's 2026 recovery directions), 14 vendor compliance pages and Bolna's 257-chunk dashboard bundle. The harness refused the report.md write; its text is in the lane's structured output.

Proposed: post-sale first. Lead with due-date reminders (renewal and pre-due payment/EMI, with service-appointment reminders included), then onboarding/application follow-up. Pre-sale enters only in a second wave, as consented inbound-lead follow-up inside TRAI's 7-day inquiry window. Never cold outbound. Not in v1: market surveys and collections in default.
nodes.rationale: Service calls need no explicit consent (inferred consent lasts the contract's life), are never blocked by DND once FULLY BLOCK migrates to BLOCK PROMO, have no TRAI calling band, and are covered by DPDP s.7(a). A self-serve platform can therefore ship them compliantly with nothing outside its control. Promotional calls need 140xx, a 10:00-21:00 window and 7-day inquiry evidence. DND numbers (16% of subscribers) are reachable only with CRF-registered consent, and CRF upload is open only to 11 pilot banks; bought lists lose their DPDP basis on ~2027-05-13. Promotional volume is ~11x service volume, so this is a friction/risk choice, not a market-size one.
nodes.reverse_if: Any of the following. Buyer interviews show self-serve buyers' main job is inbound-lead follow-up (then add it to v1 with a consent ledger). TRAI opens CRF legacy-consent upload to all senders, or DPDP consent managers ship usable APIs. Counsel holds that non-BFSI, non-1601 senders may not make service calls from declared 10-digit numbers. TRAI adds an AI-specific consent rule or series for service calls. The A2P charge on declared numbers moves toward INR 0.50/min or per attempt. Measured pickup on 1600/declared CLIs is too low for reminders to work.

nodes.rationale: One promotional line turns a service call promotional (def (av)), and wrong-category templates are now sanctioned in their own right. Every vendor read leaves compliance to the buyer, and their docs are stale (no A2P declaration) or wrong (9-21 hours; 'voice needs no DLT'). Buyers rarely complain about compliance (1.3% of coded Indian complaints), so it is a floor, not the wedge.
nodes.reverse_if: Account-phase tests show incumbents already enforce category, windows and A2P declaration correctly (then it is parity, not a gap). Or counsel finds a lighter rule set for AI service calls. Or buyer interviews rank these features irrelevant to switching.

nodes.title: Cold outbound sales (bought or scraped B2C lists, win-back) as VP's lead job.
nodes.tried: Evaluated cold promotional outbound against the primary texts as a candidate first job for the self-serve platform.
nodes.broke: It needs 140xx and a 10:00-21:00 window, and reaches only non-DND numbers (deemed consent). It carries the highest complaint exposure; sanctions bar or disconnect all of the sender's numbers at all operators. Its DPDP basis for bought lists of individuals ends ~2027-05-13 (no legitimate-interest ground). Every module it needs depends on operator scrubbing or CRF consent, which VP cannot control.

nodes.title: DPDP Rules G.S.R. 846(E), read in primary from eGazette (previously TLS-blocked). The Gazette is dated 2025-11-13, so Rule 4 (consent managers) applies from ~2026-11-13 and the core obligations (notice, security, rights, retention) from ~2027-05-13. Rule 6: one-year log retention and processor-contract safeguards. Rule 15: no general localisation. Rule 16 / s.17(2)(b): a research exemption.

Is a feedback/NPS call to one's own customer a service call, a commercial communication, or neither? Is a third-party market survey a commercial communication? TRAI's 2018 memo says surveys 'may not be directly falling under' the definition; Exotel treats both as UCC (9-21).
nodes.closes_when: A counsel opinion or a TRAI clarification classifies feedback and survey calls.

nodes.title: Could VP, as bring-your-own-carrier software placing calls on the tenant's CLIs, be read as a TCCCPR 'Sender' under def (bf)(iii) ('caused ... the voice call to be made')? Could it be an RBI 'recovery agency' or an IRDAI 'telemarketer' when it runs calls as a managed service?
nodes.closes_when: A counsel opinion on VP's role under TCCCPR def (bf), RBI para 6(11A) and IRDAI CA Regs def (q), for both the self-serve and the managed configuration.

nodes.title: From ~2026-11-18 every AI call on every number series must come from CLIs pre-declared as A2P to the originating operator and recorded on DLT; an undeclared call is UCC. No Indian vendor doc read covers this, and tenants onboarding in November may not know.
nodes.mitigation: The product collects and exports each tenant's A2P declaration pack (CLI ranges, purpose, volumes), blocks campaigns on undeclared CLIs, and confirms with Plivo/Vobiz/Exotel how they record declarations (account phase).

nodes.title:
Retell architecture (verified).
- Retell-operated hosts are US-West: sip.retellai.com AWS us-west-2 EC2, mcp.retellai.com an ELB in us-west-2, neither geo-routed; api.retellai.com is Global Accelerator anycast. Support (t/1949, 2026-03-25): 'Retell infrastructure is only in US(west) region.'
- Not every media edge is US-West: the legacy LiveKit Cloud project (retell-ai-4ihahnq7.livekit.cloud) resolves Indian client subnets to 143.223.94.x, the /24 LiveKit labels 'production-ohyderabad1a-main'.
- Browser media moved in Sept 2026 from LiveKit Cloud to a Retell-operated WHIP-style gateway (web SDK 3.0; create-web-call returns 'gateway' only). The gateway keeps LiveKit's room and identity-token model; its server software is unknown.
- The SIP allowlist has 3 LiveKit Inc. blocks (which include LiveKit's Mumbai and Hyderabad /24s) beside AWS us-west-2. Inference: some PSTN media lands on LiveKit addresses.
- Retell describes its own call-scheduling queues, containers and workers in two postmortems (vendor-claimed). Whether the runtime is built on LiveKit Agents, Pipecat or its own code is unknown.
- STT: Deepgram, Soniox, Azure, AssemblyAI and an unexplained 'Muse'. TTS: ElevenLabs, Cartesia, MiniMax, Fish, OpenAI, Inworld and 'Platform' (mostly re-listed MiniMax/Fish/Cartesia voices, per the account phase).

Retell all-in INR per connected minute for an Indian outbound call, computed from the rate card (not billed; ex GST, FX 95, 60 s call, Platform voice).
- BYO Indian SIP trunk, prompt up to 4k tokens: INR 8.3-13.6.
- Same with a 6k-token prompt: INR 8.7-20.0, depending on whether the 4,000-token rule scales only the LLM line or the whole duration.
- Retell-managed US number dialling India: INR 22-37 (Twilio USD 0.15, Telnyx USD 0.25 per min). This +1 path cannot carry BFSI service calls, which must come from 1600-series numbers.
The BYO band is 1.2-3.8x the lowest Indian list band (3.55-7), inside the 8-18 band other Indian vendors post, and 2.8-6.8x VP's INR 2-3 target; the infra line alone is INR 5.2/min. Caveats: the transcript counts toward the 4,000 tokens, so long-call rows are optimistic; whether an Indian trunk may terminate on a US SIP edge at domestic rates is unverified. The calculator-default margin is unknown (no price for its LLM in the cited inputs).
nodes.n: observed rate card x 3 telephony paths x 3 TTS x 3 LLM x 4 call lengths x 2 prompt sizes (324 rows; re-run byte-identical by the verifier)
nodes.method: Computed with pricing_allin.py from the public pricing page and docs read on 2026-10-20 (re-fetched 19:27Z, unchanged) and VP's Indian telephony input INR 0.43/min on 30-s pulses (2026-10-18 model inputs.csv). Not a billing measurement; RET-P11 tests the scaling rule.

nodes.title:
Retell does nothing India-specific for compliance (verified).
- 0 mentions of TRAI, DLT, NCPR, DPDP, DND or data residency across the 338 docs pages and the OpenAPI.
- Numbers are US/CA only (one docs page contradicts this), and caller-ID trust services are US-only; an Indian CLI needs a BYO SIP trunk.
- Calling windows default to America/Los_Angeles, with no TRAI window or warning.
- The internal DNC flag is off by default, honoured by single calls only with honor_internal_dnc=true, and NOT checked by batch calls.
- PII categories are US-centric (no Aadhaar or PAN).
- Active support runs 9 AM-9 PM Pacific: 21:30-09:30 IST until 2026-11-01, 22:30-10:30 IST after.
An Indian buyer carries all TRAI and DPDP work alone. Post-sale is not uniformly lighter: BFSI service calls must come from 1600-series numbers (ledger REG-10, REG-20), which Retell cannot supply.

Retell's Indic coverage is thin.
- Six Indian locales of 63: en-IN, hi-IN, kn-IN, mr-IN, ta-IN, ur-IN. No Telugu, Bengali, Gujarati, Malayalam, Punjabi, Odia or Sarvam; kn/mr/ta/ur ASR is Azure or Soniox only.
- Forum threads show Hindi digits mis-transcribed, with staff blaming the default Deepgram ASR (t/2713), and Indian multilingual drift back to English (t/2502, 330 views).
- Telugu and Bengali requests got 'try GPT Realtime' (t/1645); Sarvam requests are unanswered (t/2856, t/2866); some Indian browser users intermittently fail to join web calls (t/1949, where staff say the infrastructure is US-West only).

Retell's outbound surface and data model (verified).
- Batch calls take a CSV with any column as a dynamic variable, plus time windows and reserved concurrency. They have no per-call pacing, no documented retries and no DNC check. The API can only create a batch.
- A 'Campaigns' object exists server-side: the OpenAPI lists 'campaign' as a dashboard dataset, and the DNC doc refers to per-lead attempts and campaign DNC settings. It has no docs page and no endpoint; its retry and pacing fields are inferred from marketing.
- Strong diagnostics: 39 disconnection reasons, per-call cost line items, per-component latency, PCAP download, live listen and take-over.
- Hidden price multipliers: prompts over 4,000 tokens (including transcript and KB) scale billed duration; a 10-s minimum on a dynamic opener; burst +USD 0.10/min on the entire call. The marketing line 'No minimums' contradicts the 10-s rule.

Retell reliability and velocity, 2026-04-20 to 2026-10-20 (verified).
- Reliability: 12 status incidents (6 major). 2026-09-05: a custom-LLM race stalled the fleet; the degradation grew undetected for about 6 h (10:00-16:00 PST, no queue monitoring existed), and the first status post came 39 min after the 16:10 fleet-wide failure. 2026-09-16: a deploy double-assigned calls and failed about 22% of calls for 43 min; paged 7 min after errors rose, public post 35 min after.
- Velocity: 80 retell-sdk releases, 16 deprecation notices (2026-04 to 2026-12), 4 marketing changelog posts (none since 08-24), web SDK 3.0 on 09-08, spec revision 2026-10-19.
- Company: USD 80M ARR with 50 staff (vendor job posts).
nodes.n: 12 incidents in 6 months (50 most recent incidents returned by the status API, back to 2025-03-14); 80 npm versions; 16 deprecation notices
nodes.method: Read status.retellai.com/api/v2/incidents.json (capped at the 50 most recent), npm registry metadata, docs llms.txt and the changelog page on 2026-10-20; durations from incident timestamps and postmortem text, re-read by the verifier

nodes.title:
Retell v2 notes (verified).
- Contact memory is one rewritten brief of at most 2,000 characters per phone number, updated after phone or SMS conversations; saving is off by default for new agents and web calls don't save. Marketing's 'resume where the last call left off' describes that summary; it is not retrieval over history (consistent with ledger CMP-01's verifier note).
- Learning: Conductor turns failed calls into simulation tests and proposes fixes for human approval; AI QA cohorts cost USD 0.10/min; A/B uses fixed weights. No autonomous optimisation, bandit or significance test is documented.
REA inspect-web-network-capture on a full Playwright HAR with embedded response bodies.
nodes.tried: REA 6.7.0 inspect-web-network-capture on the full dashboard-login HAR with embedded response bodies (lane-reported 15.5 MB including a 6.9 MB PNG; the full HAR was not kept).
nodes.broke: Decoder failed with 'Capture decoder failed unexpectedly (RangeError)'. The same HAR with bodies and cookies stripped (120 KB) decoded cleanly. Workaround: slim every HAR before giving it to REA. REA analyze-web-bundle over a local CDP Chromium worked on the pricing page (40 scripts, 0 parse failures).

nodes.closes_when: Predictions RET-P01 to RET-P12 in predictions.json are scored, using each prediction's verifier_check scoring fix, against a run on our own Retell trial workspace (Instinct reported it ready, USD 10 credit, TOTP on every login), with stereo handset recordings, PCAPs and a time-and-motion log.

nodes.title: Retell's legacy LiveKit Cloud web host is geo-routed and has an Indian edge; Retell's own hosts are not. Client-subnet DNS (22 lookups, 19:25Z): retell-ai-4ihahnq7.livekit.cloud gives Indian subnets 143.223.94.99/.107 (RDAP label 'production-ohyderabad1a-main'), a us-west-2 subnet San Jose, 8.8.8.0/24 Phoenix, the sandbox Ashburn; sip, api and mcp.retellai.com give every subnet the same records. The SIP allowlist's LiveKit blocks also hold LiveKit's Mumbai and Hyderabad /24s. So 'US-West only, no other PoP' holds at most for Retell-operated compute; whether Indian PSTN media on a BYO trunk lands on an Indian LiveKit edge is open (a PCAP shows it).

Inference: Retell has no compliant path for BFSI post-sale calls in India. Service and transactional calls by RBI/SEBI/IRDAI/PFRDA entities must come from 1600-series numbers irrespective of consent (ledger REG-10, REG-20). Retell numbers are US/CA only, so its +1-to-India route (INR 22-37/min) is out for an insurer's or intermediary's renewal call; a BYO trunk must carry a 1600 number, which takes about 7-14 business days to provision, has no published price, and no CPaaS states it may stream media to a third-party AI gateway (REG-23 to REG-25), let alone a US-hosted one. For VP's insurance-renewal beachhead, post-sale on Retell is different plumbing, not lighter plumbing.

Retell has a platform AI-disclosure control: the Agent Handbook preset 'AI Disclosure When Asked' (HandbookConfig.ai_disclosure, ~30 tokens), documented as on by default for new agents; agents built through Retell's Claude connector also open with 'Hi, this is an AI assistant.' The account phase found an API-created agent with no handbook_config at all, so the default depends on the creation path. Two pre-registered predictions (RET-P03, RET-P12) rested on 'no disclosure control documented' and now carry corrected scoring.

Adversarial verification of the retell lane: 41 of the lane's 60 claims re-checked against their evidence (manifest 471/471 hashes match; DNS re-run with 4 client subnets; rate card re-fetched; pricing_allin.py re-run byte-identical; OpenAPI enums, SDK source, HAR, status API and 8 threads re-read). 23 confirmed, 14 corrected, 4 downgraded (RET-22, RET-24, RET-33, RET-36), 0 whole claims refuted (5 sub-statements refuted and fixed in place: the 'US-West only' hosting summary, 'post-sale needs less' for BFSI, 'INR 3 needs Indian hosting', and the 'no disclosure control' basis of RET-P03 and RET-P12), 7 added (RET-22b, RET-36b, RET-47b, RET-61 to RET-64). Biggest changes: Retell's legacy WebRTC edge has an Indian PoP; BFSI post-sale needs 1600 numbers Retell cannot supply; the calculator-default margin and the 'not LiveKit Agents' claim are unknown; AI disclosure is a platform preset. 7 of 12 predictions are only partly falsifiable as registered and all 12 carry scoring notes; RET-P01's sign-up clause was known before registration. Record: per-claim verification fields in claims.json, verifier_check in predictions.json, raw re-checks under data/teardown/retell/verify/ (report.md and verify.md were refused by the harness).

Teardown lane sarvam (account-free), after adversarial verification: 66 graded claims (45 observed, 13 inferred, 4 vendor-claimed, 4 unknown) and 14 pre-registered account-phase predictions. The verifier re-checked 52 of the 62 original claims: 30 confirmed, 16 corrected, 3 downgraded, 2 refuted (SAR-07, SAR-31), 1 regraded, 1 split out (SAR-39b), and added 3 (SAR-63-65). Sources: 162 Voice Agents docs pages plus the OpenAPI (68 ops, 175 schemas), changelog and status feeds, HARs of the product and login pages (53 dashboard chunks, 700-event analytics catalogue), npm and PyPI SDKs read without installing, DNS/RDAP/cloud IP ranges, and the round-2 widget WebSocket dumps. The lane's report.md was never written to disk; the verifier created it with a findings index and the Verification section.

Sarvam architecture, observed. The Voice Agents runtime and REST APIs (apps.sarvam.ai) are in Azure Central India (4.213.0.0/16). api.sarvam.ai, the Model APIs and the dashboard's production API base, sits on an AWS ap-south-1 ELB named k8s-vistaar-, and the Mixpanel proxy on another (k8s-saasprodplatforma-); the dashboard frontend is on Azure Front Door. The web path is one JSON/base64 WebSocket (chunks labelled audio/wav are headerless 16 kHz PCM, about 100 ms each) with no WebRTC, so not a LiveKit or Daily room; whether the server side uses a framework such as Pipecat is unknown. BYO telephony from 7 providers; rented numbers on Vobiz.

Inference (computed from the observed rate card, not from billing): Sarvam effective all-in price per connected minute, ex GST, on Sarvam telephony. PAYG 30-s call INR 7.40, 45-s 5.20, 60-s 3.90, 90-s 5.07; Growth 90-s 4.60. Calls of 30-90 s that are not whole minutes cost INR 4.40-7.40 across plans; whole-minute calls 3.40-3.90. The 2026-10-17 'INR 3.55-3.90 all-in' holds only for whole minutes. Actual debits are scored by SAR-P13.

nodes.title: Sarvam leaves India plumbing to the buyer. Rented numbers are 10-digit 11/79/80 series only (KYC as Individual or Corporate). Across 162 docs pages there is no 140/1601, A2P, DLT, NCPR or DPDP handling; TRAI appears once, only as an example failure reason where a BYO provider (Exotel) rejects an NDNC number. Caller-ID rotation is pitched to stop contacts "learning to ignore one number"; calling windows are free-form; there is no AI-disclosure control, and the demo agent claimed to be human 6/6. Inference: its EMI-reminder showcase needs a BYO 1600 trunk to be lawful for a regulated lender, and its Cart Abandonment vertical, which auto-rents a 10-digit number, would need 140xx if cart recovery is promotional.

Sarvam's 700-event product-analytics catalogue (583 active) is public in its login-page bundle. Each event names an owner team (platform 202, samvaad 158, studio 147, devplatform 108, akshar 53, cart-abandonment 32), and 77 carry an activation role (aha 35, setup 34, habit 8). It shows its activation definition (agent created and deployed, tool, KB, inbound and campaign created; MCP bound), the Cart Abandonment vertical (Shopify + Razorpay + an auto-rented number after KYC), Razorpay UPI autopay billing, and an org model-training consent toggle. A reference for VP's own activation metrics.

Sarvam already sells the post-sale collections and EMI-reminder job VP is weighing: its showcase EMI agent carries a full collections disposition model and its testimonial is Tata Capital's CDO. It also sells pre-sale jobs (cart recovery, which is its one productised vertical, lead qualification, pre-approved loans). At INR 3-3.5/min list with India-hosted Hindi-first models, post-sale-first is contested in collections specifically.
nodes.mitigation: Compete where Sarvam is absent, not on list price or language: regulated BFSI service calls that are 1600/A2P-ready and compliant by construction, enforced AI disclosure, a handset reply gap of 1.5 s or less, better turn-taking, and fair short-call billing (its 60-s pulses make 30-90 s calls cost INR 4.4-7.4/min). Prove each with the account-phase battery before claiming it.

nodes.title: Proposed: against Sarvam, VP claims only these measurable edges: (1) AI disclosure enforced in code; (2) handset reply gap on Indian PSTN of 1.5 s p50 or less (its demo 3.1 s browser-side; its public model APIs reach about 1.0-1.2 s server-side in our pipeline); (3) turn-taking under elderly pauses and babble; (4) regulated-call plumbing (1600/A2P routing, category windows, opt-out from the CSV); (5) fair short-call billing. Not claimed: list price, Hindi/Tamil language hold, or having a copilot (Genie exists).
nodes.rationale: SAR-34/35/38/44-49/53/54 in the lane claims, as corrected by verification. Sarvam leads on list price (not on effective price for short calls, SAR-38) and holds language; Genie already covers chat-driven build, deploy and diagnosis.
nodes.reverse_if: The account phase shows configured Sarvam agents disclosing AI by default and a handset p50 of 1.5 s or less on PSTN, or Sarvam ships 1600/A2P routing and a disclosure guardrail.

nodes.title: REA analyze-web-bundle through our loopback CDP Chromium on indus.sarvam.ai
nodes.tried: rea-agents 6.7.0 analyze-web-bundle --fetch-source-maps against a headless Chromium on CDP port 9333, loading the public login page (no login).
nodes.broke: In that CDP-attached browser, REA saw 5 scripts, including Cloudflare's challenge-platform precursor, and 0 endpoints, so the page stayed on Cloudflare's challenge (the 'Attention Required' title is not in the saved REA JSON). A Playwright-launched Chromium got the same precursor script but passed and loaded the real app (53 Next.js chunks). We did not bypass it; the analysis came from the Playwright HAR plus static grep. inspect-web-network-capture only decodes HARs, and analyze-javascript-application is Electron-oriented (zero counts on the npm SDK).

nodes.title: Sarvam account phase: score the 14 pre-registered predictions (SAR-P01-P14; P02 split into P02a/b and P13 scored in credits, per verifier notes). Sign-up and KYC path; Genie agent quality and disclosure; messy-CSV dedupe and opt-out; out-of-hours window; voicemail on Indian operator announcements; warm vs blind transfer on BYO Plivo; failed-call reason; export columns; handset reply gap (predicted p50 1.6-2.4 s); invoice pulse rounding; and whether logged-in dashboard sessions are recorded to PostHog US with network bodies (SAR-63/64).
nodes.closes_when: A trial account on team email runs the fixed task list twice and the PSTN battery (n of at least 30 clean turns) on our Plivo number, each prediction is scored hit or miss in predictions.json, and one logged-in HAR shows whether replay uploads to k.sarvam.ai/s/ occur on transcript and contact pages.

nodes.title: Sarvam's dashboard records sessions to PostHog's US cloud (observed config; the residency implication is inference). The bundle initialises PostHog with api_host k.sarvam.ai, ui_host us.posthog.com, session recording on and maskAllInputs off; the remote config served on the public login page enables replay for all sessions over 30 s with network body and header capture. k.sarvam.ai CNAMEs to a PostHog cf-prod-us proxy. Inference: logged-in views of transcripts and contacts would leave India unless masked, against the docs' "all data, including any PII, stays within India". Not yet seen after login.

Teardown lane squadstack (account-free), after adversarial verification: 76 graded claims (50 observed, 14 inferred, 12 vendor-claimed, 0 unknown; 69 from the lane, 7 added by the verifier) and 14 pre-registered predictions. Sources: about 53 marketing, legal and blog documents plus llms.txt and the sitemap; the portal Next.js build manifest and 98 chunks; the AI-platform auth page HAR, its agent-editor page chunk and the app.osno.ai build; the in-app SDK; the Vanta trust centre; the Postman API collection; careers; Play Store and Capterra; DNS and AWS IP ranges; the GitHub org. The verifier re-checked 36 claims: 19 confirmed, 9 corrected in wording, 5 refuted in part, 2 downgraded to inferred, 1 upgraded from unknown. report.md (filled from the lane's structured output) now ends with a Verification section. verify.md was not written; verification.json is the verification log.

SquadStack architecture, from its own public code and trust centre. Observed: an in-app SDK on @pipecat-ai/client-js 1.13.1 + Daily transport (POST /bot/connect), so a Pipecat-style server is inferred. TTS: ElevenLabs is the customer-visible provider, default model constant eleven_flash_v2_5, with Multilingual v2 hidden as legacy and calls on the India-residency endpoint; Cartesia (Sonic 3.5/3.6) and Sarvam are internal-only. STT: an arc_stt router with fallback / best-latency / load-balance strategies. In-call LLM providers named in the editor: OpenAI, SimpliSmart, AWS Bedrock, OpenRouter. Post-call extraction and RAG default to Gemini 2.5 Flash via OpenRouter. Subprocessors: Exotel and Ozonetel (telephony, India), Plivo (USA, "Human-like Voice AI Agents"), OpenAI (USA), Google Gemini. Origins are AWS ap-south-1; a Django backend is inferred. Contradicts "owned, not orchestrated": ownership is plausible only for ASR (Arth) and perhaps an LLM hosted on SimpliSmart or Bedrock.

SquadStack, the managed incumbent with 60+ enterprise logos, has a builder ready for self-serve but has not opened it. ai-platform.squadstack.ai ("Build, deploy, and optimize personalized AI voice agents in minutes") and its second brand Osno AI (app.osno.ai, same Firebase project and code) both ship ENABLE_EMAIL_DOMAIN_RESTRICTION=true. Only squadstack.ai/.com or allowlisted emails get in ("Sign in is temporarily disabled for external users"); Osno adds per-user access with an expiry. The parts needed to open it already exist: onboarding, credits, test call, inbound-number generation. Three Voice AI platform PM roles specify self-serve onboarding, APIs and SDKs. The portal's Plug-N-Play wallet flow sells human tele-callers, not AI agents. The risk is a flag flip, not a build.
nodes.mitigation: Win on what a self-serve rookie with a BPO data model lacks: minutes to first live call, a per-call technical failure reason, real-time AMD, compliance by construction (1600/140 routing, consent, a 10:00-21:00 promotional window, fixed AI disclosure) and published pricing. The change-watch should re-fetch the ai-platform and app.osno.ai auth chunks monthly and alert when ENABLE_EMAIL_DOMAIN_RESTRICTION flips or the allowlist disappears.

nodes.title: SquadStack's public API is a 2024 Postman collection for lead ingestion only. It has per-campaign create/update/upsert/convert/disable/delete endpoints (bulk 100), basic auth, 100 requests/min and mandatory IP whitelisting; SquadStack creates the campaign. Data flows out as per-customer disposition webhooks (call event plus an end-of-journey 'judgement'). No developer docs, changelog or status page exist (docs.squadstack.com 301-redirects to the Postman collection). The 61-route portal and the AI-platform agent object (temperature 0.5, max_tokens 100, max session 240 s, idle 10 s x 3, summarisation after 5 turns) give VP a parity reference.

Inference: SquadStack COGS per connected minute, ex GST, over its observed provider options. With ElevenLabs Flash v2.5 at PAYG (the likely customer default) it is INR 1.95-3.6: a loss at INR 2, a 23-34% mid margin at 3.5. With legacy Multilingual v2 (hidden in the editor) it is INR 3.3-5.3; Cartesia Sonic-3.6, INR 1.9-3.5; Sarvam Bulbul, INR 1.2-2.7; self-hosted TTS, INR 0.7-2.1. Corrected by the verifier: the lane called Multilingual v2 "the bundle default", but the bundle hides it.
nodes.n: 15 stack combinations (3 STT x 1 LLM proxy x 5 TTS) x lo/mid/hi
nodes.method: desk computation: g4 component list prices (2026-10-18) and model/results/inputs.csv (telephony INR 0.38-0.48, infra) applied to providers observed in SquadStack's public bundles and trust centre. The in-call LLM is a Gemini flash-lite proxy, but the editor names OpenAI, SimpliSmart, AWS Bedrock and OpenRouter, so the LLM line is unverified. Not measured on SquadStack traffic; arithmetic re-run by the verifier, all 15 rows reproduce.

nodes.title: SquadStack India plumbing. Observed: a DNC blacklist marked "verified DND by scrubbing" (10-digit paste field), an in-call dnd_request() closing tool, and SMS blocks that take the customer's Sender ID and DLT Entity ID. Zero mentions of 140, 160 or 1600-series numbers across about 53 documents, the portal UI and the agent editor; the marketing sells "spam number rotation". The only calling window in code is a UI notice that calling pauses 23:00-09:00 daily. That allows 21:00-23:00 and 09:00-10:00, against the marketed "hard-enforced 9:30-20:30" and the 10:00-21:00 default promotional band. The Terms make the buyer warrant consent to record and to train on voice data, and disclaim regulatory fitness. The privacy policy is the legacy gig-worker notice with no DPDP notice for the people called. OpenAI and Plivo are US subprocessors despite "all data within India". "Configurable AI disclosure" is claimed; no disclosure setting was found in code.

Inference: SquadStack's headline numbers do not reconcile. Arth's '1 crore minutes in two months at 80% of traffic' implies on average about 2 lakh AI minutes a day, or INR 15-38 Cr a year at INR 2-5, the same order as FY24 revenue of INR 26.5 Cr. A ramp could make today's rate higher. Even so, '50 lakh+ calls a day' is about 0.04 min per call, and under 0.2 min at 5x, so 'calls' means dial attempts. Other contradictions: training data of 600M vs 900M minutes vs 3B interactions; 20+ vs 1,000+ voices; a setup fee per use case vs '$0'; and the 'Turing test', dated September, October or November 2025 and scored as 'picked at least one of two AI recordings as human'.

Proposed: against SquadStack, VP competes on five tasks we can run, not on logos or ASR. (1) Minutes to first live call: SquadStack is sales-led and its builders are allowlisted. (2) A per-call technical failure reason customers can see beyond 10 days: SquadStack shows outcome labels plus aggregate STT/LLM/TTS counts; per-call traces live in its internal Lens. (3) Real-time voicemail/AMD: SquadStack classifies voicemail post-call from transcript keywords. (4) Compliance and honesty by construction: 1600/140 routing, consent capture, a 10:00-21:00 promotional window and a fixed AI disclosure. SquadStack has number rotation, buyer-warranted consent, a 23:00-09:00 pause and configurable disclosure, but it does have in-call DND capture. (5) Published pricing with no setup fee. Head-on pre-sale BFSI, where SquadStack holds logos and outcome pricing, stays out of v1.
nodes.rationale: Observed SquadStack surface (claims SQS-11, SQS-18, SQS-34, SQS-37, SQS-47..SQS-50, SQS-70..SQS-72, after verification) and its BPO-shaped data model; buyer complaints elsewhere are ~70% support, billing and account UI (l4a/r2). Transfer was dropped as a differentiator because the editor has a transfer_call() tool.
nodes.reverse_if: The account phase or buyer interviews show any of: SquadStack/Osno self-serve sign-up to first PSTN call in under 30 min; per-call technical failure reasons shown to customers; real-time AMD; or 1600-series routing with fixed disclosure. Also reverse if the listener panel or a pilot shows that VP's fixed AI disclosure raises hang-ups by more than 5 points over undisclosed agents.

nodes.title: SquadStack teaches Indian enterprise buyers that winning means being mistaken for a human. Its naturalness KPI counts calls dropped after the caller realises it is an AI; it markets a 'Turing test' and 'configurable AI disclosure'. Buyers may score VP's never-deny, disclose-once rule as a naturalness loss in bake-offs.
nodes.mitigation: Measure the effect of one-time light disclosure on hang-ups within 10 s and on task success, in the listener panel and the first pilot. Sell the rule as regulatory and brand safety (DPDP, TRAI, RBI/IRDAI conduct). Never relax the rule; it is a standing owner rule.

nodes.title: REA on SquadStack: the HAR path failed, and the CDP bundle path finished late with no usable evidence.
nodes.tried: npx rea-agents@latest inspect on a Playwright 1.56 HAR (content embedded) of ai-platform.squadstack.ai; analyze-web-bundle over CDP (headless Chromium 141, port 9334) with --fetch-source-maps and 6 s of observation.
nodes.broke: inspect: "Cannot open artifact: unsupported binary format" (target_unavailable) on a Playwright 1.56 HAR. analyze-web-bundle: it overran the 280 s timeout, but the orphaned child still wrote a complete result about 308 s after start (34 scripts parsed, 502k AST nodes). The result held only Next.js/React fingerprints, 1 route (/_next/image) and 1 endpoint (/__cookies__), and source maps were "not_requested" despite --fetch-source-maps. It found none of the provider, auth-gate or window strings that plain grep over the same chunks found. rea doctor reports healthy:false (analysis engines missing). The fallback that worked: the Next.js _buildManifest and route-shell chunk lists, direct download of public chunks, and string extraction. The lane first recorded the CDP run as "no output"; the verifier corrected that from rea-ai-platform-web-bundle.json.

nodes.title: SquadStack account phase: how can VP get a time-and-motion run at all? Contract terms are not the blocker, because the owner overrode vendor terms (directive.2026-10-20.terms-override). The blocker is access. Both ai-platform.squadstack.ai and app.osno.ai allowlist sign-in to squadstack.ai/.com and named emails, and Osno adds per-user expiry (SQS-70). A team@vyakti.ai sign-up would stop at "Sign in is temporarily disabled for external users". Getting past the gate other than by SquadStack provisioning access is an authentication bypass, a kept line in decision.2026-10-20.teardown-lines. The routes are: SquadStack grants access under VP's real identity (a sales/demo request, which needs the owner's go because it contacts the vendor), or buyer interviews.
nodes.closes_when: SquadStack provisions an account for VP's real identity (then run the 14 predictions in predictions.json, re-scoped per verification.json). Or 3 or more buyer interviews (e.g. IndiaMART, BankBazaar, Moneyview, Upstox, Shiprocket) supply onboarding time, failure-reason visibility, number series, calling-window control, AMD/transfer behaviour and a written price. Or the monthly change-watch sees ENABLE_EMAIL_DOMAIN_RESTRICTION turned off.

nodes.title: SquadStack v2 reference. Marketed: Persistent Memory (lead-level, masked fingerprint, up to 20 plain-language extraction points, Refresh or Rolling History, pass-through or AI-summarised briefing, stale facts flagged), Lift (one prompt edit at a time, human-reviewed, locked compliance/pricing/identity sections, rollout from a small slice to 1/4, 1/2 and all traffic) and Optimize (80/20 splits, significance flag). Observed in code: intra-call memory only. That is state management with multi-stage prompts, per-stage summaries and memory_keys, plus "In-Call Memory" summarisation (5-turn threshold, keeps 3, gpt-4o-mini by default). Also observed: model hot-swap and fallback, agent evals and prompt-version history. No cross-call memory, Lift or Optimize screen is in the captured bundles.

SquadStack's public failure record is supply-side, not buyer-side. Capterra has 0 reviews; G2, Trustpilot and SourceForge are behind 403 (not bypassed). The partner app (com.squad.run; 15,007 ratings, 3.85 stars) shows payouts stuck for months, no work for 6 months after passing assessments, deactivations with money held, a stated hiring pause and templated replies (Jun-Jul 2026). Its managed 'human advisors' fallback sits on a shrinking gig pool (FY24 revenue halved).

Adversarial verification of the squadstack lane: 36 claims re-checked against the cited files and fresh public captures (the app.osno.ai build, the AI-platform agent-editor chunk, redirect headers, the GitHub org). 19 confirmed, 9 corrected in wording, 5 refuted in part, 2 downgraded to inferred, 1 upgraded, 7 claims added. The refutations are: the ElevenLabs default (Multilingual v2 is hidden legacy; Flash v2.5 is the default constant); the STT provider list (it is an internal-only filter; arc_stt is a router); a 9:30-20:30 window (code shows a 23:00-09:00 pause); "no transfer" (a transfer_call() tool exists); and "REA produced no output" (it produced a late, near-empty result). The biggest addition is that both AI-platform builds allowlist sign-in. Three of 14 predictions rest on corrected premises (P03, P05, P07), P02 is now near-certain, and P12 and P13 carry little information.

Teardown synthesis, account-free phase (wf_560edf6c-5d6): 8 deep vendors + regulation + radar consolidated into a method calibration, a pre/post-sale recommendation, a Kano parity floor over 46 features, 10 where-we-win hypotheses with kill bars, architecture and economics tables, a 125-prediction registry and an account-phase test plan. 25 synthesis claims (16 observed, 8 inferred, 1 unknown) over 662 lane claims (478 observed, 105 inferred, 64 vendor-claimed, 15 unknown). SYNTHESIS.md and predictions.md were returned as text (subagent rule against report files) for the main loop to save under research/2026-10-20/teardown/.

Teardown method calibration: Bolna blind inferences scored against its code hit 0.90 lenient / 0.75 strict (0 wrong; Brier 0.089 / 0.066; second rater 0.85, kappa 0.74). Docs-led inferences 0.96 / 0.79, bundle-led 0.70 / 0.60, bundle-flag mechanisms 1 of 4 fully right; 16 material features were never inferred. Across the 7 closed-vendor lanes, adversarial verifiers kept 89% of 309 re-checked claims in substance and 57% verbatim.
nodes.n: 20 pre-registered checkable Bolna inferences (18 contamination-free); 309 re-checked claims across Sarvam, Vapi, Retell, ElevenLabs, Synthflow, SquadStack and Exotel
nodes.method: Pre-registered (TRUE + 0.5 PARTLY)/n and Brier against bolna-ai/bolna @bc59921, lenient and strict rules, two raters; verifier tallies read from each lane verify file or claims.json verification blocks, 2026-10-20

nodes.title: Proposed: weight inferred claims on closed vendors by evidence class. Keep at face value (about 0.9): hosting and region from DNS plus cloud IP ranges, transport from our own captures, structure and bounded negatives from docs. Discount to about 0.75: mechanisms read from docs. Discount to about 0.5: mechanisms read from bundle constants or flags (dead code and hide-lists were misread as defaults). Treat as unknown: server-side framework identity from client artefacts, margins built on analogue COGS, media anchoring from signalling DNS, and every timing constant. For thin-doc vendors (SquadStack, Exotel) discount one class further. Absence of an inference is not evidence of absence (recall gap of 16 features on Bolna).
nodes.rationale: Bolna calibration by evidence type and claim kind (TS-01..TS-03) and the cluster of verifier downgrades across the closed-vendor lanes (TS-05) point to the same weak classes.
nodes.reverse_if: A second open-source calibration target (for example a Pipecat- or LiveKit-based platform) or the account phase contradicts more than 20% of claims in a class this rule keeps at face value, or confirms more than 80% of a class it treats as unknown.

nodes.title: All 8 deep-set vendors leave Indian calling compliance to the buyer: 0/8 ship category-aware calling windows, a consent or inquiry ledger, an A2P CLI-range declaration or an in-call promotion fence; only Sarvam (org DND list) and SquadStack (DNC blacklist plus in-call dnd_request) suppress on every outbound path; Bolna and Exotel publish 9-21 as the TRAI window for all calls. Bounded negatives over each vendor's saved docs, confirmed at API level for 5 vendors.

Proposed (decision 1): post-sale first on one shared post-sale core. Lead jobs: (1) due-date reminders (renewal, pre-due payment/EMI, service appointments); (2) onboarding and application follow-up. Second wave: consented inbound-lead follow-up inside the 7-day inquiry window. Not in v1: cold outbound, surveys, collections in default (phase 2, RBI trigger 2027-01-01). Feedback/NPS is a fast-follow once counsel classifies it. Insurance renewal (beachhead-v2) becomes the first vertical preset and design-partner set, beside lending pre-due and subscriptions/utilities presets, not the product boundary.
nodes.rationale: Service calls need no explicit consent, are not DND-blocked, have no TRAI band and fit DPDP s.7(a), while pre-sale depends on CRF consent upload that only 11 pilot banks have; every incumbent leaves compliance to the buyer. Counterweights recorded: promotional volume is about 11x 1600 volume, compliance is 1.3% of complaints, and funded BFSI post-sale specialists exist.
nodes.reverse_if: Any of: 10-15 buyer interviews show the main self-serve job is inbound-lead follow-up (move it into v1 with the consent ledger); TRAI opens CRF upload to all senders or DPDP consent managers ship APIs; counsel rules non-BFSI service calls may not use declared 10-digit numbers (then BFSI-only post-sale); TRAI adds an AI-specific consent rule or series for service calls; the A2P charge rises toward INR 0.50/min; counsel holds intermediary renewal reminders are solicitation (drop the insurance preset only); measured pickup on 1600 or declared CLIs is too low for reminders; or the account phase shows a post-sale specialist already passes W1, W2 and W6 by default.

nodes.title: Proposed (decision 2): v1 parity floor as a Kano draft over 46 features x 8 vendors (kano.csv). Must-be: 21 items plus AI disclosure as a VP rule, including 10 present at all 8 vendors (test call, list campaigns, inbound, transfer, voicemail detection, KB, HTTP tools, typed post-call extraction, webhook, versions) and the India-specific items where coverage is thin (suppression on every path 2/8, recurring window 2/8, Indian CLI path 4/8, INR+GST billing 3/8, India residency 2/8). Performance: reply gap, language hold, price and pulse, tests, copilot builder (parity, not a wedge), MCP/API, live listen, A/B, analytics, WhatsApp, CRM, typed cost, actionable failure reasons, CSV hygiene. Delighters (0-2 of 8): category-aware windows, promotion fence, A2P export, series provisioning, consent ledger, memory, automatic improvement, carrier failover, customer-owned outcomes, full API parity. AI disclosure is a VP rule regardless of buyer class.
nodes.rationale: Coverage counts come from graded lane claims and the API-key phase; Kano classes are our proposal until buyers rank them.
nodes.reverse_if: Buyer interviews classify an item differently (for example WhatsApp follow-up as must-be, as the radar proposes), or the account phase shows documented features behave differently from the docs on 2 or more vendors.

nodes.title: Proposed (decision 3): 10 where-we-win hypotheses, each tied to a fixed task or battery item with a pass bar and a kill bar: W1 compliance by default (N2 opt-out number never rings); W2 CSV hygiene and campaign robustness; W3 Indian-PSTN reply gap; W4 Hinglish short-reply turn-taking; W5 language hold against non-Indian platforms only; W6 failure explainability; W7 minutes to the first Indian-CLI ring; W8 fair billing; W9 support in IST hours; W10 stored config equals what runs, with every dashboard action on API/MCP. None is proven; W3 and W4 are unproven for VP itself.
nodes.rationale: Each hypothesis traces to incumbent docs gaps and raw complaints (support 114, billing 107, account/UI 99 of 459 coded Indian complaints), and each task can be scored identically on VP and the incumbents.
nodes.reverse_if: A hypothesis hits its kill bar in the account phase (listed per hypothesis in where-we-win.json), or buyer interviews rank it outside their top switching reasons.

nodes.title: All-in INR per connected Indian minute, computed from published rate cards (not invoices): Sarvam 3.4-3.9 whole-minute, 4.4-7.4 on 30-90 s calls; SquadStack 2-5 (vendor statement); Bolna 4.2-8.0; ElevenLabs 8.2-8.9 (Exotel/Plivo); Retell 8.3-13.6 on a BYO trunk, 22-37 on its US numbers; Vapi 12.5-17.0; Synthflow 15.2-25.6 plus a USD 30k/yr floor; Exotel quote-gated. Incumbents with reconstructable costs keep 44-72%+ margins, so price alone is not a wedge.
nodes.n: 8 deep-set vendor rate cards read 2026-10-20 (7 priced), plus the radar Caller.digital itemised stack
nodes.method: Lane computations at FX 95, ex GST, per call-length scenario, with pulse rounding; COGS from 2026-10-18 component list prices; no billed call

nodes.title: Proposed: run the dashboard and call-battery account phase on Bolna, Sarvam (Voice Agents workspace), ElevenLabs, Retell, Vapi (with a Twilio leg for PSTN), Exotel (after company KYC) and Gupshup Voice AI in Synthflow's place. Synthflow and SquadStack stay desk-deep and are covered by buyer interviews unless the owner approves a sales conversation; SquadStack sign-in is allowlisted in code, a hard stop under the no-auth-bypass line.
nodes.rationale: Synthflow sells only enterprise contracts from USD 30k/yr behind a review gate; SquadStack restricts sign-in to its own domains; Gupshup is self-serve with 100 free minutes and Indian numbers.
nodes.reverse_if: Synthflow grants a self-serve workspace, SquadStack provisions an evaluation account under VP's real identity, or Gupshup's trial turns out not to be self-serve.

nodes.title: Run the account-phase plan: per vendor, tasks T0-T9 twice (sign-up to first ring, build the standard agent, messy 50-row CSV, calling-window battery, voicemail and transfer, five induced failures, export, invoice audit, IST support ticket, promotion fence and opt-out carry-over), the l4b caller battery answered on our Plivo number (4 personas x 2 calls, >=30 clean turns, stereo), and a default-template disclosure test; score the 125 registered predictions and the 10 where-we-win kill bars. Needs owner decisions: spend caps, a Plivo recharge above the INR 80 monthly cap, two more owned numbers (Delhi 11-series preferred), a Twilio leg for Vapi, Exotel KYC documents, a named person for Retell Persona KYC, Sarvam credits and workspace key.
nodes.closes_when: At least 6 vendors have scored task sheets and >=30 clean battery turns each, every registered prediction is scored hit, miss or not-testable with a reason, and each where-we-win hypothesis is marked passed or killed.

nodes.title: A synthetic test list can ring real strangers: Vapi's dashboard turns a 10-digit Indian number into +98... and Retell's import into +1..., so any 10-digit test row whose mis-normalised form is a live number abroad would be dialled. A 10-digit form of a Bengaluru (80-series) number maps to a plausible US number under the +1 default.
nodes.mitigation: Render every test CSV with messy_csv.py, which expands each phone cell under every known normaliser and fails closed unless each candidate is ours, reserved fictional, or unassignable; use Delhi 11-series numbers so the full list passes (11XXXXXXXX lands in NANP area code 1XX); otherwise withhold the flagged rows and score those behaviours from code, as already observed.

nodes.title: Messy 50-row synthetic CSV kit: template with BOM, CRLF, messy headers, cross-format and cross-script duplicates, an opt-out number that must never ring, two-number cells, impossible dates, mixed amounts, broken rows and unroutable junk; a per-row spec of the expected VP behaviour; and a fail-closed renderer that reads our numbers from a mode-600 env file and refuses any row a vendor normaliser could turn into a stranger's number.
nodes.value: One identical, safe input for task T2 on every vendor and for VP's own import tests; doubles as the v1 import test fixture.
nodes.effort: Built and dry-run on fictional numbers on 2026-10-20; needs the real owned numbers in the env file at run time.

nodes.title: Prediction registry for the account phase: 125 pre-registered predictions from 10 lanes, numbered TP-001..TP-125 with verbatim text, confidence, scoring rule and the status known on 2026-10-20 (1 hit, 6 partly supported by API reads, 9 with weakened or contradicted premises, 2 not scoreable as written, 105 open).

Synthflow public teardown (account-free), adversarially verified: 59 graded claims after verification (46 observed, 9 inferred, 2 vendor-claimed, 2 unknown). Of the lane's 55, 30 were confirmed, 18 corrected, 2 downgraded (SYN-22 observed to inferred, SYN-53 inferred to unknown) and 5 not re-checked; the verifier split out SYN-21b and SYN-31b and added SYN-37 and SYN-66. Sources: 370 docs pages as Markdown, the OpenAPI spec (69 paths, 110 operations), passive Playwright captures of the site, the React app and the Bubble login, app and widget JS bundles, a public feature-flag snapshot, IP-to-region mapping, DNS, job posts, GitHub, the status feed, Trustpilot (via WebFetch) and the feedback board. The sha256 manifest covers 486 lane files plus the verifier's re-checks. report.md and verify.md were created by the verifier.

Synthflow has gone sales-led. Only Enterprise is priced (from $30k/yr), the old Pro/Growth/Agency plans are 'no longer sold', and new accounts 'may be reviewed' before access. Campaigns, SIP/custom numbers, Aurora, GPT models (so BYOK), SSO, the fallback voice and scheduled exports are Enterprise-only. Non-enterprise agents were forced onto 'Synthflow LLM' on 2026-08-25, and a GPT value sent through the API is silently ignored. Inference: self-serve looks closed to new buyers; whether a new sign-up can still buy a non-enterprise plan is unknown (SYN-P01). The 'no-code UX reference' now behaves like a sales-led enterprise CX vendor.

Synthflow has no India footprint. 69 of the 70 SIP, media and egress IPs map to GCP us-east1, europe-west3 or northamerica-south1 (the 70th is Microsoft's); clusters are Global/US/EU only; numbers can be bought only in the US, Canada and Australia; SIP is Enterprise-only; no Indian carrier is among its telephony providers; and the 370 docs pages never mention TRAI, DLT, NCPR/DND, the 140/160 series or DPDP. Inference: an Indian enterprise cannot present a compliant Indian CLI out of the box. The non-native routes are a Synthflow PoP in India (offered on request, vendor-claimed) or a buyer-built bridge from an Indian CPaaS media stream (e.g. Exotel AgentStream) into Synthflow's WebSocket media API; whether either is lawful for 140/1600-series calling is not established.

Synthflow stack from public material (observed unless marked). Telephony: SIP on ports 32681/32682; a VoIP job post asks for Kamailio, RTPEngine and FreeSWITCH, and the GitHub org has FreeSWITCH and VoiceBlender forks (own SBCs inferred). Browser calls and live listen-in go through a Janus gateway (janode, AudioBridge, TURN relay forced); custom web integration uses WebSocket media (RTP or raw codec frames). STT: Deepgram (Nova-2 and Nova-3), Soniox and 'Synthflow STT'; the 'Multilingual' language list matches Deepgram's ten-language multi set word for word (Nova-3 or Flux; inferred). TTS: ElevenLabs, Deepgram Aura-2 and 'Synthflow TTS'. LLM: OpenAI models plus an undisclosed 'Synthflow LLM'. Aurora (builder copilot) routes between Claude Sonnet and Haiku, yet Anthropic and Soniox are missing from the subprocessor list. The orchestrator is probably Python (aiohttp-style errors; inferred); in-house vs framework is unknown. No LiveKit, Daily or Pipecat on the browser path; LiveKit appears only as a 2024 dev Egress service account; a server-side framework cannot be ruled out.

Inference (computed from list prices, not an invoice): a Synthflow Indian outbound minute costs about INR 15.2-25.6 (FX 95). Low end: H1-2026 component rates $0.11-0.14 plus BYO Twilio to an Indian mobile at $0.0496. High end: Synthflow's own H1-2026 'PAYG typically $0.15-0.24', less its $0.02 managed US Twilio, plus Twilio India. Enterprise floor $30k/yr (INR 28.5 lakh); if it is a usage commitment the effective rate is INR 47.5/min at 5k min/month and INR 23.75 at 10k; if it is a fee on top, add those amounts. About 2-7x Indian list prices (INR 3.5-7). Reconstructed third-party COGS $0.034-0.085/min (INR 3.2-8.1, including an unsourced infra placeholder) implies a 39-69% gross margin against the H1-2026 rates.

Vapi's native telephony cannot carry a domestic Indian CLI:
- Observed: Vapi's Plivo guide says TRAI requires SIP termination on an Indian server, "which Vapi does not currently support". Twilio allows outbound to India only from non-Indian numbers. Free Vapi numbers are US-only. Regions are US (us-west-2), EU (Premier only) and AUS; there is no India region.
- Inference: on Vapi alone an Indian enterprise has no 140xx/1600xx/declared CLI and no DLT or A2P path. A bridge through an Indian-licensed provider (its media stream into Vapi's WebSocket transport) is the only route, and Vapi does not document it for India.
- Vendor-claimed, unverified: an Indian DID reseller's dev.to post says +91 inbound can terminate to Vapi's SIP URI.

nodes.title:
Vapi v2 notes (verified):
- No memory across voice calls. The nearest feature is chat Sessions (persistent chat context, 24 h default expiry, optional customerId). Voice personalisation is server-supplied variables at call time.
- The improvement loop is started by a human: monitors, issues, scorecards, evals, simulations, traffic splits without statistics, and a flag-gated Composer "Improve the assistant" kickoff. Once started, Composer can apply the fix, run simulations and, in "Bypass approvals" mode (2026-09-28), publish without pausing. The docs line "cannot deploy to production automatically" is stale.
- Unannounced alpha: Mission Control (sentiment cards, live listen, live call control).

nodes.rationale: Vapi ships the deepest developer surface: versioning, tools, logs with 638 ended reasons, evals, simulations, monitors, Composer and campaigns. Its native telephony cannot place calls with a domestic Indian CLI (only via a bridge through an Indian-licensed provider), and its list price for an Indian minute via Twilio is INR 12.5-17. So it sets the parity bar but competes for Indian buyers only through a bridge. The five tasks are where its documented behaviour fails Indian operations.

That supports the 'fee included' branch of the open question and makes the INR 8.0 all-in case unlikely at PAYG; it is unproven until an invoice or a billed call shows it. The 30-second pulse on telephony and platform also differs from the earlier 'billed per minute, rounded up' claim.

Observed in the Bolna dashboard (Engine tab of the saved synthetic agent): Endpointing 500 ms, Linear delay 900 ms, words before interrupting 1, Response Rate 'Custom'. These equal the API lane's stored values (500 / 900 / 1) and not the docs (400 / 2), and contradict the calibration note's 'hosted dashboard defaults' of 300 ms / 2 words / 300 s. Caveat: the agent's creation path is unknown and the New Agent draft's Engine tab was never opened, so what a dashboard-created agent gets is not settled. The UI shows the two sliders without a sum, so the 1.4 s reply floor is invisible to the builder.

Observed in the Bolna dashboard: the New campaign modal has three inputs (name, workflow plus version, contacts CSV or JSON up to 32 MB and 150,000 rows) and no consent, DND, DLT, retry or schedule field. The only calling-window control is per agent (Calling tab: Start 9:00 AM, End 9:00 PM, whole-hour selectors; enforcement default not seen), and the Violations tab is reactive ('Reports forwarded from telephony providers'). The default 9:00 to 21:00 matches Bolna's docs, not the 10:00 to 21:00 in ledger CMP-27.

Observed in the Bolna dashboard: the Vobiz KYC page says it verifies PAN + Aadhaar (persons) or PAN + GSTIN (companies), and the Compliance Settings table has a Tax ID Number column and no CIN column. This contradicts the earlier 'number KYC needs a CIN and accepts Pvt Ltd companies only'; the CIN rule may belong to the Plivo compliance application, which was not opened. The India number-buy dialog shows no price before Subscribe.

Inference from the Bolna dashboard: outbound has two entry points. Campaigns bind to a published workflow version (the New campaign Version select needs one), while Batches is a separate agent-scoped CSV upload. The shortest route to a first campaign is create agent, create workflow with an Agent node, publish, verify a phone number, then New campaign (about 5 to 7 steps before any dialling); Campaigns itself is Beta. The trial limit to verified numbers blocked it here.

Proposed v1 dashboard parity floor taken from Bolna's UI: a persistent per-minute cost header with a component bar; a transparent pricing table with pulse and included models; per-language prompt/voice/transcriber settings; a searchable voice picker with preview; tool presets plus custom function from cURL; webhook config with Send test; a workflow canvas with Wait, Retry, Condition, API, Callback and WhatsApp nodes; an Ask-the-platform chat that can read and act; per-page API and MCP buttons; async reports; SIP-trunk health columns; a Truecaller verification column; invoices and a recharge dialog with INR equivalents.
nodes.rationale: Each item is observed in the Bolna dashboard on 2026-10-21 and is either a measured-useful pattern or something a buyer coming from Bolna will expect on day one. The parity floor is a floor, not the wedge (open.2026-10-20.parity-floor-vs-wedge).
nodes.reverse_if: The call battery or buyer interviews show an item is unused or harms task success (for example nobody opens the workflow canvas, or the persistent cost header slows setup), or a later walkthrough shows Bolna removing it.

nodes.title: Proposed ways VP's dashboard beats Bolna's, each testable: (1) show the predicted reply gap (endpointing + hold + model) next to the turn-taking controls and give plain-language presets; (2) put consent, DND, calling-window and retry fields in the campaign itself, on by default; (3) one outbound system with no mandatory workflow; (4) show per-option latency and price in every model and voice picker; (5) price and bill in INR with GST, with per-number price shown before purchase; (6) editable, visible outcome judges; (7) an unsaved-changes indicator and visible versions; (8) a language-aware voice picker with no romance voices in business catalogues.
nodes.rationale: Bolna's dashboard hides the 1.4 s reply floor (500 + 900 ms, no sum shown), has compliance only at account and agent level, forces campaigns through workflows, shows no latency or per-option price, bills in USD and hides per-number price. Each gap was seen in a capture and maps to a measurable task (setup time, case handling, reply gap).
nodes.reverse_if: A live call shows Bolna's default reply gap p50 at or under about 1.0 s (the floor claim fails), or interviews show Indian buyers prefer USD invoices or a single flat price with no per-option detail.

Observed in the ElevenLabs dashboard: turn-taking is exposed as an eagerness enum (Normal), a turn model (Turn V3), a silence timeout in seconds and an interruption-ignore-terms list, not as millisecond endpointing or reply-delay constants; a banner says the ASR choice is locked because Turn V3 requires Scribe v2 Realtime, so turn model and ASR are one coupled choice. The read-back of the same agent shows turn_timeout 7 s, speculative_turn on, silence end-call never and an empty ignore-terms list. Help text for the ignore list gives English examples and says it 'seeds safe defaults for the agent's languages'; whether a Hindi preset exists was not shown.

Observed in the ElevenLabs dashboard: outbound is a single-page batch form of 7 inputs (name, phone number, ringing timeout 60 s, concurrency Auto, agent, CSV or XLS up to 25 MB with phone_number required, send now or schedule with a start time and timezone defaulting to Asia/Calcutta) with no calling window, retry rule, do-not-call, consent, DLT, price estimate or stated reason for a disabled Submit. The phone import menu has Twilio, SIP trunk and Exotel only; the Exotel panel defaults its region to Singapore under a +91 country code, with Mumbai as the other option. The hidden lead-level campaigns surface from the bundle is not visible in a new self-serve workspace.

Arithmetic on the ElevenLabs ElevenAgents plan cards: price over included minutes is $0.0800 on Starter ($6/75), Creator ($22/275) and Business ($990/12,375) and within $0.0001 of it on Pro ($99/1,238) and Scale ($299/3,738), equal to the $0.08/min pay-as-you-go rate, so included minutes are prepaid platform fee and tiers buy concurrency (4, 6, 10, 20, 30, 40), seats and features, not a lower rate. At the default LLM (DeepSeek Flash 4.1, about $0.0078/min displayed) a minute is about $0.0878, about INR 8.3 at FX 95 before telephony; in burst ($0.16) about INR 15.9.
nodes.n: 6 plans (Free to Business) from one subscription page capture
nodes.method: Division and FX 95 arithmetic on vendor-displayed prices read from 51-subscription.png and its text capture and 61-llm-list.txt; the vendor-displayed LLM figure is assumption-dependent (see evidence.2026-10-21.wt-elevenlabs-llm-price-assumption-gap); no invoice was read and no call was billed.

nodes.title: Observed: ElevenLabs Architect, the chat assistant that builds, tests and fixes agents, is offered from the New agent screen (Beta), the sidebar (Alpha) and every agent page, with the note 'free to use during the alpha, through October 2026' and no post-alpha price. Its home page carries a 10-item go-live checklist (agent context, user preferences, guardrails, KB auto-sync, procedures, simulation tests, custom data capture, eval criteria, live on a channel, issue flagging), 0 of 10 done on a new agent. It is the closest incumbent analogue to VP's chat-driven setup.

Proposed parity floor for VP v1 from the ElevenLabs dashboard (match, not beat): a model picker that shows latency range and cost per minute and per message on every row with a detailed-costs panel; a description with billing impact under every setting and an explained lock when one setting forces another; a test panel docked on every config page with a mock-tools switch; templates with a live flow preview; branches with traffic split and a Live badge; an inline CSV column contract (required, optional, custom variable columns) shown before upload; an analytics page with date range, granularity, group-by and branch filters; per-agent allowlist, authentication and per-call overrides; a go-live checklist inside the chat assistant.
nodes.rationale: These are surfaces an Indian enterprise buyer will expect from a top incumbent and none is a differentiator alone; the owner's v1 is parity made better (directive.2026-10-20.product-brief).
nodes.reverse_if: Buyer interviews or the call battery show these are not switching factors, or open.2026-10-20.parity-floor-vs-wedge resolves to a narrower floor.

nodes.title: Proposed places for VP to beat the ElevenLabs dashboard, each with a task: (1) an India-aware batch form with consent, DND/NCPR scrub, category-driven calling windows in IST, retries, a stated reason when Submit is disabled and a cost estimate; (2) a number path that offers India numbers with the KYC time and cost stated up front, instead of import-only with 7 provider fields; (3) turn-taking controls in milliseconds with Hindi and Hinglish back-channel lists on by default and a visible floor; (4) safe call-control defaults: end-call tool on, silence hang-up on, burst opt-in, AI disclosure in the first message, no open allowlist; (5) a Hinglish language option and Indic voice filters in the pickers; (6) an LLM cost strip that states its prompt-size assumption and itemises telephony; (7) a first-class contact object instead of a user-ID string; (8) every dashboard action reachable by chat.
nodes.rationale: Each item is a gap visible in the dashboard captures or a default the captures show; none is proven to change a buyer's choice.
nodes.reverse_if: A call battery shows ElevenLabs defaults already hold Hinglish turn-taking and hang up correctly, or ElevenLabs ships India compliance controls and Indian numbers in the self-serve dashboard.

nodes.title: What does a default dashboard-created ElevenLabs agent do on a live call to an Indian handset: does it ever hang up (the End conversation tool and silence hang-up are both off), does it burst to 2x price (bursting reads on), does it treat 'haan' and 'hmm' as interruptions (the ignore-terms list is empty), does it hold Hindi or Hinglish, and does it disclose it is an AI (the default first message does not)? The dashboard shows the settings; only a call shows the behaviour.
nodes.closes_when: A synthetic call battery of at least 30 clean turns plus the short back-channel set, to our own verified numbers over an Exotel or Plivo route, is run on an untouched dashboard-created agent and on the same agent with the ignore list, end-call tool and silence hang-up enabled, and the arms are compared on cut-ins, hang-up, language hold and billed cost (needs a number and an owner go).

nodes.title: Observed in the Exotel Voice Agents dashboard (trial account, 2026-10-21): the builder is a linear Bot > sub-agent > End graph; the top-level system prompt is locked behind a one-sentence 'strict guardrails' description, and the editable prompt is a raw markdown Instruction on the sub-agent. Rollout gives versions with a traffic split and Test Threads; Knowledge Base is a corpus table; Database is account-level tables; Tools is a custom-API form only; transfer and voicemail live in App Bazaar flows. Settings below the fold (denoiser 0.8, nudges 7 s x 3, PII masking off, greeting off) rest on Instinct's notes, not screenshots.

Inference from the Exotel dashboard notes: the only conversation-control settings captured are Denoiser, an empty VAD Configuration, Conversation Nudges (7 s, 3 times, then end call) and a disabled max-duration toggle. No endpointing, interruption, backchannel, reply-delay, DTMF or voicemail control was seen, so Exotel's turn-taking is not tunable by the buyer in the captured surfaces, unlike Vapi, Retell and ElevenLabs. Nudge-then-hang-up at 7 s x 3 is the same order as Bolna's 20 s hangup-on-silence. Whether the defaults are English-tuned is unknown until a call battery runs.

Exotel trial account as displayed on 2026-10-21: Credits 150 (classic top bar), Voice Agents Credit Usage 0 min, concurrency 0 / 5 across all agents with an increase 'subject to monthly charges' and no price; no per-minute rate, latency or quality figure shown in any Voice Agents capture; plan pricing is gated behind GST details. Vendor-displayed, not billed, not measured on a call.

Consistent with the account-free finding that windows and consent are left to the buyer. Fields Instinct did not list cannot be excluded, and the form could not be completed on the unverified account.

Is the Exotel trial account India-region or Singapore-region? Instinct's notes record account region Singapore and API subdomain api.exotel.com on my.exotel.com, while the Voice Agents app is on voicebot.in.exotel.com with a flow named mum-prod; the account-free checklist said to sign up on the India console because the region is fixed at sign-up. The API Settings screenshot was withheld, so this is notes-only.

nodes.title: Proposed from the Exotel dashboard: VP matches Exotel's day-one builder floor (versions with traffic split and test threads, knowledge-base corpora with training status, account-level lookup tables, custom-API tools with a test step, intents as outcomes, an interactions log with version column, emailed reports, a live concurrency meter) and beats it on testable tasks: one console from list to calls with plain-language gate messages, a browser test call and text simulation before any phone call, visible Hinglish turn-taking presets, calling-window and DND enforcement by default, and one contact store.
nodes.rationale: Each floor item is seen in the Exotel dashboard and a buyer moving from Exotel will expect it. Each beat maps to a gap seen in captures: a three-shell product, campaign loaders that fail with generic toasts, web call 'Coming soon', no endpointing or interruption controls, no consent or window fields, three contact surfaces, an Analytics frame that renders blank. The floor is a floor, not the wedge (open.2026-10-20.parity-floor-vs-wedge): the beats must be won on measured task failures.
nodes.reverse_if: A live call battery shows Exotel's default turn-taking and reply gap match VP's on the same Hinglish tasks, or buyer interviews show Indian enterprises value Exotel's carrier-grade numbers and KYC plumbing over any console improvement, or the owner decides to ride Exotel rails and not compete on console UX.

nodes.title: Questions only live calls and a KYC-verified account can answer for Exotel: reply gap and cut-ins on Indian PSTN with the Deepgram, Gemini and ElevenLabs stack; Hinglish language hold; DTMF, voicemail and transfer through App Bazaar flows around the bot; whether KYC clears the Caller ID and Lists load errors; which STT serves a call (Azure or Deepgram India); the create-agent form and Templates; Test Threads behaviour; what the Analytics frame shows when it loads; real per-minute price after GST.
