nodes.title: Blind set 5 (scored once at commit c213aff, before any tuning on it): benign FP 25/240 (10.4%; agent 24/160, caller 1/80), harmful caught 67/130 (51.5%; agent 28/70, caller 39/60). Devanagari and mixed-script lines and negation-then-request hard negatives were the weak spots
nodes.method: A separate agent that never saw rules.json, cases.json or sets 1-4 wrote 160 benign agent lines (half hard negatives), 80 benign caller lines (half hard negatives), 70 harmful agent lines (10 per kind, a third keyword-free) and 60 harmful caller lines (10 per signal, a third indirect), about a third each Hinglish, Devanagari and mixed script, with at least a third from clinics, D2C and education. Scored with replyDoor (service call, packs base+insurance_irdai+lending_rbi, one dues fact, disclosed, verified) and callerSignals. The rules were then tuned on its failures (coClause for RD4, Devanagari/mixed patterns), so set 5 is in-sample from commit ada4e26 on and is not reported as blind after that.

detail.not_verified: the hard-negative split, script mix and keyword-free share were written to spec by the generating agent but not counted by script

nodes.title: Learning's success metric uses each business's outcome_definition.goal_values (never a literal) and counts only contacts with a recorded outcome (verified, manager, or a trusted judge's guess); guardrails use catalogue reason codes END_OPTED_OUT, CONV_COMPLAINT, END_CRISIS on every live contact.
nodes.rationale: The calls builder found the earlier defaults ('success', 'opt_out'/'complaint') matched nothing calls writes, which silently disabled the decision and the hazard stop; untrusted AI guesses must never feed experiments (blueprint F4).
nodes.reverse_if: Calls changes where outcomes or reason codes live, or a validated leading indicator is approved as a primary metric for a tenant.

nodes.title: The agent builder's voice stack picker lists every stack from shared/stacks.ts with nothing preselected and nothing marked recommended; choosing is local until Save draft; Publish is disabled with a reason while no stack is chosen; tests of an agent with no stack come back 'invalid, with the reason', never a pass.

nodes.title: G5 treated any NCPR status outside the registered list as 'not registered', so 'unknown' passed promotional dials.
nodes.source: review WGC-01 (blocker), confirmed by reading gate.ts
nodes.broke: In production the DND provider is disabled and contact.dnd_refresh stamps checked_at with status 'unknown'. Every consented promotional row became dialable, including DND-registered numbers. Rule: an allow list ('not_registered' only), never a block list, for any fact that permits a call.

nodes.title: G5 took the latest consent record per purpose and accepted any granted covering purpose, so an older 'all' grant outranked a newer 'promotional' or 'service' withdrawal.
nodes.source: review WGC-03 (blocker), confirmed by reading gate.ts; WGC-06 adds that order was insert time, not consent time
nodes.broke: A person who withdrew from promotional calls was still called promotionally because an older 'all' grant counted as a basis. Re-importing an old consent=yes file also became the latest record. Rule: the newest record by effective time across every purpose covering the call's category decides; withdrawals win ties.

nodes.title: The kernel granted A3 (run at once) by actor type: any 'agent' ran attempt.retry_per_ladder, which re-dials a person, without a tap, though members asking for it got a card.
nodes.broke: The Operator acts for a member as an 'agent' carrying that member's role, so a chat turn, or text injected into an upload, could re-dial anyone with no human tap. Rule: approval follows the principal, not the actor type. An agent with a member's role is held exactly as that member. Only system and role-less agents are autonomous. One function, heldForApproval in server/tools.ts, decides for both the registry and the Operator's plan view.

nodes.title: Login and sign-up throttles were keyed on the raw X-Forwarded-For header, which the client controls.
nodes.broke: Rotating the header gave unlimited password guesses: 12 wrong passwords, 12 times 401, no 429. Rule: throttle per account, counting failures only, and per client address. The address comes from clientIp() in server/http.ts: the socket peer, or the right-most X-Forwarded-For hop that is not a trusted proxy (loopback and private ranges by default; VP_TRUSTED_PROXIES=none to trust none).

nodes.title: The never-deny-being-an-AI rule was a block list of denial shapes (RD2 claims_human); short natural denials matched none of them.
nodes.broke: 'Ji nahi, main bot nahi.', 'मैं machine नहीं, Riya हूँ।' and 'बिल्कुल इंसान हूँ।' reached TTS unchanged. The voice runtime also counted any 'bot' token as the disclosure. Rule: self-reference about her own nature is allowed only when it affirms AI-ness (an allow-list that over-triggers). A false positive costs one honest sentence; a false negative breaks a non-negotiable.

nodes.title: An outcome guess counts only if its quote is in a caller line of the stored transcript (by line index). If the only match is the agent's own words, the outcome is 'unclear' and not recorded
nodes.rationale: Review M6: the agent saying 'aap kal payment kar denge' while the person said 'Abhi nahi' was recorded as will_pay. An outcome is what the person said or did, so evidence must come from the person, as memory already requires.
nodes.reverse_if: An outcome definition is about the agent's own action (e.g. 'disclosure given'); then let that definition name the speaker its evidence must come from.

nodes.rationale: Each finding had a reproducing test against the real gate. The two blockers (WGC-01, WGC-03) made DND-registered or withdrawn people dialable.
nodes.reverse_if: Counsel rules that NCPR does not bind a consented promotional call, or intake supplies a structured consent effective-time column that should replace evidence.statedAt.

nodes.title: Intake writes age-like columns under three canonical keys (date_of_birth, age, is_minor) and exports the rule (AGE_KEY_SYNONYMS, canonicalAgeKey) for memory's children's-data gate
nodes.rationale: Memory's gate matched whole keys, so 'Customer DOB' -> customer_dob slipped past. One list, owned where headers are mapped, cannot drift. 'age' maps only when it names the person (Age, Customer Age, Age (years), Umar), so Vehicle Age or Policy Age keep their own keys.
nodes.reverse_if: A tenant needs two different person-age columns kept apart, or the gate moves to typed attributes with a declared meaning.

nodes.title: Attribute keys built with [^\p{L}\p{N}] split Devanagari words
nodes.tried: Snake-casing headers by keeping only Unicode letters and numbers.
nodes.broke: Vowel signs and the virama are marks (\p{M}), so 'उम्र' became 'उम_र' (caught by the age-key test). Keys now keep \p{M}.

nodes.title: Consent is ordered by its effective time (when it was given or withdrawn), not insert time; an older or undated imported grant after a withdrawal is history only
nodes.rationale: Review WGC-06: re-importing an old consent=yes file became the latest record and undid a newer withdrawal. consent_record.effective_at (0105) is the source's stated time, else the insert time, clamped so a source can never post-date its claim; latest = (effective_at DESC, created_at DESC). Undated grants following a withdrawal are stored just before it.
nodes.reverse_if: Counsel says a tenant's re-assertion of consent (undated) must count as a fresh grant; then require an explicit dated consent.record for it instead.

nodes.title: Two more canonical age keys: birth_year (Year of Birth, Birth Year, YoB, जन्म वर्ष) and age_group (Age Group/Band/Range/Bracket, आयु वर्ग), person-noun prefix allowed
nodes.rationale: Review WGC-09: these headers fell through as no age data, so memory ran for a 14-year-old. Memory reads birth_year as the younger possible age and fails closed on an age_group with any bound under 18.
nodes.reverse_if: The gate moves to typed attributes with a declared meaning.

nodes.title: Rejected: gating the shadow A/A on outcome-coverage imbalance across the shadow split (two-proportion p < 0.01).
nodes.tried: shadowAA() failed the plumbing check when the share of calls with an outcome differed between the two hash-split shadow arms at p < 0.01.
nodes.broke: The shadow arms are a hash of the contact id, so a real outcome-writer bug cannot correlate with them. The gate fired only by chance: 13 of 2,000 healthy datasets (150 contacts, 20 without an outcome). Each firing left the experiment unlaunched (aa_failed plus an issue), and it was the likely cause of the learning CI flake at 7bec779. The overall coverage floor is kept; the imbalance p is still reported.

nodes.title: Shadow A/A on healthy synthetic history (150 contacts, 30 successes, 20 without an outcome, random ids and salts): the coverage-imbalance gate fired 13/2,000 (runs 200) and 6/1,000 (runs 1,000). nodes.title: Caller-crisis judge, shared half: judge.json contract (fixed instruction prompt, caller text as quoted redacted data, schema {crisis, confidence, kind}, threshold 0.5, timeout 800 ms, modes off/shadow/raise, default shadow), judgeCallerCrisis and judgeTranscriptCrisis in TS, wired into practice runs (agents/simulate.ts), and an eval harness for the lab VM

A safety judge can only add a signal: the floor runs first and stands; the judge is skipped when the floor already fired; a timeout, error, bad output or missing model leaves the floor's verdict and logs judge_unavailable; with no keys it is never called; default mode is shadow, and raise needs the owner's go
nodes.rationale: Blind set 6 caught 4/30 indirect crisis lines with the floor. A model can hear indirection and new languages, but it must never make the floor weaker or become the only check, and it must not spend before keys exist.
nodes.reverse_if: Shadow data from live calls shows the judge's false alarms cost more than its catches (e.g. more than 1 false crisis per 100 calls), or its p95 exceeds the 800 ms budget on the runtime host; then keep it in shadow or replace it with a distilled local classifier.

nodes.title: In post-call analysis, a shadow-mode crisis-judge hit is recorded on the analysis (judge_shadow) and never written as a call_safety_event. Only a judge_raised hit becomes an RD3 'flagged' safety event.
nodes.rationale: Any call_safety_event row sets analysis.safety_violation (calls/analysis.ts). Learning reads safety_violation as an experiment guardrail (learning/index.ts, probe.ts tolerance 0), and the safety_event_rate monitor reads it too. A shadow hit written there would move experiments and monitors, so shadow would no longer change nothing, which breaks decision.2026-10-21.judge-raise-only-contract.
nodes.reverse_if: The owner sets mode 'raise' for post-call analysis, so hits are meant to count. Or safety_violation stops being derived from call_safety_event rows, and a separate shadow event type exists that no guardrail or monitor reads.

nodes.title: A runtime shadow judge that waits before speaking and logs its guesses as safety events
nodes.tried: The voice runtime attached the crisis judge's task to every reply whenever its mode was not 'off', and awaited it before the first sentence. It emitted judge_shadow and judge_unavailable as `safety` RD3 'flagged' events.
nodes.broke:
Two things, both caught in review before any keys were set:
- In shadow mode every turn could wait up to 800 ms for a verdict that cannot change anything.
- calls/ingest.ts turns every `safety` event into a call_safety_event row and the 'safety' flag. That drives analysis.safety_violation (learning's guardrail) and the safety_event_rate monitor. So every judge timeout and every shadow guess would have marked a call unsafe and moved experiments.
nodes.instead: Only mode 'raise' gates the reply; shadow runs fire-and-forget. Only judge_raised becomes a `safety` event (RD3 suspended_goal). Shadow and unavailable outcomes go to a separate `judge` runtime event, stored in call_judge_event, which nothing counts as safety (decision.2026-10-21.judge-shadow-never-a-safety-event).

nodes.title: In raise mode, each reply's first sentence waits for the crisis judge, up to its 800 ms timeout, so the judge's latency beyond the brain's first sentence adds to the reply gap on every turn.
nodes.mitigation: Measure it before the owner decides on raise. Run judge-eval on the lab VM for judge p50/p95, and compare against each stack's first-sentence time. The alternative is to speak first and cut into the crisis path when a raise lands, accepting about one sentence of normal reply before help is offered. Present both options with numbers.

nodes.title: Post-call crisis judge in calls: a raise hit is an RD3 'flagged' call_safety_event (counts as a safety event); a shadow hit lives only in analysis.judge_shadow and changes no event, flag, safety_violation, monitor or experiment
nodes.rationale: Keeps the shadow semantics of decision.2026-10-21.judge-raise-only-contract. learning and the safety_event_rate monitor read safety events, so a shadow row there would change outcomes. Calls loops over caller lines with safety's judgeCallerCrisis rather than judgeTranscriptCrisis, so it also sees judge_unavailable and the usage of every call, hit or not.
nodes.reverse_if: The owner moves the judge to raise in production (set VP_SAFETY_JUDGE_MODE=raise; the code path already exists), or safety extends judgeTranscriptCrisis to return unavailable counts and per-call usage; then call that instead of the local loop.

nodes.title: RuntimeEvent 'judge' (caller_crisis: mode shadow|raise, outcome raised|shadow|unavailable, kind, confidence, reason, latencyMs; never text) is stored in call_judge_event for analysis only. A live raise is two records: the 'safety' RD3 event (handling, flag, violation) and the 'judge' event (the judge's record)
nodes.rationale: The live runtime needs the same 'shadow counts nothing' rule as post-call analysis. Ingest writes no flag and no call_safety_event for a judge event. analysis.crisis_judge sums the runtime and post-call counts. It is not analysis.judge, which learning reads as the outcome judge.
nodes.reverse_if: The owner wants judge-unavailable outages to open an issue; then add a monitor on call_judge_event (outages only, never shadow hits).

nodes.title: Voice runtime audio path on the 4-vCPU sandbox: one runtime process holds about 25 concurrent phone calls before event-loop lag p99 passes 20 ms (12.8 ms at 25, 29.1 ms at 35); outbound audio stays on time to 35 calls and underruns at 50; one process is bound to one core (96% at 50); Silero VAD is the largest CPU cost (~24% of busy time), then numpy resampling and mu-law (~22%)
nodes.method: product/voice/bench/audio_bench.py --calls 10 25 35 50 --seconds 120 (metric as of fefbd7f), Python 3.13, Silero VAD, coding sandbox with 4 vCPU, 2026-10-21. Runtime in its own process; N Plivo-style mu-law 8 kHz media websockets over localhost through the real audio path (decode, 8->16 kHz FIR, Silero VAD, cascade turn-taking, reply door, 24->8 kHz FIR, encode, playAudio). Fake providers: final transcript +300 ms, first sentence +700 ms, first audio +250 ms then 2x real time. Callers: synthetic Azure TTS phone stimuli, ~2 s talk / 4-6 s quiet. n = outbound frames judged (26,354 + 65,485 + 91,478 + 128,747), after a 10 s warm-up. Results: N=10 cpu 32% (3.2%/call), RSS 175 MB, loop lag p50/p99/max 0.7/3.6/49.7 ms, frames >20 ms late 71 (0.27%), runtime turn-end->first-audio overhead p50/p99 176/204 ms (VAD end-of-speech 160 ms included). N=25 cpu 67%, 320 MB, lag 0.9/12.8/116.7, late 81 (0.12%), overhead 177/268. N=35 cpu 88%, 405 MB, lag 1.5/29.1/328, late 147 (0.16%), overhead 183/302. N=50 cpu 96%, 559 MB, lag 4.9/94.3/345.8, late p99 36.4 ms, 1,486 late (1.15%), overhead 209/484. Profile at N=30 (cProfile, 60 s): onnxruntime run 14.1 s of ~58 s busy; FIR correlate 3.4 s, ulaw_decode 3.5 s, downsampler 3.0 s, ulaw_encode 1.8 s; websocket parse/send ~4 s; reply-door regex 0.6 s. Load generator lag p99 1.4-1.7 ms (its numbers are trustworthy). Not measured: real providers, real carrier jitter buffers, the deploy host, more than one process.
nodes.value: ~25 calls per runtime process (one core) on the sandbox; RSS ~10 MB per call

nodes.title: Calls per deploy host. On the sandbox, 4 worker processes carry 90 calls at lag p99 8.3 ms, so it scales with processes (measure.2026-10-21.voice-audio-multiprocess-sandbox). Inference until measured there: about 20-25 per vCPU at the default cap. Unbuilt levers, by expected gain: batch Silero VAD across a process's calls into one onnx run (~24% of CPU today); mu-law by lookup table and a cheaper 8<->16 kHz resampler (~22%); run the VAD only every second window while the caller is silent

nodes.title: Kernel control calls to the voice runtime with an empty body

nodes.title: Voice runtime across 4 worker processes on the 4-vCPU sandbox: 60 and 90 concurrent phone calls stay under the single-process knee; 90 calls (22-23 per worker) shows lag p99 8.3 ms and 0.16% late frames, against 12.8 ms at 25 calls in one process. Calls-per-host scales with processes
nodes.method: product/voice/bench/audio_bench.py --calls 60 90 --seconds 120 --workers 4, Python 3.13, Silero VAD, coding sandbox with 4 vCPU (the load generator shares the cores), 2026-10-21. The harness and fake providers are as in measure.2026-10-21.voice-audio-capacity-sandbox. Runtime: python -m vpvoice.launch with 4 workers, cap 30 each. Tickets go through the launcher front (least-loaded placement). Media goes straight to each worker's port, as nginx would route /w/<i>/; nginx's own cost is not measured. n = outbound frames judged: 156,991 + 234,636 + 233,473 for the front-media run. N=60: placed 15/15/15/15; cpu 176% summed (44-45% per worker, 2.9%/call); RSS 889 MB; loop lag p50/p99/max 0.8/5.4/50.3 ms; 76 frames >20 ms late (0.05%); overhead p50/p99 176/201 ms. N=90: placed 22/23/23/22; cpu 240% (58-62% per worker); 1,182 MB; lag 0.9/8.3/726.6; 368 late (0.16%); overhead 177/368; generator lag p99 2.9 ms. N=90 with media through the front: lag 1.0/9.7/65.6; 154 late (0.07%); overhead 178/215; front process cpu 33%. The 726 ms max is one stall, n=1 per configuration, and it did not recur; cause not isolated. Not measured: the deploy host, real providers, nginx in the path, more than 4 workers.
nodes.value: 90 calls on 4 vCPU at 22-23 per process: lag p99 8.3 ms, 0.16% late frames; a Python media hop through the front costs ~0.37% of a core per call

nodes.title: The voice runtime caps each process at VP_MAX_CALLS_PER_PROCESS (default 20). Past the cap it refuses tickets at intake with 503 at_capacity, Retry-After and placed:false, before any record, sink or event. A host runs one worker per core (python -m vpvoice.launch). A front places tickets least-loaded, overflows on at_capacity and routes call routes to their owner. Media is routed to workers by the /w/<i>/ prefix (nginx or ingress in production), not SO_REUSEPORT
nodes.rationale: The audio path is CPU-bound in one Python core per process, with the knee between 25 and 35 calls (measure.2026-10-21.voice-audio-capacity-sandbox). 20 leaves headroom for real providers. SO_REUSEPORT spreads connections at random, but a call's ticket, media socket and carrier webhooks must reach the same process, and idempotency is per process. A refusal before anything is created is safe to resend, so the dialer can treat it as not placed rather than as a failed attempt.
nodes.reverse_if: the deploy-host bench puts the per-process knee well away from 25 (move the default cap); or VAD batching or a native audio path lifts per-process capacity enough that one process per host suffices; or the ingress cannot route by path prefix (then switch to per-worker ports or a front that proxies media, at ~0.37% of a core per call)

nodes.title: A supervisor whisper is untrusted guidance for her next reply only. It is redacted, capped at 300 characters and placed in the LAST block as a colleague's note (never quoted, ignored where it conflicts). It is spent after one reply and appears in no event. Her reply still goes through the reply door, so a whisper telling her to deny being an AI is blocked by RD2 (tested)
nodes.rationale: Position is mechanism: the LAST block is where per-turn guidance takes effect. A whisper comes from a person, but it is still free text into the model, so it gets the same redaction and the same door as anything else. Spending it after one reply keeps a stale note from steering later turns.
nodes.reverse_if: supervisors need standing guidance for the rest of the call (then a separate, still-doored, persistent note), or whisper-driven replies measurably break RD rules the door does not catch

nodes.title: On takeover she stops for good. A held reply is dropped; a playing one is cut at its sentence end if that is within 300 ms, else at once. One doored hand-off line plays and hand_off {reason:'takeover', target:'member:<id>'} is emitted. The member is bridged both ways through the runtime's media socket. Caller speech is still transcribed; the member's is not (v1). Her limits, door and judge stop acting. A member drop, or nobody joining within 60 s, closes the call with one doored line as handed_off; she is never brought back. A crisis call can be taken over and only a runaway guard (2x duration) ends it, silently
nodes.rationale: Owner-loop constraints of 2026-10-21: the AI never speaks again after a person joins, no misrepresentation in the hand-off line, no silent return of the AI. The bridge runs through the runtime, so it works the same on browser and SIP without a carrier transfer. hand_off.target is a free string, so the contract does not change.
nodes.reverse_if: members need their speech in the transcript (then transcribe the member leg as a new speaker, which is a contract change); or carrier-side transfer is needed for quality or cost; or the owner prefers that a dropped member returns the caller to her with disclosure instead of ending the call

nodes.title: Listen is a receive-only socket carrying both legs mixed (pcm16le 16 kHz) on the caller's 20 ms clock. Nothing from it is recorded or stored, and it is allowed even after a recording refusal (monitoring, not retention). Closing it never ends the call, and it takes no call slot. It is counted in health and marked by a live_listen_started/ended moment pair per listener
nodes.rationale: A supervisor must hear the call as the caller does, without being heard and without creating a retained copy. The moment pair gives the call page its listened-from/to timeline, and carries no audio and no listener id.
nodes.reverse_if: a jurisdiction treats live monitoring of a call that refused recording as needing consent, or the timeline needs the listener's identity from the runtime rather than the control plane's audit

nodes.title: Closed: runtime-protocol.ts and ingest list the supervisor moments (3a84688), and the runtime emits them. live_listen_started and live_listen_ended come as one pair per listener, closed before call.ended. whisper is emitted with no note, and takeover alongside its hand_off. The runtime fixture's supervisor_live call passes calls' validateRuntimeBatch (product/tests/voice-runtime-events.test.ts 4/4, and the live validator in tests/test_runtime_fixture.py)
nodes.closes_when: the contract lists the kinds and the runtime emits them, or the timeline reads the control-plane audit instead

nodes.title: Browser flows that only ever ran in builder sandboxes
nodes.tried: tests/web.test.ts runs the 13 browser flows when a precheck finds Chromium and Postgres 16 binaries, and skips with a reason otherwise. The CI control-plane job has neither.
nodes.broke: Every CI run skipped all 13 flows, so CI green never covered the approval hold, the Ask Saarthi paths, the developer-text scan or the plan-card refusals. A load-sensitive race in those flows was found only because one builder ran the suite in parallel by chance.
nodes.instead: A web-e2e CI job (5e9253d) installs Chromium and Postgres 16, requires the precheck to pass (a skip is a failure), runs product/web/e2e/run.sh, and uploads the failing flows' screenshots and logs.

nodes.title: Browser tests that hold a button, or read server state, on wall-clock time
nodes.tried: The e2e hold() pressed for a fixed 1,500 ms against the button's 1,200 ms timer. One flow read the server's proposals as soon as the plan card appeared.
nodes.broke: Under CPU load (6 busy loops on 4 cores) 1 in 4 runs failed. The browser could deliver the press late and the release right after it, so the hold never completed. The plan card renders before the server has filed the proposal. Neither was a product bug.
nodes.instead: Wait on the condition the flow needs: the button's holding/finished state, the proposal row existing, or polling instead of fixed sleeps. 12 of 12 runs passed under the same load after the fix, and the full suite passed 372 of 372 three times on a fresh database.

nodes.title: Owner: Vertex is back (vp-voice reinstated); use it, and give Instinct a prompt for anything that needs setting up.

Google Cloud Trust & Safety email to the owner: project vp-voice reinstated 'based on information that you have provided'. It asks us to fix any outstanding issues so the project complies with the GCP Terms of Service and Acceptable Use Policy. The same notice is in Cloud Logging. Seen as phone screenshots at about 00:02 IST on 22 Oct.

The new vp-voice service-account key goes from the owner's machine straight to the India lab VM by a write-only, one-blob Azure SAS link with a 12 h expiry. It never passes through chat, Drive or the agent's context. The VM pulls it, the blob is deleted, and only client_email and project_id are checked.
nodes.rationale: A key pasted in chat was one of the three likely triggers of the 2026-10-20 restriction. The appeal promised that key was deleted and that Agent Platform is called only from the India server. The SAS link was tested: PUT returned 201 and GET returned 403.
nodes.reverse_if: Google Workload Identity Federation from the Azure VM's managed identity is set up, so no key exists at all, or org policy blocks key creation.

nodes.title: The vp-voice appeal's statements bind every later use. Agent Platform is called only from India (the lab VM now, and the product's voice runtime when deployed). There is one key, holding Vertex AI User only. Spend is capped at INR 20,000 with alerts. There are no evaluation batches in the first 48 h after the key lands, then at most 1 request/s, from the VM only.
nodes.rationale: Google reinstated the project on the information in that appeal. Using it differently would make the appeal untrue and risk a second, harder action.
nodes.reverse_if: Google confirms a different usage pattern is fine, or traffic moves to a paid project under its own terms.

nodes.title: If the product's voice runtime is deployed outside India and routes Gemini through Vertex (product/voice/vpvoice/providers/google.py routes there whenever VERTEX_SA_FILE is set), it breaks the appeal's India-only statement.
nodes.mitigation: Deploy the voice runtime in Azure Central India (vp-research-rg) or leave VERTEX_SA_FILE unset outside India. The deploy plan presented to the owner must say which.

nodes.title: Keeping the pasted vp-voice key (id ending a6d78b) in the scratchpad for redeploys
nodes.tried: lab_ops.secrets() sends scratchpad vertex-sa.json to the VM as VERTEX_SA_B64 on every deploy.
nodes.broke: Every redeploy would have pushed back the key the appeal said was deleted. If Google had not deleted it, that key would be live again on the VM.
nodes.instead: The local copy was deleted on 2026-10-21. vm_setup.sh leaves the VM's key file alone when VERTEX_SA_B64 is empty, so the new key delivered by the hand-off survives redeploys.

nodes.title: A Run practice callers button that is live before the caller library has loaded
nodes.tried: test-panel.tsx always rendered an enabled 'Run 6 practice callers' button. The default six were picked in a useEffect only after simcaller.list returned.
nodes.broke: A click before the list arrived ran zero callers: simulate(agent, []) resolved at once to an empty list. The person saw '0 of 0 passed' under a button that promised 6. CI web-e2e on 5e9253d failed this way, with a 30 s wait for the first result. It passed 13/13 on 4afd749, where the flow took 1.7 s. A 3 s delay on simcaller.list reproduced the failure in the practice flow and in the Copy flow.
nodes.instead: The default selection is derived on the same render the list arrives. The button reads 'Run N practice callers' with N the callers that will run. It is busy until the list loads, disabled with a reason when the list fails or nothing is picked, and run() refuses an empty pick. The practice flow now holds the list back 1.5 s on every run. That guard fails on the old panel and passes on the fix, and the suite passed 13/13 with it.

nodes.title: Owner: use Vertex AI for everything Google/Gemini (text brains, TTS voices, Live ears and speech-to-speech), in the product and the lab.

Gemini runs only through Vertex (project vp-voice, from India). The Gemini API key route and the OpenRouter Gemini route are retired from the product and the lab. A Gemini model or feature that Vertex does not offer makes its stack unavailable, with a plain reason. It is never rerouted to the API key or OpenRouter.
nodes.rationale: Owner directive. It also leaves one credential, one project and one data-terms regime for Google, which is what the reinstatement appeal described. The OpenRouter and API-key routes existed only as workarounds while Vertex was restricted and the keys were capped.
nodes.reverse_if: A model the owner wants is only on the Gemini API (e.g. a Live model with no Vertex release), or Vertex quota in India cannot carry the product's concurrent calls.

nodes.title: Vertex AI Live API and Gemini TTS, from Google's public docs read 2026-10-21. Endpoint: wss://{LOCATION}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/ws/google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.LlmBidiService/BidiGenerateContent with an OAuth bearer token. gemini-3.8-live (GA) is listed in us / eu / us-central1 only, not India and not global. gemini-3.5-transcribe-live-preview exists (text out). Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS is listed as preview via the Gemini Enterprise API only. Vertex TTS ids are gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview and gemini-2.5-flash(-lite-preview)/pro-tts
nodes.value: Live on Vertex is regional and, per the model pages, not offered in India; 3.8 TTS may not be on Vertex generateContent

nodes.title: The voice runtime reaches Gemini only through Vertex. Model ids and locations are configuration, with no API-key or OpenRouter fallback: VERTEX_MODEL_MAP (our id -> Vertex id), VERTEX_LOCATION (text/TTS, default global), VERTEX_LIVE_LOCATION (Live, no default). A model Vertex does not offer, or Live without a location, makes the stack unavailable before the call, with a plain reason per component. There is no Live default location because the docs list gemini-3.8-live outside India only
nodes.rationale: Owner directive decision.2026-10-21.gemini-vertex-only. What Vertex offers moves faster than code. The owner's console report and Instinct's Model Garden read decide the real ids and regions, so the runtime must not guess them, and must refuse rather than reroute. Calling a us-central1 Live endpoint from an India-hosted runtime keeps the India-only calling promise, but it puts processing outside India: that is the owner's call, not a default.
nodes.reverse_if: Vertex lists the Live models in asia-south1 (then default VERTEX_LIVE_LOCATION=asia-south1); or the owner rules that Live processing must stay in India (then the Gemini-ears stacks stay unavailable, and the ears move to Sarvam or Azure); or the console shows different model ids (update DEFAULT_MODELS)

nodes.title: Every v2 stack except sarvam-india uses Gemini ears over Live, and the docs list gemini-3.8-live (and so probably the transcribe-live preview) only in us / eu / us-central1. Does the owner accept Live processing outside India from an India-hosted runtime? If not, which ears replace Gemini's? Also open: whether the 3.8 Flash(-Lite) TTS voices are on Vertex at all (the docs say Enterprise API preview only) Counter-evidence on TTS: the 2026-10-20 appeal record (research/2026-10-20/voicelab/google-access.md) says the lab generated speech with Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS through Vertex on 19-20 Oct, so the docs reading may be incomplete; the Model Garden report decides.
nodes.closes_when: the owner's console report gives the Live and TTS model ids and regions, and the owner rules on Live processing location

nodes.title: An approval sheet that offers the hold before the change's details have loaded
nodes.tried: The approval sheet fetched the change's arguments (amount, cap, audience) in a useEffect, while 'Hold to approve' was available at once.
nodes.broke: On a slow request a person could approve a ₹500 top-up without the ₹500 on screen. The web builder found it in the audit for the run-before-library pattern.
nodes.instead: The sheet shows a loading line and no hold until the arguments are in. If they fail to load, the hold is disabled with a reason: not safe to approve blind. A 14th browser flow holds /v1/actions back 1.5 s; it failed on the old sheet and passes on the fix. The audit of the other screens was by code reading only, not runtime delays.

nodes.title: Owner: Gemini (Vertex) may process call audio and text wherever Google processes it: the US, EU or global endpoints are acceptable.

Owner: no Google Cloud project was created on compliance@carbonsettle.com. VP uses Vertex only from team@vyakti.ai, project vp-voice. The owner made the new key and checked the console personally; Instinct was not used.

Owner: the product UI is never written in Hindi or Hinglish (e.g. a 'Suprabhat, Asha' greeting is unacceptable). VP is a world-class product for medium-to-large Indian enterprises first; small businesses only by use case. Every screen must read as professional enterprise software. The agents' spoken Hinglish on calls is the product's voice, not UI copy.

Owner: the user selects the whole voice stack, component by component (ears/STT, brain, voice/TTS, or a speech-to-speech engine), at least for testing. A default stack is also offered. Which components work best is decided later, from real use-case calls on the finished product.
Owner: route every model by availability. Gemini goes through Vertex. Anything available in Azure AI Foundry goes through Azure Foundry. Only what is in neither goes through OpenRouter.

Owner restated the bar. VP must beat every competitor on quality, value and price: emotional, relational, expressive agents that are self-learning and personalised, deliver better conversions and metrics, offer world-class UI/UX and product journeys, and are run through LLM agents so the user does less and makes fewer mistakes. The analytics and the learning are LLM-driven. Nothing gimmicky.

The new vp-voice service-account key (id ending 4589e6) was pasted in chat by the owner, who said that is acceptable. A pasted key was one of the three suspected triggers of the 2026-10-20 restriction.
nodes.mitigation: Use it only from the India VM and keep the ramp (no batches for 48 h, then at most 1 request/s). Once the lab is stable, offer the owner a rotation through the write-only upload path, so the live key has never been in chat.

nodes.title: Vertex on vp-voice from the India VM, new key. Text: gemini-3.5-flash-lite, 3.6-flash and 3.8-flash all 200 (0.95-1.67 s for 5 tokens). TTS: gemini-3.8-flash-tts 200 (2.07 s, whole clip) and 3.8-flash-lite-tts 200 (1.65 s), so both ARE on Vertex generateContent, contrary to the docs reading; 3.1-flash-tts-preview 20.1 s; 2.5-flash-tts 3.06 s. Live: gemini-3.8-live gives setupComplete only at us-central1 (2.08 s including connect). It reports 'not found' in europe-west4, europe-west1 and asia-south1, gives 404 on the us/eu hosts, and refuses TEXT output ('Unsupported modality for Vertex Live API'). gemini-3.5-transcribe-live-preview and gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview are 'publisher model not found' at us-central1 and europe-west4. TLS connect is about 30 ms to every aiplatform host.
nodes.n: 1 request per model/region (about 22 in all, spaced about 2 s apart)
nodes.method: Run Command probe scripts on vl-vm-cin (Central India) with the service account's bearer token: generateContent (global) and the Live websocket setup (LlmBidiService v1), reading close reasons. No call came from the sandbox.

nodes.title: Gemini ears are retired: Vertex offers no Gemini transcription model, and Live refuses text-only output. Ears go to Azure Speech (Central India, streaming hi-IN), per the routing rule that what Azure has goes to Azure. The lab's round-2 stacks (v2-flashlite, v2-54mini, v2-38flash, v2-mai, v2-luna) now listen with Azure Speech. The older Gemini-ears presets show unavailable, with a reason. VERTEX_MODEL_MAP maps gemini-3.5-transcribe-live to null.
nodes.rationale: The probe found 'publisher model not found' for the transcribe model in both regions, and 'Unsupported modality' for TEXT out on 3.8-live. Azure Speech was measured at 0.45 s from India. One measured weakness: a quiet elderly 'hmm' was missed (ledger.LAT-06).
nodes.reverse_if: Vertex lists a Gemini transcription model for vp-voice, or measured Hinglish WER or turn-taking on Azure ears is clearly worse than another available ear (Sarvam Saaras, or gpt-4o-transcribe on Azure).

nodes.n: 1 call x 2-3 replies per stack
nodes.method: voicelab/tests/sim_caller.py on the VM against the deployed lab: synthetic Hinglish caller clips (g5 battery), 3 turns, scenario renewal. Cost from the lab meter.

nodes.title: VERTEX_LIVE_LOCATION=us-central1, the only region where gemini-3.8-live set up for vp-voice. The owner accepts processing outside India (directive.2026-10-22.processing-anywhere).
nodes.rationale: Measured: setupComplete at us-central1 only.
nodes.reverse_if: Live set-up succeeds in a nearer region (europe-west4 or asia-south1), measured by the same probe.

nodes.title: Provisional default stack: v2-flashlite (Azure ears + Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite brain + Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite voice). New agents start on it, stack.list names it, and the user can change it. Agents saved before the default keep stackId '' and must choose before they publish.
nodes.rationale: The owner asked for a default plus free choice, and leans towards Gemini voices. Flash-Lite was the fastest well-judged brain (0.70 s to first text, 2026-10-20). Every part is on Vertex or Azure, and the 22 Oct smoke completed with 0 errors (2.0-2.7 s reply gap). v2-live is faster (1.1-1.5 s) but beta: it talks over callers and has not passed the safety attack test.
nodes.reverse_if: Round-2 human ratings or the first real use-case calls favour another stack on quality, reply gap or conversion; or Gemini TTS pricing (doubling 2027-01-01) or availability changes.

nodes.title: Build your own: voice = { stackId: 'custom', components: { ears, brain, voice, gatedEars } | { s2s } }, with parts drawn from shared/components.ts (ids are the runtime's catalog keys). resolveStack() is the one resolver for every caller (createVersion, ticket builders, the campaign gate, blockers). Every CallTicket carries stack.components. A built stack is always beta, so it runs test calls only until measured. Its availability is every part's runtime health, and it is unknown until the runtime reports parts.
nodes.rationale: The owner wants component-level choice 'at least for testing', while calls to real people stay on measured, safety-tested combinations. Beta already blocks non-test dials (decision.2026-10-21.beta-stacks-test-only), so no new gate is needed. One resolver means no caller can read a custom stack differently.
nodes.reverse_if: Measured custom combinations should go live: add a promote path that measures one and marks it available.

nodes.title: stack.set keeps the chosen voice when the part that speaks (the voice or s2s component) is unchanged, e.g. switching only the brain. It clears the voice only when the speaking part changes.
nodes.rationale: A voice name belongs to the TTS or s2s part, not to the whole stack. Clearing it on a brain change threw away a choice that still applied.
nodes.reverse_if: Voices start depending on the brain (e.g. a per-brain style map).

nodes.title: Routing in the parts catalog: Gemini goes through vertex. GPT-4.1/5.4 mini, gpt-oss, Llama and Kimi go through azure-foundry (India, or Singapore for Kimi). The GPT-6 and GPT-5.6 tiers go through OpenRouter, because our Foundry quota for them is held by Taxila. Sarvam goes direct. gpt-oss-120b@groq (OpenRouter) is not offered, because gpt-oss-120b is on our Foundry.
nodes.rationale: Owner directive.2026-10-22.provider-routing. Cost of the Groq rule: gpt-oss first token was 0.48 s on Groq against 1.47 s on Azure (lab, n=6, 2026-10-19).
nodes.reverse_if: The owner prefers Groq's speed for gpt-oss, or Foundry quota for the GPT-6 tiers becomes ours.

nodes.title: The in-product assistant is shown as 'Assistant', not 'Saarthi'. Internal code names (operator) are unchanged.
nodes.rationale: There are two reasons. The owner's directive rules out Hindi in the UI. Saarthi.ai is also an existing Indian voice-AI competitor in collections (ledger.SEG-10), so the name would clash with their brand.
nodes.reverse_if: The owner picks a brand name for the assistant.

nodes.title: The product voice runtime had no Azure Speech ears (only Gemini and Sarvam). build() also sent every non-gemini ears kind to SarvamEars, so 'azure' ears would have run Sarvam with no model.
nodes.mitigation: The voice builder is porting the lab's Azure Speech ears, with a fake-based test. Until then, Azure-ears stacks must show unavailable at the runtime, never fall into SarvamEars.

nodes.title: Independent review of the built-stack contract (d6b1d97 + 0c5997a). Found clean: no path for a built stack to dial a real person (always beta, refused at G10); voiceId kept or cleared correctly; no draft-hash drift; built and curated stacks with the same parts price identically for all 7. Found and fixed: (1) availability read 'available' while the runtime refused 'custom'; (2) compile.ts dropped SOUNDS and DELIVERY for built stacks; (3) campaign rate and estimate ignored a built stack's parts; (4) money.estimate silently priced a curated stack that was sent with parts. Handed on: the web client reads getStack(stackId) in 4 places (test panel, beta warnings, call label); the launcher's /v1/health drops components and customStacks.
A built stack is available only when the runtime's health says customStacks: true and every part is available. Healthy parts alone are not enough.
nodes.rationale: The review found the parts reading healthy while the runtime refused stack 'custom'. The person would have picked a stack that could never ring.
nodes.reverse_if: Every runtime in service runs built stacks and the flag is retired by a protocol version bump.

nodes.title: The member-phone verification call (campaigns verify.ts announcement()) is spoken in English. It is a fixed system announcement to the business's own staff, so the enterprise-English directive applies. Hinglish stays for agents talking to customers.
nodes.rationale: Integrator ruling on directive.2026-10-22.enterprise-english-ui after the web builder changed the script in 1187a05. The campaigns test checks the script through announcement(), not its wording (840ae68).
nodes.reverse_if: The owner wants staff-facing system calls in the member's chosen language, or Hinglish for this call.

nodes.title: Reading a call's run-manifest components one-to-one as stack parts
nodes.tried: web data.ts mapped manifest {stt, llm, tts ?? voice, s2s} straight onto {ears, brain, voice, s2s} and resolved it with stackOf.
nodes.broke: The manifest's `voice` is the voice's name (Kore, hi-IN-Kavya), not a part, and `stt` ends in '/ungated' when the ears ran ungated. On the real runtime, a built speech-to-speech stack and ungated ears both showed 'A stack that is no longer listed' on the call page (2 of 3 manifest shapes unresolved). Devsim named an s2s run as 'llm', so the browser flows could not see it.
nodes.instead: web/src/catalog.ts partsRan() maps the manifest to parts (s2s alone, or ears without the suffix + brain + tts). Devsim names an s2s run as the real runtime does. A unit test in tests/web.test.ts covers the three shapes and fails on the old mapping (95f1799).

nodes.title: Launch-readiness audit of product/ against the blueprint's must-bes and the owner's 2026-10-22 bar (read-only, code and tests, not context claims). DONE: bounded call and spend defaults, state integrity, AI disclosure, horizontal (17 templates, 12 industries, 9 sector packs), stack part by part plus a default, English UI (apart from leftovers). PARTIAL: price and latency at every choice, contacts DND, chat-driven setup, LLM analytics, learning loop. MISSING: a customer price. First-week blockers: (1) a tenant cannot fund calls (top-up off, no trial credit, no member can credit); (2) no carrier KYC path, so no real call dials; (3) the Operator offers 166 tools (~21k tokens) per model call against a 60k-token turn cap; (4) no customer price; (5) DND provider off and no suppress/export UI; (6) integrations dead loop (assistant refuses credentials, Settings has no form); (7) cross-call analytics are counters only; (8) reply-gap labels oversold.
nodes.n: 1 audit; tsc clean; 181 tests across e2e, operator, learning, agents-tools, web, campaigns, money and intake passed
nodes.method: Read-only subagent at high effort over product/ at 54ebd67, with file:line evidence; the main loop re-checked the operator tool count, the reply-gap figures and the stack.list price before acting.

nodes.title: Headlining time-to-first-reply-text as a stack's reply gap
nodes.tried: shared/stacks.ts showed '0.70 s, reply text starts' (v2-flashlite, the default), '0.96 s' (v2-54mini) and '0.43 s, voice starts after the text' (v2-mai) under the 'Reply gap' heading. The picker's footnote defines reply gap as caller-finishes to first audio.
nodes.broke: The default stack read 0.70 s while its measured whole gap from India is 2.0-2.7 s (measure.2026-10-22.round2-smoke-vertex). Stacks measured on different bases sat side by side, so a buyer would rank them wrongly.
nodes.instead: Whole measured gaps headline (v2-flashlite 2.0-2.7 s, v2-mai 1.8-2.1 s, v2-38flash 2.6-2.7 s; one call of 2-3 replies each). Stacks without a whole gap on their current parts read 'not measured', with the partial figures in the source. tests/shared.test.ts refuses a partial figure in the headline (5d9bca0).

nodes.title: stack.list returning price 'not measured' while the picker computes it
nodes.tried: agents stackCard hard-coded pricePerMinute 'not measured' ('money.estimate not wired into the picker yet').
nodes.broke: The picker had since been wired to money.estimate, so the Operator (which reads stack.list) and the screen disagreed on price. The source string was developer text that would have reached a person.
nodes.instead: stack.list calls money.estimate through the registry. It reads 'not measured' only when money is absent or has no lines. A test asserts parity with money.estimate for every curated stack (5d9bca0).

nodes.title: The Operator replies in professional English by default. A client's saved presentation preference may change that; the default never mirrors Hinglish.
nodes.rationale: directive.2026-10-22.enterprise-english-ui: product copy is never Hindi or Hinglish, and the Operator's replies are product copy. Before, loop.ts told it to mirror Hinglish.
nodes.reverse_if: The owner rules that the assistant should mirror the client's language.

nodes.title: Owner: the trial credit for a new workspace. The blueprint recommends ₹500; the mechanism is built with the amount in config, default 0, because price is deferred.
nodes.closes_when: The owner names the trial credit amount (or confirms none).

nodes.title: Owner: the DND (NCPR) lookup. Contract an NCPR lookup, or rely on carrier scrubbing. Until then every number reads 'DND not checked' and promotional calls stay blocked.
nodes.closes_when: The owner picks an NCPR lookup provider or confirms carrier scrubbing.

nodes.title: Cross-call insight in calls: themes (objections, drop-offs, unanswered questions, what preceded a reached goal) across a scope's recent analysed calls, every quote verbatim and verified, through insight.get / insight.refresh and a nightly job

A cross-call theme is kept only with 2+ quotes that are exact substrings of one line of the cited call's stored transcript. Objections and unanswered questions must quote the person, and success drivers only calls whose best outcome is a goal value. Its count is the distinct sampled calls it was seen in, never the model's own number
nodes.rationale: The owner's bar for LLM-driven analytics the business can trust: every claim about calls must be backed by what was said, the same law as per-call analysis. A test proves the guard is what stops a fabricated quote: with a trusting grounder the quote survives.
nodes.reverse_if: Labelled review shows true themes are dropped too often because of transcript normalisation (matras, romanisation); then match on a normalised form and still cite the original span.

nodes.title: Insight runs are bounded: 40 most recent calls, an input budget of 12,000 tokens x 4 characters (whole calls only), 1,500 output tokens, a 30-day window, and no run when no call ended since the last insight. Nightly covers at most 100 workspaces with 10 agent or campaign scopes each
nodes.rationale: The owner wants cost-bounded analytics. These caps keep a nightly run to about one small LLM call per active scope; the numbers are untuned guesses.
nodes.reverse_if: Measured cost per run or theme quality on real calls says the caps are too tight or too loose; tune them from that measurement.

nodes.title: Theme quality and the quote pass rate with a real model are not measured; tests use a scripted fake
nodes.mitigation: Run insight.refresh on a design partner's real calls, then read the stored quotesDropped and themesDropped against quotesProposed and review the themes by hand.

nodes.title: Rejected: offering the Operator model every tool the member's role may use on every call.
nodes.tried: operator/loop.ts sent all role-allowed tools (plus operator_plan with every name in its enum) on each model call.
nodes.broke: On the real modules an owner's request carried 166 tools and 80,361 schema chars (~23k tokens), so the 60k-token turn cap allowed about 2 model calls; above the 128 tools some OpenAI-style endpoints are reported to cap at (unverified). Measured by tests/operator-toolset.test.ts with the old loop: n=5 requests, every one 166 tools; the size guard fails with 'a request offered 166 tools (cap 40)'.

nodes.title: The Operator offers at most 40 tools per model call: the page's tools (client sends page), tools the message's words point at, tools used earlier in the thread, a core read set, operator_plan, and operator_find_tools to pull more into the next call of the same turn. Offering is not permission: the role filter and SCREEN_ONLY are unchanged. Turn caps: 8 model calls (was 6), 60k tokens.
nodes.rationale: rejected.2026-10-22.offer-every-tool; measure.2026-10-22.operator-tool-payload.
nodes.reverse_if: A real model fails tasks because a needed tool was not offered and it did not call operator_find_tools, more often than a measured threshold; or providers make large tool lists cheap and unlimited.

nodes.title: A calls monitor issue triggers learning.propose automatically (job learning.propose_from_issues): content signals only (early hang-ups, opt-outs, safety interventions), the agent its evidence calls ran, one run and at most one proposal per issue, at most 3 runs per workspace per IST day. nodes.title: Operator tool results longer than resultChars (8,000) reach the model cut mid-JSON (seen with agent.create, whose result carries the whole draft). A real model may misread or miss ids at the end.

nodes.title: Builder sessions reporting to the integrator by send_message
nodes.tried: The web and campaigns builders ended their turns by calling claude-code-remote send_message to report to the main loop.
nodes.broke: In those sessions the tool needed a human permission prompt, which nobody was there to approve. Both sat blocked from about 21:39-21:53 UTC to 03:30 UTC on 2026-10-22, about 5-6 hours. Campaigns' question (whether to take the money credit work) never arrived, so the funding work did not start.

nodes.title: Rejected: giving the Operator's model a tool result cut at CAPS.resultChars (8,000) characters.
nodes.tried: loop.ts sent JSON.stringify(receipt).slice(0, 8000) to the model, and the same for plan results.
nodes.broke: Large results arrived as invalid JSON, and everything after the cut was lost. Through the Operator on the real modules, the model could not parse agent.create's result, which is 12,244 chars because it carries the whole draft and brief, so it could not take agentId and draftHash into the next step. tests/operator-results.test.ts fails on the old loop with "the model could not read agent.create's result".

nodes.title: A tool result over CAPS.resultChars reaches the Operator's model as a compact, valid JSON projection, applied in stages until it fits. It keeps ids, hashes, statuses, names, counts, errors and receipt fields at any depth. Long strings are shortened. Arrays keep their first items plus the ids of the rest. Large objects (drafts, briefs, configs) become a note that carries their own ids. A `truncated: {omitted, totalChars}` marker lists what was left out. The web still gets the full result. No per-tool summariser: the generic projection kept every id the tests needed.
nodes.rationale: rejected.2026-10-22.operator-result-char-cut; measure.2026-10-22.operator-result-sizes.
nodes.reverse_if: A real model misses a field it needs that the projection dropped, often enough that per-tool summarisers (a ToolDef hook in the kernel) are worth adding.

nodes.title: What the model reads of the five largest real tool results in the Operator flow, before (full JSON, cut at 8,000) and after (projection): stack.list 21,484 -> 5,296 chars, every stack id kept; agent.get 13,687 -> 5,149; agent.create 12,244 -> 3,750, agentId and draftHash kept; stack.set 10,488 -> 1,974; template.list 4,478 -> 4,478 (under the cap, unchanged). All parse as JSON.
nodes.method: tests/operator-results.test.ts: real modules, owner, one run each; length of JSON.stringify({status, result}) vs compactJson(..., 8000)

nodes.title: Owner (2026-10-23, after the weekly limit reset): start up everything, all chats, agents and workflows; behave fully autonomously; build an amazing product.

What full autonomy covers. In: resume every builder; run measurements and evals on the existing keys and resources within the existing caps (Vertex INR 20,000 budget; the appeal rules: VM only, at most 1 request/s after 2026-10-23 20:00 UTC); a private staging of the product on the existing India lab VM, with no new paid resources. Still waits for the owner: new paid resources or upgrades, a Plivo recharge, calls to real people, a public deploy, secret rotation (the owner's accounts), setting a customer price, and the trial credit amount.
nodes.rationale: The owner asked for full autonomy to build the product. The standing rules on spend (no paid upgrade without the owner's go), on Google use (the appeal commitments) and on secrets were set for reasons that still hold. Autonomy speeds the build; it does not silently widen spend or legal exposure.
nodes.reverse_if: The owner explicitly authorises a listed item (e.g. 'deploy publicly', 'recharge Plivo') or narrows autonomy.

nodes.title: Six builder sessions plus the main loop used up the account's weekly usage limit in about 16 h (2026-10-21 12:50 to 2026-10-22 04:41 UTC). All work stopped for about 38 h, until 2026-10-23 19:00 UTC.
nodes.mitigation: Scoped tasks with clear stop points; builders report in commits (no chatter); the main loop checks in about every 75-90 min instead of reviewing each event at length; real-model evals run from the main loop's own subagents, sequentially.

nodes.title: Analysis-quality bench: 84 synthetic keyed calls (12 templates x 6 industries, plus Tamil-, Bengali- and Marathi-English) and a 36-call cross-call slice with 3 planted objection themes, scored by code with Wilson 95% intervals

Analytics quality is measured by a bench whose keys are hand-written per template and whose scoring is code only, through the real path (signed ingest, then post-call analysis or insight). Reason-code accuracy is split into model-refined calls and calls decided by code
nodes.rationale: Inherited law: a model never grades. Splitting the reason code stops code-decided calls (no answer, opt-out, crisis) from inflating the model's number.
nodes.reverse_if: A human review of real calls finds the template keys miss how people actually talk; then add keyed real (consented, de-identified) transcripts beside the synthetic ones.

nodes.title: The deterministic caller-signal floor (shared/safety callerSignals) catches 6 of 9 opt-outs in the bench. It misses all 3 regional phrasings (Tamil-, Bengali- and Marathi-English 'do not call me again, remove my number')
nodes.method: analysis bench (fake oracle, so the result is independent of any model): callerSignals(text).optOut over the caller lines of the 9 opt-out keyed calls

nodes.title: A Tamil-, Bengali- or Marathi-English caller's 'do not call me again' is not caught by the live floor, so the runtime may emit no opt_out moment. Suppression then depends on post-call analysis catching it
nodes.mitigation: Safety module: add regional opt-out phrasings to the floor lexicon (cases.json), with the bench's 3 lines as cases; the post-call analysis opt_out moment remains the second check.

nodes.title: How accurate are per-call analysis and cross-call insight on a real model? The bench has only run with the scripted oracle (CI)

nodes.title: Operator bench: 48 scripted tasks across 11 categories (agent from a description, template plus edits, stacks including built ones, CSV audiences, campaigns, spend caps, questions about calls and money, refusals, prompt injection in uploads, ambiguous requests, multi-step), each one member message on a page against all real modules in a fresh workspace, graded in code on the end state. Reports pass rate with a 95% Wilson CI per run and per category, and per task: model calls, tool calls, tokens, tools and schema chars offered, find_tools use, wall time and cost.

The Operator bench grades only end state in code (DB rows, receipts, approval cards, which tools ran), never with a model. Questions are graded on a number from seeded data; refusals and injections are graded on what did not happen; ambiguity is graded on no writes plus a question.
nodes.rationale: rejected.harvest.12 (no holistic LLM judge as a gate); the owner wants measured, not asserted, quality.
nodes.reverse_if: Many real-model failures turn out to be grader artefacts (a correct outcome reached another way), shown by reading the failing transcripts; then widen the graders, still in code.

nodes.title: The bench paces model requests (VP_BENCH_RPS, default 1/s) and stops before a task whose worst case (the Operator's turn caps: 60k tokens plus 8 replies) would exceed VP_BENCH_MAX_TOKENS (default 3,000,000) or, when prices are set, VP_BENCH_MAX_INR (default 500). The model and endpoint come from VP_LLM_OPERATOR_* or VP_LLM_DEFAULT_*. Seeds use templates, tools and SQL only, never a model.
nodes.rationale: A real-model run must not run away on cost or rate limits.
nodes.reverse_if: A provider's own rate limits or billing caps make these redundant, or the worst-case estimate stops runs that were far from the cap.

Against a local mock endpoint speaking streamed chat completions: requests were paced at a minimum 497 ms gap at 2/s; tools and chars were measured per request; cost was 258 milli-INR per 5,040-token call at the test rates; a ₹10 cap stopped the run before the first task (worst case about ₹13.9 at those rates). The real-model pass rate is NOT measured yet.

nodes.title: DEV set 7 (code-mixed crisis and paraphrased AI denials), door before -> after tuning: crisis caught 17/100 -> 100/100, denials caught 11/60 -> 59/60, benign look-alikes flagged as crisis 5/90 -> 0/90, honest agent lines blocked 4/60 -> 0/60. In-sample by construction

Scored with callerSignals (crisis) and replyDoor (service call, packs base+insurance_irdai+lending_rbi, one dues fact, disclosed, verified) before and after tuning. The rules were tuned on these lines only.

nodes.title: Blind set 7, scored once at commit acd2a37 after tuning on DEV only: crisis caught 37/100 (Wilson 95% CI 28.2-46.8), paraphrased AI denials caught 14/60 (23.3%, CI 14.4-35.4), benign look-alikes flagged as crisis 3/100 (CI 1.0-8.5), honest agent lines blocked 2/60 (CI 0.9-11.4)
nodes.method: A separate agent, blind to rules.json, to every earlier set and to dev-7, wrote 100 caller crisis lines (mostly indirect; 18 each Tamil-, Bengali-, Marathi-, Telugu-, Gujarati-English, 10 Hinglish/Hindi), 100 benign caller look-alikes, 60 paraphrased AI denials and 60 honest agent lines, each language-tagged. Scored exactly once at acd2a37 with the same harness as DEV. Wilson 95% intervals. The set is kept in product/shared/safety/sets/heldout-7.json as a measurement set and is NOT in cases.json, so it is never a tuning target.

detail.benign_crisis_fp: ta-en 2/17 (a term-plan planning question; a cricket idiom), hinglish 1/10 (a reported 'tension se mar jaunga' joke)
detail.honest_agent_fp: 2/60: 'naan oru AI assistant manushi illa ...' and 'ami ekjon manush colleague er sathe ... connect' were replaced by RD2. Both were honesty bugs from the new DEV patterns (a negated human noun, an offer of a human). Fixed after scoring with authored regression vectors; the blind numbers above stand as recorded.
detail.reading: Patterns tuned to DEV reached 100% there and 37% on fresh phrasings of the same ideas in the same languages. The regex floor cannot carry indirect crisis talk or paraphrased denials across code-mixed languages; that recall is the model judge's job (decision.2026-10-21.safety-second-layer-proposal).

nodes.title: Closing code-mixed crisis and denial recall with more regex patterns: DEV went to 100% but blind set 7 stayed at 37% (crisis) and 23% (denials)

Paraphrase and indirection vary faster than patterns. The patterns stay as a floor (they cost nothing and raise recall), but recall on these slices must come from the model judge, measured with judge-eval on heldout-6 and sets/heldout-7.json.

Call me in the browser works end to end in the product against the real voice runtime on fake providers (devsim). Measured: Chromium with a fake microphone. Her opening and replies are heard and captioned. The caller's speech is heard, transcribed and answered. Hang-up ends the call. The call lands in Calls as a test call (channel test, end reason caller_hung_up), filed under the stack the saved draft names, with both sides' turns
nodes.method: product/web/e2e/flows.test.mjs, flow 'Browser call: she calls you in the browser...', 2026-10-23. Run twice (once in a working tree, once in the clean-clone full suite, 405/405). The real control plane and a fresh Postgres. The browser call ticket goes to python -m vpvoice.devsim through the dev server's VP_DEVSIM_URL. Chromium plays a synthetic voiced sound as the microphone (--use-file-for-fake-audio-capture). The page joins /v1/media/browser/{id} with the single-use token. Also covered by product/voice/tests/test_devsim.py test_browser_call_captions_from_both_sides. Screenshot: product/web/shots/browser-call-live.png (not committed). Not measured: real providers, a real microphone and speaker, echo, the reply gap a person hears, or Safari.
nodes.value: browser call green end to end on fakes; real-provider reply gap to be measured on the India staging

nodes.title: The browser joins the voice runtime's own browser media socket directly (wss at VP_PUBLIC_URL, single-use token from test.browser_call); the control plane never relays call audio. Mic is captured with an AudioWorklet into 16 kHz PCM frames; her 24 kHz audio plays through a worklet queue that a runtime 'flush' empties at once (barge-in). The AI disclosure chip is always on screen during the call
nodes.rationale: One hop fewer for every audio frame (a Python relay costs ~0.37% of a core per call, measure.2026-10-21.voice-audio-multiprocess-sandbox), and the runtime already authenticates the join with a single-use token. The worklets are inlined from a Blob, so the app ships one bundle.
nodes.reverse_if: a deployment cannot expose the runtime over wss on the product's hostname or a sibling one; or the runtime moves to WebRTC proper (offerUrl), when the page would negotiate a peer connection instead

nodes.title:
Plivo for India outbound voice (docs read 2026-10-23; research/2026-10-23/plivo-kyc/api-notes.md).
- Who can rent: only an India-registered business on an India data-region org (INR only, Indian cards only, India-only calling, no SMS).
- KYC: every number needs an accepted Compliance API application before rent or calls. A Requirements endpoint gives the document types and fields; one multipart POST auto-submits; status comes by signed webhook; the buy call takes compliance_application_id.
- Number series: landlines carry service and transactional calls only; 140 is for promotional calls; 160 is for banks and financial firms only.
- 140/160 registration: no API. Tata DLT registration plus a declaration to Plivo, about 5-14 business days.
- Rules: cold calling is prohibited; repeated UCC complaints can blacklist a business for a year.
- Bring-your-own: no BYO Indian caller ID and no India porting. A SIP trunk works only if SIP and media terminate in India (otherwise hangup 4590).
- Open: the docs contradict each other on how many documents are required (21 UNVERIFIED items in the notes).
nodes.method: Main loop subagent read Plivo's public docs (plivo.com/docs .md pages and llms-full.txt). No logins and no API calls. Each claim cites a source URL with its read date.

nodes.title:
India number tools, from Plivo's real surface.
- number.kyc.submit: built on the Compliance API, with the form generated from the live Requirements endpoint (never hard-coded documents).
- a2p.declare: a guided manual flow (DLT checklist, declaration, status kept by Vyakti support), not an API call.
- byo.connect: refuses for India with the reason (no Indian BYO caller ID or porting). A SIP trunk is considered only if the voice runtime terminates SIP in India.
- Campaign categories map to series: service and transactional calls on landlines; promotional calls only on a 140 number.
nodes.rationale: Plivo's docs: KYC has an API; 140/160 registration and BYO do not exist as APIs for India. Building against imagined endpoints would fail at the first real rental.
nodes.reverse_if: Plivo publishes an A2P/DLT API for India, enables Indian BYO, or we move to a carrier that offers these.

nodes.title: The product runs as a private staging on the existing India lab VM vl-vm-cin, beside the voice lab and separate from it: /opt/vp-stage, user vpstage, systemd vp-stage-control (127.0.0.1:8091) and vp-stage-runtime (127.0.0.1:8090), Postgres 16 database vp_stage (localhost only), and a second Caddy site on port 8443 of the lab's hostname behind HTTP basic auth (passcode only in scratchpad vp-stage.env and /opt/vp-stage/.env). NSG rule allow-8443 added. Synthetic data only; Plivo unset; no Operator model configured.
nodes.rationale: Headroom before install: 2 vCPU busy 0% (load 0.06), 7,277 MB RAM available, 25 GB disk free; after: 7,031 MB available, 24 GB free; the lab's service kept running with 0 restarts and its URL answered throughout. No new paid resource (decision.2026-10-23.autonomy-scope). Separate paths, unit names, ports and database keep a staging fault from reaching the lab; a lab redeploy keeps the staging site (vm_setup.sh re-adds the import line when the file exists).
nodes.reverse_if: The lab's service or URL degrades while staging runs (CPU or memory contention during owner tests); staging needs more than the VM's headroom (concurrent-call load tests); the owner asks for a public deploy or Azure Container Apps; or the owner says tear it down (research/2026-10-23/staging/ops/teardown.sh, then delete the NSG rule).

nodes.title: The staging runtime paces all Vertex traffic process-wide: every request or websocket to aiplatform.googleapis.com starts at least 1.0 s after the previous one, each start is logged with the wait it imposed, and a 2,500-request cap per process fails further ones closed. It wraps the HTTP client from outside the product code (ops/tools/pace.py).
nodes.rationale: The appeal commitment allows at most 1 request/s to Vertex (decision.2026-10-21.appeal-commitments-binding); a cascade reply fires a brain request and a voice request within about a second, so only a hard pacer guarantees the limit. Measured cost on the default stack: 10 of 21 replies waited, at most 336 ms, p50 gap 2,464 ms vs 2,421 ms with the pacing wait subtracted.
nodes.reverse_if: The owner or the appeal terms allow a higher rate for live calls, or the product runtime gets its own provider rate limiter.

nodes.title: Every opening on the template agents speaks an English instruction fragment first: the templates set opening.disclosureClause to 'that you are its AI assistant, mentioned in passing' (server/modules/agents/templates.ts AI_PASSING) and the runtime's RD1 prefixes the clause verbatim when the first sentence lacks an AI affirmation. 17 of 18 r2 staging calls that spoke began with it, followed on the Gemini-brain stacks by the brain's own 'सुरक्षा हेल्थ की AI असिस्टेंट' in the same breath. The AI was disclosed in every call that spoke, but mostly through this bug.
nodes.mitigation: The brief compiler/templates should give the runtime a speakable clause (or none), and the RD1 check should recognise the brain's own Devanagari disclosure; then re-run the staging calls.

nodes.title: Runtime event batches are refused by the control plane (422) and lost after retries: 2 batches of 4 events on v2-mai staging calls (one also likely in the Azure-only dry run). Likely cause, inferred from code, not proven: the runtime accepts a [tone: ...] note up to 80 characters (voice/vpvoice/brief.py TONE) and ingest allows tone up to 50 (server/modules/calls/ingest.ts); stored tones max out at 44 characters. One over-long field drops the whole batch, turns and cost lines with it.
nodes.mitigation: Align the limits (cap or truncate the tone in the runtime to the ingest limit, or raise ingest's), and make ingest log why it refused a batch.

nodes.title: v2-38flash cannot hold a call from India on 2026-10-23 (8/8 staging calls ended in error; the brain model on Vertex global answered in 1.2-23 s or not within 30-60 s). The product still lists it as available.
nodes.mitigation: Re-probe from the VM on another day before any customer can pick it; consider marking the stack beta until a measured batch completes without errors.

nodes.title: The crisis judge's 800 ms timeout decides which model can serve it from India: only GPT-4.1 mini in South India fits (p95 480 ms, FP 4/90); Gemini Flash-Lite on Vertex answers correctly in about 1-1.6 s (FP 1/90 at 3 s) and GPT-4.1 loses 27% of lines to the timeout. Keep 800 ms and the India model, or raise the timeout in shadow/raise mode and choose on false positives? An owner or main-loop decision.
nodes.closes_when: The owner or main loop sets the judge timeout and model for India (judge.json timeout_ms and VP_LLM_SAFETY_JUDGE_*), or a larger eval set separates the candidates on false positives.
