nodes.title: Safety judge candidate: GPT-4.1 mini on the regional South India deployment, the only model measured inside the 800 ms judge budget (recall 29/30, FP 4/90, p95 480 ms, INR 21.6 per 1k turns). It stays in shadow mode.
nodes.rationale: FP 4/90 (4.4%) per benign caller turn would add a crisis line to roughly a third of ordinary 10-turn calls. On held-out set 6 the floor already catches 30/30, so the judge's added recall is not measured there. The set that matters is BLIND 7, where the floor catches 37/100.
nodes.reverse_if: On BLIND 7 the judge lifts crisis recall well above the floor's 37/100, with FP at or below 1% on benign turns (n large enough that the upper CI bound is at or below 2%), and the owner approves raise mode.

nodes.title: Opt-out DEV set (code-mixed), door before -> after tuning: opt-outs caught 59/150 -> 150/150, benign look-alikes flagged 10/110 -> 0/110. In-sample by construction
nodes.method: A separate agent, blind to rules.json and every other set, wrote 150 opt-out requests (16 each Tamil-, Telugu-, Bengali-, Marathi-, Gujarati-, Kannada-, Malayalam-English; 20 Hinglish, 6 Hindi, 12 English; direct and indirect, polite and angry, some buried in long utterances) and 110 hard look-alikes (deferrals, 'don't cut the call', 'call my other number', 'don't call my wife's number, call mine', DND questions). Scored with callerSignals(text).optOut before and after tuning; the rules were tuned on these lines only.

before.benign_flagged: 10/110 (8 were 'DND is on my phone, how did you call?' questions)

nodes.title: Opt-out BLIND set, scored once at commit 87ebb00 after tuning on DEV only: opt-outs caught 92/160 (57.5%, Wilson 95% CI 49.8-64.9); benign look-alikes flagged 9/140 (6.4%, CI 3.4-11.8)
nodes.method: A separate agent, blind to rules.json, every earlier set and optout-dev, wrote 160 opt-out requests (18 each Tamil-, Telugu-, Bengali-, Marathi-, Gujarati-, Kannada-, Malayalam-English; 20 Hinglish, 6 Hindi, 8 English; direct, indirect, polite, angry, sarcastic, buried) and 140 hard look-alikes. Scored exactly once with callerSignals(text).optOut at 87ebb00. Wilson 95% intervals. Kept in product/shared/safety/sets/heldout-optout.json, out of cases.json, so it is never tuned on.

detail.missed_classes: conditional threats ('if you call again I will complain to TRAI / consumer court / police', 'last warning'); 'no call should come from your company'; polite negative imperatives on verbs DEV did not use ('phone panna vendaam', 'kaluhisabedi', 'call cheyyalle'); sarcasm ('wow, so dedicated, now remove my number'); requests buried in long rambles
detail.benign_flagged: 8 of 9 are one redirect class absent from DEV ('don't call my father, he is unwell, call me instead', in every language); 1 is 'what is DND and does it stop your calls'. Logged, not tuned (the set is spent).
detail.reading: As with crisis talk (blind set 7), DEV-tuned patterns reach 100% on DEV and about 58% on fresh phrasings. Opt-out is a hard legal line (TCCCPR), so a missed opt-out means calling someone who said stop.

nodes.title: Should opt-out get the same raise-only model judge as crisis (judge.json judges.caller_opt_out, default shadow), given that the regex floor reaches 57.5% on fresh code-mixed phrasings and a miss is a TCCCPR breach?
nodes.closes_when: The owner decides; if yes, a judge measured with judge-eval on sets/heldout-optout.json plus a fresh blind set reaches >= 97% opt-out recall at <= 3% look-alike false positives within the turn budget. Until then, post-call analysis (which reads opt_out moments from the transcript) is the second net.

nodes.title: End-to-end opt-out test across processes and modules: voice runtime (devsim) -> signed hook -> calls ingest -> intake contact.suppress_after_opt_out. It proves the agent confirms, the call ends with end_reason opt_out, call_opt_out is applied, a workspace in_call suppression and a consent withdrawal exist, and that the same check FAILS when the suppression tool is missing (the opt-out stays pending)

Product runtime turn-taking, held-out TEST split, before the fix: she cut in during a caller's mid-thought pause on 32.7% of turns (18/55, 95% CI 0.22-0.46) and talked over the caller on 25.5% (14/55, 0.16-0.38). End of turn to her first audio: median 1000 ms, including 450 ms of fixed fake provider time. Barge-in: 2/55 missed, she yields in a median 725 ms. Backchannel and noise false barge-ins: 0/55 each
nodes.method:
product/voice/bench/turn_bench.py --split test --set STATEMENT_HOLD_MS=0, 2026-10-23, Python 3.13, Silero VAD, in real time.
- Clips: 102 synthetic Hinglish caller clips (research/2026-10-17/lanes/l8-azure-bench/stimuli, phone band, with their text), split DEV/TEST by a hash of the clip id (47 DEV / 55 TEST).
- Labels: speech regions from each clip's energy envelope (-38 dBFS, gaps under 150 ms bridged); internal pauses of 250 ms or more count as mid-thought pauses.
- Runtime: the real cascade turn logic (VAD, held and withdrawn replies, barge-in).
- Fakes, fixed timing: the final arrives 250 ms after the VAD's end of speech, with words snapped to punctuation at pauses; brain 300 ms; voice 150 ms to first audio; no echo.
- Scenarios: turn (a whole clip, which always ends in a question); statement (the clip cut after its last full stop, 50 turns); barge (the caller starts 2 s into her long opening); backchannel (a 300 ms vocal burst, and separately a 300 ms burst of noise at -30 dBFS).
- CIs: Wilson for proportions, bootstrap for medians.
- Not measured: real ASR finals, real providers, echo, real callers, telephone jitter.
nodes.value: premature cut-in 32.7% of turns, talk-over 25.5% (TEST, n=55)

nodes.title: A 1200 ms hold after a caller's statement (chosen on DEV) cuts premature cut-ins on held-out TEST from 32.7% to 3.6% of turns (2/55, 95% CI 0.01-0.12) and talk-over from 25.5% to 3.6%. The cost: turns that end in a statement get her first audio at a median 1314 ms instead of 986 ms (+328 ms, n=49/41). Question-ended turns are unchanged (998 ms). Barge-in, backchannel and noise handling are unchanged
nodes.method:
Same bench, --split test, defaults after the change (STATEMENT_HOLD_MS=1200), 2026-10-23.
- DEV sweep over 0/600/1000/1200/1400 (bench/results/turn-2026-10-23-dev-sweep.md): premature cut-ins 40% / 38% / 19% / 2% / 2%; statement latency 977 / 979 / 1116 / 1308 / 1493 ms. 1200 was chosen on DEV and is reported on TEST only.
- Cause, traced on a DEV clip: the hold is counted from the end of the caller's speech, but the transcript lands about 410 ms later, so a 0 ms hold after a sentence that reads complete releases her reply inside 0.3-1.4 s mid-thought pauses.
- The speculative reply is generated while she waits, so with real providers (slower than the fakes) more of the hold hides behind generation. Not measured.
- Caveat: the stimuli end every whole turn in a question, so the question fast path (HOLD_MS=0) is favoured by this set; the statement scenario exists to show the cost.
nodes.value: premature cut-in 3.6%, talk-over 3.6% (TEST, n=55); +328 ms after statements

nodes.title: The cascade's held reply waits by how the caller's words end: no hold after a question (it hands her the turn); 1200 ms of silence after a statement; 1400 ms after an unfinished turn (a trailing comma or connective)
nodes.rationale: measure.2026-10-23.turn-taking-statement-hold: cut-ins and talk-over fall from about 1 in 3 turns to about 1 in 28 on held-out clips, at +328 ms only after statements.
nodes.reverse_if: on real calls (the India VM bench with real ASR, or live test calls) the statement wait is felt as slow, or cut-ins stay low with a shorter hold because real ASR finals arrive at a different time; or a semantic end-of-turn model beats punctuation

nodes.title: She yields to a caller who talks over her in a median 725 ms (TEST, n=55, 95% CI 708-739), and missed 2/55 barge-ins within 1.5 s. People yield in about 200-400 ms. Lowering BARGE_MS / BARGE_LONG_MS speeds this up but risks false barge-ins on backchannels and noise (0/55 each today). Next lever to bench on DEV
nodes.closes_when: a DEV-tuned barge-in rule lowers the yield time on TEST without raising false barge-ins, or the real-provider bench shows 725 ms is not felt

nodes.title: The product runtime's ears for the curated cascade stacks (v2-flashlite, v2-54mini, v2-38flash, v2-mai, v2-luna) are Azure Speech real-time STT (hi-IN, Central India, LAB_SPEECH_KEY/REGION) through the VAD gate, ported from the lab's measured AzureSTT via the Speech SDK (azure-cognitiveservices-speech 1.52.0). Gemini ears stay in the catalog, unavailable with "Gemini listening isn't offered on Google Cloud"; never rerouted
nodes.rationale: decision.2026-10-22.ears-azure-not-gemini: Vertex has no Gemini transcription model (measure.2026-10-22.vertex-availability-probe). The SDK path is what the lab runs and measured; a hand-rolled websocket protocol would be new, unmeasured code on the hottest path.
nodes.reverse_if: Vertex offers a Gemini transcription model and it beats Azure on Hinglish accuracy or latency in the lab; or the Speech SDK cannot run in the deploy image (then the REST/websocket protocol or Sarvam ears)

nodes.title: The product runtime does not offer gpt-oss-120b@groq: gpt-oss-120b runs on our Azure Foundry (routing Vertex > Foundry > OpenRouter). The cost is first-token latency: Groq 0.48 s against Azure 1.47 s (n=6, India VM, 2026-10-19, tests/brain_bench.py)
nodes.rationale: directive.2026-10-22.provider-routing: OpenRouter only for what is in neither Vertex nor our Foundry.
nodes.reverse_if: the owner judges the extra ~1 s of first-token latency worth an OpenRouter route for gpt-oss-120b

nodes.title: The voice runtime runs the parts a ticket names (stack.components). A curated id must carry exactly the parts of the runtime's own table, else 422 stack_mismatch. 'custom' is built from catalog parts: a cascade needs ears, brain and voice; an engine stack has s2s only. Unknown parts, incomplete sets and parts that differ from agent.voice.components are refused. Missing credentials are named per part (503 stack_unavailable with missing), and so are parts Vertex does not serve. combination_id uses the same algorithm over the parts, so a built copy of a curated stack files under the same combination
nodes.rationale: directive.2026-10-22.full-stack-selection: users pick every component, with a default stack. Never substituting a part, and filing under what actually ran, keep test integrity.
nodes.reverse_if: built stacks need settings beyond parts and the gate (e.g. per-part regions or speeds); then the ticket carries them and the combination id must include them

nodes.title: shared/components.ts matches the voice runtime catalog on every listed part: id, part, route, requires, and voices as a subset with the same default. All 7 curated stacks are built from offered parts. Known difference: components.ts offers 6 of the catalog's 12 Sarvam voices

nodes.title: The analysis contract is written as shapes: the model may name CONV_* codes only, null outcome only when no PERSON line bears on the question, every agreeing PERSON line is a commitment, and the outcome carries a confidence
nodes.rationale: The real-model bench showed three miss classes. Mini gave null outcomes on wrong-person, complaint and opt-out calls; found 7 of 21 commitments; and named END_HANDED_OFF, an engine code, on 2 complaint calls. The changes are class-level, from the template pattern of the misses, not tuned item by item. A mutation test proves the CONV_* guard is what stops an engine code.
nodes.reverse_if: The TEST split on a real model shows no gain over the old contract on outcome and commitment recall, or a loss elsewhere.

nodes.title: The analysis model is chosen per workspace from a curated list: single, or tiered (a cheaper first pass that escalates failed, outcome-less or low-confidence calls to a stronger model). No default model is chosen in code
nodes.rationale: Computed for a 3-minute call: mini about ₹0.073, GPT-4.1 about ₹0.38, against a ₹0.17 budget. Tiered costs ₹0.073 plus e x ₹0.38, so it stays under budget while the escalation rate e is below 26%. The bench's no-outcome rate for mini was 16.7%.
nodes.reverse_if: The TEST split shows tiered accuracy significantly below GPT-4.1-only, or a real-traffic escalation rate of 26% or more.

nodes.title: Analysis bench on real models (integrator's run, older contract): outcome 70/84 (mini) vs 84/84 (GPT-4.1); moment recall 57/72 vs 67/72; quotes grounded 230/230 and 277/277; cross-call themes 3/3 on both; ₹0.048 vs ₹0.263 per call
nodes.method: product/scripts/analysis-bench.ts at 1 request a second on Azure models; scored by code against hand-written keys

nodes.title: Every audited tool run records its subject as {type, id} only (from its input, or for a create from what its result made). activity.list resolves the name at read time inside the workspace, and a contact without a name shows as 'a contact', never a number
nodes.rationale: Closes open.2026-10-21.activity-row-subject (walkthrough S4). Storing ids, not names, keeps the hash-chained audit free of personal data and lets a renamed or deleted thing read correctly. A guard test makes every new *Id argument either a subject key or an explicitly internal id.
nodes.reverse_if: The activity ledger must show the name as it was at the time of the change (for example for a compliance export); then store a name snapshot beside the id, with redaction.

nodes.title: Tool schemas carry only portable regex patterns: no flags, no \p{…}, lookbehind, named groups or \u{…}. A non-portable pattern stays a server-side check and the schema describes it in words. tests/tool-schemas-portable.test.ts walks every registered tool.
nodes.rationale: rejected.2026-10-23.unicode-regex-in-tool-schemas.
nodes.reverse_if: Every provider the product supports accepts Unicode property classes in function schemas, verified by a request to each.

nodes.title: Every tool and plan result reaches the Operator's model with an outcome first (DONE / NOT DONE / WAITING FOR APPROVAL / UNKNOWN; plans say n of m steps ran plus a notDone list), the compactor always keeps it, and the conduct rules say NOT DONE means nothing changed.
nodes.rationale: On the 2026-10-23 bench a reply claimed an edit that had been refused; plan results began with status 'planned' even when every step was refused.
nodes.reverse_if: A real-model re-run shows false success claims persist at the same rate; then the cause is elsewhere (e.g. the model ignores tool results) and needs a code-level check on the reply.

nodes.title: agent.create from a description: the drafting prompt states field types (mirrorCaller true or false), and a draft that fails validation gets exactly one repair turn carrying the validator's message; a second failure is refused naming the field and the accepted form. Code never guesses a value.
nodes.rationale: Both gpt-4.1 and gpt-4.1-mini returned mirrorCaller as a language code; strict validation refused every draft (bench bug 2).
nodes.reverse_if: Repair turns rarely succeed in bench re-runs (cost without benefit), or a structured-output mode makes invalid drafts impossible.

nodes.title: The Operator bench counts a turn that ended in a model error as a fail and reports 'reached the model' separately (count and pass rate with CI); a clarifying request counts as asking with or without a question mark.
nodes.rationale: On 2026-10-23, 5 refusal and injection tasks per model scored PASS only because the provider refused the request and nothing changed; imperative clarifications were scored as no question.
nodes.reverse_if: Never for the model-error rule; widen the clarification detector if real replies show other phrasings.

nodes.title: The caller judge reads two labels in one call, crisis and opt_out (judge id caller_crisis kept for the runtime protocol). Opt-out is raise-only, threshold 0.6, never raised while a call is in crisis. A raise replaces the reply about to be spoken with rules.json texts.opt_out_confirm, emits the opt_out moment (calls then suppresses the contact) and ends the call with end reason opt_out
nodes.rationale: The opt-out floor reaches 57.5% on fresh code-mixed phrasings (measure.2026-10-23.optout-blind), and a missed opt-out is a TCCCPR breach. A second label on the call already made for crisis costs no extra latency. Using the floor's existing opt-out path keeps one suppression mechanism.
nodes.reverse_if: Shadow data or a blind eval shows the opt-out label's false positives above 3% on look-alikes (ending calls people did not ask to end), or the owner prefers post-call review for opt-outs; then keep the label in shadow or drop it.

nodes.title: The runtime protocol's 'judge' event and calls' call_judge_event table only know crisis (judge 'caller_crisis', kind direct|indirect). Opt-out shadow verdicts are therefore logged by the runtime but not recorded for analysis
nodes.closes_when: The kernel adds an opt-out record to RuntimeEvent 'judge' (e.g. label 'opt_out' with confidence) and calls stores it; then the runtime emits it for shadow and raise, and shadow opt-out precision can be read from live calls.

nodes.title: judge-eval scores both labels: --task crisis|opt_out|both (default crisis), cases.json rows by expectation, --set files by shape (sets/heldout-7.json crisis, sets/heldout-optout.json opt-out); per-task slices with Wilson CIs, floor/judge/combined recall and false positives

When her first sentence does not say she is an AI, the runtime's RD1 fallback prefixes a fixed, speakable line from shared/safety/disclosure.json, built from the brand's spoken name, in the call's language and her script. agent.opening.disclosureClause is guidance for the brief compiler and is never spoken. lexicon.ai_affirm recognises first-person disclosure in Roman, Devanagari, English, Tamil and Bengali, and refuses mentions ('about the assistant') and denials. Shared vectors keep the Python and TS sides in parity
nodes.rationale: Staging 2026-10-23: 17 of 18 openings read the template guidance 'that you are its AI assistant, mentioned in passing' aloud, because the fallback prefixed the clause verbatim and affirms_ai missed the brain's Devanagari disclosure.
nodes.reverse_if: agent configs start carrying a speakable, owner-approved disclosure sentence (then the fallback may use it, after a lint that it affirms); or a language is added that has no checked line (then add one rather than use the Hinglish fallback)

nodes.title: Confirmed: calls' validateRuntimeBatch refuses a whole event batch when one turn's tone exceeds 50 characters ('events[0].tone: must be at most 50 characters'), and the runtime accepted tone notes up to 80. This explains the 2 dropped v2-mai batches on staging. The runtime now trims every limited field to ingest's limits before sending
nodes.method: A batch of two turns, one with a 79-character tone, through product/server/modules/calls/ingest.ts validateRuntimeBatch, 2026-10-23. Regression: product/voice/tests/test_event_limits.py, which runs the runtime's real batches through the same validator when node and tsx are present.
nodes.value: one over-long field drops the whole batch; runtime trims to fit

nodes.title: Goal reached, defined once (calls/goal.ts): a call's best outcome (verified, then manager, then AI guess) is one of its own definition's goal values. The funnel and insight use that predicate, and the reason code follows it: CONV_GOAL_DONE exactly when the goal is reached, wherever the goal is knowable. Engine-decided codes are never rewritten
nodes.rationale: Closes open.2026-10-23.q-goal-key-vs-goal-semantics. Before, the model's CONV_GOAL_DONE could contradict the outcome (goal done on a 'not now' call), and a later verified payment did not move the reason. The funnel read the campaign's definition while insight read the outcome's. Grade travels beside the answer: the funnel shows goals by grade, and learning still requires a trusted grade (conversation.outcome).
nodes.reverse_if: The owner wants 'agenda completed' (the conversation went to plan) shown separately from 'goal reached' (the business result); then add a separate agenda-done signal instead of overloading the reason code.

Two mini passes disagree on 4/34 calls, so differences of 4 or fewer are noise; mini is never measurably worse and costs about 1/6.
nodes.reverse_if: After the outcome rule is rewritten on DEV and escalation skips engine-decided calls, two TEST passes per design show gpt-4.1 or tiered ahead of mini by more than 4/42 on outcome (or on moments/commitments), at a cost inside the Rs 0.17 per 3-minute-call analysis budget.

nodes.title: The crisis/opt-out judge moves to Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite on Vertex with a 1,500 ms verdict window, run non-blocking beside the reply; it stays SHADOW. A raise that arrives before the reply's first audio replaces the reply; a later one applies to the next turn
nodes.rationale: BLIND 7 (100 crisis / 100 look-alike benign caller lines): Flash-Lite floor-or-judge recall 99/100 (94.6-99.8) with FP 10/100, p50 961 ms, p95 1,126 ms, 0 unavailable; GPT-4.1 mini at the 800 ms contract: 87/100 with FP 23/100. Flash-Lite is better on both recall and false positives; only the 800 ms blocking contract excluded it, and a judge that runs beside the reply (brain TTFT plus first audio is 2.2-3.0 s on staging) does not need to block. The 50 requests/minute ceiling of the only mini deployment inside 800 ms is also avoided.
nodes.reverse_if: Flash-Lite's p95 on India staging exceeds the reply's first-audio time on more than 10% of turns, Vertex availability for the judge drops below 99% over a staging day, or a DEV-tuned GPT-4.1-mini (or another Azure model) matches its recall with fewer false positives inside the window.

nodes.title: Owner: switch the judge from shadow to raise mode, with a judge-only raise leading to a gentle check-in (she pauses the agenda and asks how the person is) rather than the full crisis script; the floor, or the caller's confirmation, still triggers the full crisis path. Inference: a check-in makes a false raise cheap (FP 10/100 on look-alike lines, 2/90 on ordinary benign lines) while lifting recall from 37/100 to 99/100
nodes.closes_when: The safety builder ships the check-in path behind config (default shadow) with tests; the prompt and threshold are tuned on DEV only; a fresh BLIND 8 is scored once; and the owner says raise or stay shadow.

nodes.title: A Vertex judge on every caller turn across concurrent calls would exceed the appeal commitment of at most 1 Vertex request per second from the VM; production traffic on Vertex needs that commitment lifted with Google first
nodes.mitigation: Shadow mode on staging only until the owner confirms the commitment's end; the runtime keeps a provider-agnostic judge spec so an Azure model can serve it if Vertex volume is not allowed.

nodes.title: The runtime 'judge' event carries the judge's opt-out verdicts as label 'opt_out' (raised or shadow, with a confidence; no kind, no reason), beside the crisis ones (label absent means crisis). One contract, product/shared/judge-event.json, is read by calls' ingest validator and by vpvoice/judge_event.py. calls stores the label (call_judge_event.label, migration 0605), counts it apart (analysis.opt_out_judge; crisis_judge now counts crisis rows only), and call.get returns plain-English judgeMarks that the call page shows. Shadow stays log-only: only the 'moment' opt_out of a raise suppresses
nodes.rationale: Closes open.2026-10-23.judge-event-opt-out-fields. Before, a shadow opt-out verdict was only a runtime log line, so the shadow trial could not be measured or shown. 'raised' means this verdict acted (the moment was sent). A raise-mode verdict that did not act (a crisis in progress, an opt-out already signalled) is sent as outcome 'shadow' with mode 'raise', so the page never claims an action that did not happen. An outage is reported once, as crisis, because one model call reads both labels. A post-call opt-out verdict is counted only, never acted on after the call.
nodes.reverse_if: The owner wants a post-call opt-out raise to suppress the contact (today only the live raise does), or the judge gains a label whose outage must be reported separately.

nodes.title: Fix for rejected.2026-10-23.upload-newlines-folded-by-redact: redact (TS and Python) now finds secrets on the folded text as before but writes its output from a same-length fold that keeps tab, CR, LF, VT, FF, U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029. A 3-row CSV uploaded through the Operator (scripted model copies the upload into source.upload, then source.commit) imports 3/3 rows; before the fix 0/3 (tests/operator-upload.test.ts, run before and after). Detection is unchanged: spans come from the same folded text.
nodes.n: 1 Operator e2e CSV (3 rows, CRLF and LF mixed) + 1 unit (TS) + 1 unit (Python); fresh-DB suite 456/456, voice unittest 225/225
nodes.method: node:test against a throwaway Postgres 16 with setFakeLlm; python -m unittest
nodes.not_verified: Not run against a real model on the VM (the csv-pune bench task should be re-run there). A secret split across lines is still found, because digit runs read the folded text (unchanged).

nodes.title: No outcome is recorded on a call whose reason is END_CRISIS, END_EARLY_HANGUP or CONV_LANGUAGE_MISMATCH, whatever the model guessed (calls/analysis.ts NO_DECISION; the guess shows as outcomeUnclear 'not recorded: ...'). The prompt's outcome rule is rewritten: decided only when the PERSON takes a stance; null when they could not follow the language, hung up before the question, or spoke of distress (distress is not a request for a human)
nodes.rationale: Answers rejected.2026-10-23.analysis-outcome-null-only-rule: every round-2 outcome miss on all three designs was a non-null outcome on these call types. The code guard makes them right regardless of model; the prompt rewrite keeps the commitment and complaint gains of 8a4a508 (those lines are unchanged). The prompt rewrite is NOT measured on a real model (no keys in the sandbox): it was written from the DEV templates only, TEST not consulted again.
nodes.reverse_if: A real deployment shows calls where the person decided before a crisis or a language switch and that decision is needed (then keep the guess for crisis calls as needs-review instead of dropping it).

nodes.title: Tiered analysis never escalates a call whose reason the engine decided (any code outside REFINABLE: END_CRISIS, END_OPTED_OUT, END_EARLY_HANGUP, END_HANDED_OFF, CONN_*, ...), including when the first pass failed; analysis.tier.why says so. END_HUNG_UP_MID and CONV_INCOMPLETE, which the engine leaves open, may still escalate
nodes.rationale: Answers rejected.2026-10-23.tiered-escalate-on-no-outcome: tiered escalated exactly the calls where no outcome is correct and turned 4 right answers wrong.
nodes.reverse_if: A failed first pass on engine-decided calls leaves too many calls unanalysed (then retry the same model instead of escalating).

nodes.title: The product default analysis setting is single, gpt-4.1-mini, when the deployment's curated list (VP_ANALYSIS_MODELS) has it; VP_ANALYSIS_DEFAULT_MODEL renames it; otherwise the deployment's VP_LLM_ANALYSIS_MODEL. A workspace that set tiered without a first model also starts on it
nodes.rationale: Implements decision.2026-10-23.analysis-default-mini-single.
nodes.reverse_if: That decision is reversed.

nodes.title: call.search: outcome must be one of the workspace's defined outcome values (the campaign's when campaignId is given); any other value is refused with the valid values listed, and a reason code passed as outcome is named as one ('pass it as reasonCode'). reasonCode is a separate enum filter. The result carries total, the count of every match regardless of page
nodes.rationale: Answers rejected.2026-10-23.call-search-free-text-outcome: both models passed a reason code as the outcome, got 0 rows and answered 'no calls'. The values differ per workspace, so they cannot be a static enum in the tool schema; the refusal carries them instead.
nodes.reverse_if: The operator's tool schemas become per-workspace; then put the values in the schema as an enum.

nodes.title: The Operator sends the model a short page note as untrusted data: the page, the named entity (by name, via the registry), and the only entity of a kind when the workspace has exactly one
nodes.rationale: The page only picked tools, so the model asked 'which campaign?' while the member was looking at one or when only one existed. Names are tenant data, so the note is a data block; reads use the Operator's own actor, so roles and tenancy hold.
nodes.reverse_if: The bench shows the note makes the model act on the wrong entity, or the extra reads cost more than they save (each turn adds at most 1 get plus up to 3 small list reads)

nodes.title: Every Operator NOT DONE with a field path carries a 'fix' read from the tool's schema; either-or arguments are stated in tool descriptions and enums, not JSON Schema oneOf
nodes.rationale: Models invented template ids and guessed brief fields after bare refusals (bench r2). oneOf is not accepted by every target endpoint, so the either-or rule goes in the description and run() refusals name both fields and the next step.
nodes.reverse_if: Every target endpoint is shown to accept oneOf/anyOf in tool parameters, in which case declare it in the schema

nodes.title: A provider content-filter refusal is its own Operator outcome (provider_refused): said plainly, never retried, no attempt to get past the filter
nodes.rationale: Azure returned 400 content_filter on 2 of 3 injection tasks; it surfaced as 'the brain did not answer', which reads like an outage.
nodes.reverse_if: A provider offers a documented, permitted way to mark untrusted data so its filter does not refuse the whole request

nodes.title: She addresses the person only by the contact's name. The brief gives it in Roman and Devanagari (vpvoice/names.py), and every sentence is checked before the door: a name she uses (before ji/जी, in 'kya main X se baat', after a greeting) that matches no word of the contact's name, her persona or the brand is repaired to the contact's first name in the sentence's script, or dropped when there is no name. Logged as safety RD11 'replaced', without names. String matching on a script-neutral skeleton, no model call. Identity now recognises a Devanagari question that named the person
nodes.rationale: Staging redeploy 2026-10-23 (integrator, research/2026-10-23/staging/redeploy-e95ebc2.md): 1 of 6 openings asked for 'अक्षरा जी' when the contact was Asha. A 'haan' to that question would have verified the wrong person under RD11. Separately, identity compared the Roman first name as a substring, so a Devanagari question never verified.
nodes.reverse_if: the guard repairs a correct name on real calls (a nickname, a name the rules transliterate badly): then widen the match or carry a contact-supplied Devanagari name in the ticket; or ingest gains a dedicated quality event type, then move the log off RD11

nodes.title: Reply-gap cuts on the cascade, each behind a flag: VP_SPECULATE_PARTIAL (default on: the reply starts on the caller's partial at end of speech; kept only if the final has the same words, else discarded unheard; never on digits/secrets, ACTION signals or a raising judge), VP_PREWARM (on: Vertex token refresh plus one HEAD per brain/voice host when the caller starts speaking, at most one per host per 8 s), VP_FIRST_CLAUSE (off: voices the first clause at a comma after 24+ characters, never on the opening), VP_BARGE_NOD (on: nods do not count toward BARGE_WORDS; speech heard only as nods stops her after 1500 ms). No acknowledgement filler: the turn bench has no case where one would be honest content
nodes.rationale: Staging 2026-10-23 breakdown: the brain request started ~600 ms after end of speech (waiting for the final), and the voice request started ~1.7 s after it. Per-stage timing is now in each call's status ('timing') so staging can show which stage each flag moves.
nodes.reverse_if: staging shows a discarded-speculation rate high enough that its extra brain/voice requests cost more than the gap gain, or the Vertex pacer puts the extra requests on the critical path; FIRST_CLAUSE stays off until a listening check shows the split does not hurt prosody

Barge-in latency median 733 vs 742 ms; missed barge-ins 0/47 vs 1/47. 300 ms 'haan' and noise 0/47 both

nodes.title: An experiment's readout counts only the contacts it assigned (experiment_assignment, one arm per contact, stored at first assignment), on their own arm's version since assignment. A contact seen on both versions is a crossover: counted in neither arm and reported.
nodes.rationale: rejected.2026-10-23.readout-all-calls-on-versions. Measured on the dev walk, n=1 run: the control arm held 752 contacts where 642 were assigned.
nodes.reverse_if: Never for one-arm-per-contact. Revisit counting only if a binding (e.g. inbound) cannot assign before the call; then it needs its own unit of randomisation.

nodes.title: A winning test is adopted only when its 100% rollout card is approved (the binding's latest deployment runs the treatment at 100%). Then the same edits go into the agent draft through brief.edit, the proposal becomes promoted, and an 'Adopted' lesson is written. A declined or expired card writes 'won but not adopted'. Nothing auto-publishes.
nodes.rationale: On the walk a win produced only a rollout card; the draft kept the old text, so the next published version silently dropped the learned change.
nodes.reverse_if: Agents gains first-class version branching where a published candidate can be promoted directly; then adoption should promote the version instead of re-applying edits.

nodes.title: A running test also stops when the goal rate is worse: an always-valid mSPRT (alpha 0.05) on 'did not reach the goal', with 30 or more outcomes per side. It reverts through the A3 verb, opens an issue and records a lesson, like the harm-code stop. The pre-registered design names this guardrail.
nodes.rationale: Before, only harm codes and safety violations stopped a test; a change that did worse on the goal ran to its horizon.
nodes.reverse_if: Shadow A/A runs show this stop firing on equal arms more often than alpha allows.

nodes.title: Before an approval is asked, proposal.readiness (and the proposal.accept card) plan the test without writing anything. They state the calls needed ('about N calls with a recorded outcome, M on each version, to prove X% -> Y%') or the first blocker in words with a fix kind (probe, wait, outcome, outcomes).
nodes.rationale: On the walk a person held to approve and only then saw 'no success values'; the 1,208 calls needed were shown only after approval.
nodes.reverse_if: Never: an approval card must say what it commits to.

nodes.title: Learning loop walked end to end on the dev server (fake model, synthetic data), n=1 run: 30 calls (14 early hang-ups) -> the monitor fired at 8/20 (40% > 35%) -> 1 proposal from the issue -> probe on 12 library pairs -> test approved (about 1,208 outcomes to prove 40% -> 48%) -> A/A passed at 110 contacts -> split 545/555, 0 contacts in both arms -> win +20.3 points (95% CI 15.1 to 25.4) -> rollout approved -> adopted into the draft -> version 3's brief carries the change.

nodes.title: RD1 decides on the whole opening turn: the runtime holds her first reply until a sentence affirms she is an AI (then it is said as written) or the reply ends without one (then the first sentence gets the fixed disclosure.json line). The opening is judged sentence by sentence and joined, with an ellipsis that ends a sentence read as a pause; a full stop, question or exclamation still ends the clause. Shared decision: TS disclosure.ts openingDiscloses / Python safety.opening_discloses, vectors disclosure.json opening_vectors (6 staging openings + 6 synthetic)
nodes.rationale: rejected.2026-10-23.rd1-first-sentence-window-double-disclosure: RD1 judged only the first sentence, so 3/6 staging calls disclosed twice. All 6 staging openings disclose within their first two sentences, so the hold costs one sentence of brain output in the common case.
nodes.reverse_if: Time to first audio on the opening rises noticeably on staging (the hold waits for the disclosing sentence, or for the whole opening when she never discloses); then cap the hold at two sentences.

nodes.title: Whole-opening RD1 on the 6 verbatim staging openings (prefix removed): 6/6 judged disclosed by both doors, so none would get the fixed line (before: 3/6 prefixed). Runtime (SimSession + FakeBrain): the 6 openings are said with no fixed line; a disclosure after a greeting is said once; an opening that never discloses still starts with the fixed line. These runtime tests fail on the previous code (2 failures + 2 errors) and pass after.

nodes.title: decision.2026-10-23.judge-flashlite-nonblocking implemented in the voice runtime: judge.json timeout_ms 800 -> 1,500, model_recommended (Flash-Lite, Vertex global), mode default stays shadow. The reply never waits for the judge: a verdict in before her first sentence leaves the door acts on that reply (crisis path or opt-out confirmation); a later one settles in the background and acts from her next sentence (crisis) or turn (opt-out). Sim: a 0.3 s judge in raise mode delays the reply < 0.2 s, and its crisis raise gives the lines on her next turn; a late opt-out raise confirms on her next turn and ends opt_out; a judge that is in first still replaces the reply.
nodes.n: 41 judge + runtime-fixture unit tests (2 new late-verdict tests); voice suite OK; fresh-DB 468/468
nodes.method: python -m unittest with FakeBrain first_token_s (brain time to first token) against a fake judge with a delay
nodes.not_verified: No real model in the runtime yet. Not measured: how often the verdict lands before her first sentence on staging (Flash-Lite p95 1,126 ms vs brain first sentence). The window ends when her first sentence leaves the door, not at first audio (TTS time to first byte later), so a verdict landing in that gap acts from her next sentence. Speculative replies stay off in raise mode (cascade.judge_raises, unchanged).

nodes.title: Judge-only crisis check-in, behind config and off by default (judge.json checkin, VP_SAFETY_JUDGE_CHECKIN, mode raise only). A crisis raised by the judge alone makes her pause the agenda and check in, in her own words, from rules.json checkin shapes (never lines). It is recorded as one RD3 flagged safety event, with no hand-off. If the verdict is in before she speaks, the reply is rewritten as the check-in; a later verdict makes her next reply the check-in. The floor at any time, or a crisis verdict from the judge on the caller's answer, takes the full crisis path (14416 and 112, goal suspended, human offered). A calm answer ends the round, and the agenda returns only if they invite it. Check-in off: a judge raise is the full path at once, as before.
nodes.rationale: Owner (open.2026-10-23.judge-raise-soft-checkin): a check-in makes a false judge raise cheap (Flash-Lite FP 10/100 on look-alikes in BLIND 7) while the judge lifts recall from 37/100 (floor) to 99/100. A crisis verdict on the answer, rather than parsing a yes, avoids reading 'haan' to 'are you okay?' backwards.
nodes.reverse_if: Shadow or staging data shows a judge-only raise that was a real crisis where the check-in delayed the lines harmfully, or the owner prefers the full path on every raise.

nodes.title: BLIND 8 crisis set (product/shared/safety/sets/heldout-8.json): 100 crisis and 100 look-alike benign caller lines, same language split as BLIND 7 (ta/bn/mr/te/gu-en 18/17 each, hinglish 6/10, hi-deva 4/5). Written by a separate agent with no repo access to the rules, prompt or earlier sets. The builder checked counts, duplicates (0), long digit runs (0) and overlap with earlier sets (0) by script, without reading a line. Not in cases.json. Integrator scores it once on the VM, after DEV tuning.
nodes.value: the one clean measurement of the tuned judge and the check-in threshold
nodes.caveat: The builder wrote the writer's brief, which named the benign look-alike families (exaggeration, debt anger, someone else's death, planning questions, film or news, quoting, a past feeling, medical talk, tiredness, idioms, anger at someone else). Prompt changes must therefore come from DEV false positives only, never from that list.

nodes.title:
Call recordings play from short-lived signed links to the voice runtime: GET /v1/recordings/{callId}?ws&exp&sig, sig = HMAC-SHA256(VP_RUNTIME_SECRET, 'vp-recording.v1
' + callId + '
' + workspaceId + '
' + exp). call.get returns recording {url, expiresAt, why}: a 10-minute link on VP_RUNTIME_PUBLIC_URL (else VP_RUNTIME_URL) when the call has a recording, it is inside the workspace's recordings retention (policy.retention.get recordings_days) and no erase_me request exists for the person. The runtime refuses expired links, links living over an hour, forged signatures and a workspace other than the one in the .json beside each .wav; call ids are UUID-validated, never joined raw; no listing; aiohttp FileResponse serves Range
nodes.rationale: Web's ee8aef6 found recordingUri is a file path on the voice server, so no real recording could play. A link tied to one workspace and ten minutes leaks little if copied; the browser's <audio> needs no CORS. There is no per-workspace recording switch to respect beyond the agent's own recording setting (the runtime records only when it is on and the caller did not refuse); retention is enforced at play time only, nothing deletes runtime files yet.
nodes.reverse_if: Recordings move to object storage (then sign storage URLs instead), or a per-workspace recording policy is added (then call.get must check it too).

nodes.title: Nothing deletes recording files on the voice runtime when recordings_days passes or a person asks to be erased: the control plane only stops signing links. A purge needs a signed runtime route (or storage lifecycle) driven by calls' retention and forget_request.
nodes.closes_when: A runtime purge route (or a storage lifecycle) deletes recording files past recordings_days and on an erase request, with a test that the file is gone and its link refused.

nodes.title: The outcome rule is a table of PERSON shapes mapped to the VALUE that names them: agrees -> agreeing; refuses -> refusing; not the person called -> wrong-person, never null; complains AND asks for a human -> needs-human, never null; asks never to be called again -> refusing, never call-later; asks to be called later -> call-later; null only for no shape, a language they cannot follow, a hang-up before the question, or distress. And tiered never escalates when the first pass names a NO_DECISION reason (CONV_LANGUAGE_MISMATCH)
nodes.rationale: Answers rejected.2026-10-23.analysis-stance-rule-mini-false-nulls (mini returned null on wrong-person and complaint-to-human calls and called an opt-out a callback) and rejected.2026-10-23.tiered-escalates-no-decision-model-codes (6 of 12 escalations were language-mismatch calls whose outcome code discards). Written from the DEV patterns the integrator reported; TEST not consulted. Not measured on a real model here.

nodes.title: A regex T-L1 cannot cover paraphrase: blind recall is 23/60 after the fix, as the caller-crisis floor's was 37/100. Proposal: a model check on brief text at save and publish (raise-only, like the caller judge: refuse when the model says the text tells her to pass as human or hide being an AI; the regex stays the floor). nodes.title: Stack voice samples are rendered by python -m vpvoice.samples through the runtime's own voice adapters (providers/tts.py make_voice; Gemini Live told to say the line verbatim for v2-live, with its own transcription kept as spokenText), the stack's default voice, neutral style. nodes.title: Estimate, not measured on calls: share of judge verdicts in before her first sentence = 49% on v2-flashlite and 58% on v2-mai with speculation and prewarm off, 38% on v2-54mini with the defaults. On the paced defaults it is 84% and 95%, only because her replies are slower there. Inference: on staging the judge's Vertex request would take the pacer slot before the brain's (cascade.py starts it first), costing Gemini-brain replies up to 1 s
nodes.method: For each of 119 measured replies (judge off), the slack from the final to her first sentence (runtime timing), against the empirical distribution of Flash-Lite judge latency from the VM (the two DEV runs, n=450 requests, p50 976 ms, 12 timeouts counted as never in). Expected share = mean over replies of P(latency <= slack). The planned on-call measurement (ops/judge_shadow.sh, probes k=judge vs k=reply) was blocked by the daily test budget.

nodes.title: The shipped latency defaults (VP_SPECULATE_PARTIAL and VP_PREWARM on) on a Vertex paced at 1 request per second
nodes.tried: Staging at e9fdde3 on the code defaults (d353282 / 1a67f1a), with every Vertex request held >= 1.0 s apart (appeal commitment), against a same-session arm with both flags off.
nodes.broke: Replies got slower, not faster: v2-flashlite p50 3,201 vs 2,301 ms, v2-mai 2,658 vs 2,054 ms (n=22-23 each). The pacer queues the confirmed brain request behind discarded speculative requests (24 and 28 waits per 4 calls, 12-15 s in all) and warm HEADs. Speculation kept its reply in only 2 of about 23 replies, and the defaults sent 1.5-2.0x the Vertex requests. Not a verdict on the flags without a pacer, which was not measured here.

nodes.title: Choosing the judge threshold as 'the lowest DEV sweep threshold with judge FP <= 5%' for a model whose confidences come in steps
nodes.tried: PREREG.md for BLIND 8: the lowest threshold on 0.3-0.9 with DEV judge FP <= 5%, else the fewest FP at recall >= 95%, else 0.5.
nodes.broke: Flash-Lite's DEV confidences are step-quantised (0.85, 0.95, 1.0). 6 of its 8 false positives and 24 true crisis verdicts sit at exactly 0.85, so the only qualifying value was 0.9 (DEV judge recall 88 -> 60/100). On BLIND 8 it gave judge recall 73/100, where the information-only sweep shows 93/100 at 0.5 with 1/100 FP. A next rule should choose by recall under an FP bound with a CI, or handle tied confidence steps explicitly. BLIND 8 is not re-scored.

nodes.title: On real test calls: how often the shadow judge's verdict lands before her first sentence, per stack, and what the judge costs the reply under staging's 1 request per second Vertex pacer (the judge's request starts just before the brain's)
nodes.closes_when: ops/judge_shadow.sh runs after 18:30 UTC (a fresh IST test budget, about 12 calls, about INR 33): at least 20 judged replies per stack, with the probes' k=judge against k=reply and the judge's pacer waits, plus the flags-off arm; and v2-54mini arm B topped up to >= 20 replies

nodes.title: Speculative brain calls and pre-warm run only where they measurably help: on for unpaced brains (Azure: v2-54mini 3.01 s -> 2.13 s p50), off when the brain's provider is paced (staging Vertex, where they made flashlite 2.30 -> 3.20 s and mai 2.05 -> 2.66 s); the call-start Vertex HEAD obeys VP_PREWARM
nodes.rationale: Same-session A/B on staging e9fdde3 (n=22-24 replies per arm): with a 1 req/s pacer the discarded speculative requests and warm HEADs queue ahead of the real brain request, and speculation kept its reply in only 2 of about 23 replies per stack while sending 1.5-2x the requests. On the unpaced Azure brain (54mini) the arm with the flags on had brain stage 886 ms vs 1,096 ms. The HEAD at call start ignores the flag and costs 837-998 ms on every paced flashlite opening.
nodes.reverse_if: An unpaced Vertex measurement (after the appeal commitment lifts) shows speculation saving at least 200 ms p50 with a keep rate of at least 50%, or the Azure gain does not hold at n>=20 per arm on a second run.

nodes.title: VP_BARGE_LONG_MS stays 700 ms: staging partial lag is 858 ms median (p25 722, p90 1,145, n=464), far above the ~300 ms at which the bench found 500 ms safe; faster barge-in has to come from the audio side (energy onset plus the nod classifier), not from waiting less for words
nodes.rationale: measure.2026-10-24.staging-partial-lag: 96% of partials arrive after 500 ms; the DEV bench showed 500 ms stops her on most nods at 500 ms lag.
nodes.reverse_if: Partial lag falls below 400 ms median on staging (a faster recogniser or streaming setting), or an energy-onset barge-in with the nod guard measures fewer than 1 in 20 false stops on nods.

nodes.title: Rejected: experiment.check waiting for the experiment row lock (FOR UPDATE) while it may call a sibling tool on a second pooled connection.
nodes.tried: experiment.check before 0e4e7da, run by calls after every connected call, so checks of one experiment overlap.
nodes.broke: Overlapping checks held the pool's other connections while they waited for the row lock, and the lock holder waited for a connection. The loop e2e hung for good on PG_POOL_MAX=3 and timed out once at 300 s on the default pool under load (pg_stat_activity: checks on a tuple lock behind one 'idle in transaction').

nodes.title: experiment.check takes its row with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. A check that finds it locked returns at once with a note, and the next call or the learning.check job looks again.
nodes.rationale: rejected.2026-10-24.check-waits-for-experiment-lock; measure.2026-10-24.check-deadlock.
nodes.reverse_if: Cross-module calls run on the caller's own connection (nested in its transaction); then waiting is safe again.

nodes.method: The loop e2e on pool sizes 2, 3, 5 and 10, and a stress of 6 concurrent copies plus the learning and safety suites, 3 rounds. The shadow A/A was simulated 400 times on the test's own data to rule it out.
nodes.title: Before the fix: the loop e2e hung on a pool of 3 and passed on 5. After: it passed on pools of 2, 3 and 10, and 15 of 15 stressed runs took 26-31 s (timeout 300 s). The shadow A/A failed 0 of 400 times on that data, so it was not the cause.

An agent version is 'published' or 'candidate' (agent_version.kind, migration 0204). 'The live version' is the newest published one (agent.get liveVersion). Readers never take 'the newest version'. campaign.draft and version.restore refuse a candidate, and version.candidate's parent must be published.
nodes.rationale: The web campaign and inbound forms used versions[0], so during a test a new campaign or line would have run the untested candidate for everyone. Measured: version.restore to a candidate published it as version 4. Also affected: learning's proposal base, memory, the calls test-call default, the publish parent and card, and version.diff.
nodes.reverse_if: Agents gains first-class branches, where a version's role is a pointer rather than a property of the row.

nodes.title: A probe where both versions pass none of the practice calls and nothing regressed reads 'inconclusive', with a note, never 'pass'. The proposal may still be tested on real calls.
nodes.rationale: On the dev walk, with no simulation model, both versions scored 0 of 12, and 'no regression' read as a pass.
nodes.reverse_if: Practice calls get a calibrated pass rate on the current version; then an inconclusive probe could block instead.

nodes.title: Adoption writes the adopted change onto the monitor issue that started it. A monitor closes its issue when the calls that ended after it opened (at least its minimum) are at or under 80% of its threshold. The resolution states the numbers and names an adopted change as 'observed together, not proof'.
nodes.rationale: The issue that started the loop stayed open with no link to the result. The first version, without hysteresis, closed the loop's issue at 34.8% against 35%, a rate that would reopen it on the next wobble.
nodes.reverse_if: Issues flap or close too late in real use; then tune RECOVER_AT per signal.

nodes.title: Rejected: learning's evidence reading moments from the 'moment' table.
nodes.tried: gatherEvidence before 686b491.
nodes.broke: Nothing writes that table; analysis writes call_moment. Learning never saw an objection, a question, a confusion or a commitment, and never saw insight themes.

nodes.title: Learning reads, from the live version's last 30 days: call_moment counts by kind, up to 4 caller lines per quotable kind (objection, question, confusion, callback request, commitment), reason codes, outcomes including none, and the agent's latest insight themes. A crisis call's words are never shown to the model; an opt-out is counted, never quoted.
nodes.rationale: rejected.2026-10-24.learning-reads-moment-table. These are the shapes the round-3 analysis bench produced (research/2026-10-23/benches-r3: 270 analyses, six moment kinds, twelve reason codes, 94 with no outcome).
nodes.reverse_if: Analysis changes what it stores; the fixtures in product/tests/fixtures/analysed-calls.ts must follow.

nodes.title: Every learning proposal is compiled through agents' brief.compile before it is drafted. Only a refusal the change causes counts: if the live version itself no longer compiles under today's rules, the gate records 'not checked' instead of blocking.
nodes.rationale: A learned note that reads as a line (first person, quotes, a greeting, Hindi, digits) passed every learning gate and was refused only when the candidate compiled, after a person had approved it.
nodes.reverse_if: The shape lint moves to shared/ and learning's own gates run it directly.

nodes.title: Rejected: learning's per-string gates judging every string a whole-list change contains.
nodes.tried: runGates before 686b491, on a change that sets 'objections' to the existing notes plus one.
nodes.broke: The insurance-renewal template's own note ('no defending, no discount talk') trips the reply door's promotion rule (RD7), so every objection proposal on that template was gated out by text nobody proposed. 1 of 6 template objection notes (16 templates) is affected.

nodes.title: A recurring objection theme (agent-scope insight, last 7 days, 3+ calls, 5%+ of the sample, 2+ verified quotes) that no existing note answers becomes one drafted objection note. The note is an English trigger + approach about behaviour, appended after the business's notes, which stay unchanged (gate objection_append_only). It never reuses a caller's words (gate copied_quote: any 4 consecutive words or the whole line). It runs once per theme per agent (learning_theme_run, migration 0804) within the daily cap of 3 model runs shared with issues. A trigger that already names it, or the model replying 'covered', records already_answered.
nodes.rationale: The integrator's task 2026-10-24. Caller words in a brief get recited back to the next caller (agents' lint law); a learned change must never rewrite what the business wrote.
nodes.reverse_if: Real use shows the thresholds draft too often or too rarely, measured as drafted notes per 100 insight runs and their approval rate.

nodes.title: Erasure and retention delete the audio on the voice runtime: job calls.recording_purge (every 10 minutes, advisory-locked) asks the runtime, by a signed POST /v1/recordings/{id}/purge naming the call and its workspace, to delete the .wav and its .json for calls whose person has an erase_me request (first, whatever the age) or whose recordings_days retention has passed since the call ended. The row (recording_uri cleared, recording_purged_at, recording_purge_reason retention|erased) is marked only after the runtime confirms; call.get says why the recording is gone
nodes.rationale: Resolves open.2026-10-24.recording-files-retention-purge (DPDP: erasure must reach the audio). The runtime refuses another workspace's recording (403) and a body naming another call (400); its purge is idempotent, so a run cut short between the delete and the row update is finished by the next run. A recording saved before its .json existed is deleted on a signed request (the safe direction).
nodes.reverse_if: Recordings move to object storage (then a storage lifecycle rule plus a delete on erasure replaces this route), or erasure must complete synchronously with the request (then call the purge from the erase path too).

nodes.title: Transcripts (conversation.transcript and turn rows) are not yet purged at transcripts_days nor on an erase_me request; only recordings are. Same shape as calls.recording_purge, inside the database.
nodes.closes_when: Transcripts and analysis text are deleted or redacted past the retention window and on an erase request, with a test that the rows are gone and the call page says why.

nodes.title: learning-loop-e2e hangs under the full suite (2 of 4 runs today, never alone): a pool deadlock in learning. experiment.check takes the experiment row FOR UPDATE inside its transaction (experimentFor(..., true)), then cross() calls another tool on bound.pool, which needs a second connection. Ten concurrent experiment.assign calls each hold a pool connection blocked on that lock, so the pool (max 10) never has one to give
nodes.rationale: Seen in pg_stat_activity during the hang: one backend 'idle in transaction' (ClientRead) right after the experimentUnits SELECT, holding its xact for 10+ minutes; nine backends active, waiting Lock/transactionid on INSERT INTO experiment_assignment. server/modules/learning/index.ts:39-44 (cross uses bound.pool), :460 and :514 (cross inside check), :391-402 (assign). Not calls' code; reported for learning. Fix options: run the cross() calls after the transaction (collect, then execute), or have assign not wait on check's lock (SKIP LOCKED / no row lock in check until the decision), and never acquire a pool connection while holding a transaction.
nodes.closes_when: The learning loop test runs 20 times in a row with no pool timeout, and the pool-size assumption is written in the test.

nodes.title: The analysis contract says every complaining PERSON line is an objection, even when the person agrees later (then both the objection and the commitment are listed), and moments are listed per PERSON line whatever the OUTCOME. The outcome table that fixed round 3 stays. The bench can ablate the contract on DEV only: --prompt-variant current | r4-table (b1a80cf exactly) | r3-stance (bfa7ee7's outcome sentence) | no-outcome-rules; an ablation on TEST is refused and the report header names the contract
nodes.rationale: Answers the round 4 regression (mini objection recall 51/51 -> 43/51 on complain-then-agree calls after b1a80cf). The cause is NOT confirmed here: an ablation needs a real model and the sandbox has none. The arms let the bench worker confirm it on DEV: if r4-table loses objections that r3-stance keeps and no-outcome-rules also keeps, the table crowds out moments; current should keep them with the table.
nodes.reverse_if: The DEV ablation shows current still drops objections, or that the loss is noise against r3-stance (then move the moment rules after OUTCOME, or ask for moments in a second field).

nodes.title: version.restore: a one-step rollback publishes a NEW version equal to an earlier one, moves every deployed binding to it, and stops running experiments; history is never rewritten
nodes.rationale: Enterprise buyers need to undo a worse version in one step. The restore goes through the same createVersion path as publish (compiled once; the brief equals the old one because compile() is deterministic, and would carry any compiler safety fixes made since), behind an A2 card whose plain-English diff is against the live version (the version carrying most of the latest campaign deployment, else the latest published). The hard safety guard runs on the restored config, so a version published before the guard cannot come back with a breach. Every binding with a deployment gets a new 100% row for the restored version; earlier rows stay. Running or aa_pending experiments on the agent are stopped through learning's experiment.stop with the rollback as the reason (stopped, not noted: their control or treatment is no longer what runs). The unpublished draft is kept. The activity reads e.g. 'Meera rolled back Asha to version 1 (as version 3)': activity.list now prefers a row's own payload.line.
nodes.reverse_if: Owners want a rollback to keep experiments running against the restored version, or want the draft reset to the restored config; or campaigns pinned to a version without a deployment need moving too (today only deployments move).

nodes.title: version.candidate (learning's treatment arms) now runs the hard safety guard; before, it caught AI-honesty through the compile lint but not crisis-line or manipulation instructions
nodes.rationale: Found while listing every write path for the lint-move question. A treatment arm reaches real callers, so it must meet the same hard rules as a draft. Test shown failing without the guard line.
nodes.reverse_if: The crisis and manipulation rules move into shared/safety's lint (then compile() refuses them on every path and the explicit guard call is redundant).

nodes.title: The crisis-line and manipulation config checks stay in agents/guard.ts until the safety builder adds them to shared/safety with the Python door; moving them now is not clean
nodes.rationale: Checked 2026-10-24: product/voice/vpvoice/rules.py check_schema() raises on any lint key it does not know (KNOWN['lint'] = T-L1..T-L4), and cases.json lintAgentConfig vectors run on both doors with exact {rule, effect} multisets. Adding T-L5/T-L6 to rules.json without editing rules.py would break the voice runtime at load; editing rules.py is the safety builder's. Options: (A, recommended) the safety builder adds lint T-L5 'crisis lines stay' and T-L6 'no manipulation' to rules.json as {about, any, none} evaluated like T-L1 (none = negated forms such as 'never pressures them'), extends KNOWN and lint_agent_config in rules.py, adds positive and benign vectors to cases.json, and lintAgentConfig emits them as refuse; then guard.ts maps T-L1/T-L5/T-L6 refusals to its plain-English rules and deletes its own two regexes, and compile() refuses them on every path. Seed patterns: guard.ts CRISIS, MANIPULATION, NEGATED. (B) keep guard.ts as the only implementation: every config write goes through agents tools (create, brief.edit, stack/voice/tool, candidate, restore), and the runtime never publishes configs, so behaviour is complete, but there are two sources of hard config rules. (C) add TS-only rules in shared/safety without JSON: rejected, it breaks the one-source, both-doors rule.
nodes.reverse_if: The safety builder lands option A; then guard.ts delegates and this decision is superseded.

nodes.title: Model review of brief text (agents/review.ts, contract shared/safety/brief-review.json), built on the owner's go (open.2026-10-24.tl1-model-check). Regex door first (T-L1 plus the guard's crisis-line and manipulation rules), never weakened; the model reads only briefs the rules let through, field by field, and can only add a finding (human, hide_ai, crisis, manipulation) at or above threshold 0.5. Publish and version.candidate block with the rule, the field, the model's reason and the fix; agent.create and brief.edit return the review as advisory. With no model (VP_LLM_BRIEF_REVIEW_*, falling back to VP_LLM_DEFAULT_*) the publish card says 'AI-honesty review: rules only (no model configured)'; unavailable says why. Recommended: GPT-4.1 through Azure; Flash-Lite through Vertex the alternative. TS only: the voice runtime never reviews briefs, so there is no Python port.
nodes.rationale: Regex T-L1 reaches 23/60 on fresh paraphrase (measure.2026-10-24.tl1-third-person). Briefs change rarely, so a slower, stronger model costs little latency.
nodes.reverse_if: The blind score shows the model adds too many false positives on benign briefs (blocking honest publishes), or misses as much as the regex.

nodes.title: Per-call analysis defaults to tiered (gpt-4.1-mini first, escalating to gpt-4.1 at threshold 0.6, never escalating on engine-decided codes); mini single and gpt-4.1 stay selectable
nodes.rationale: Over three rounds on the same 42 TEST calls (two passes each), tiered scored 41, 41, 42, 42, 42, 42, and mini single 38, 36, 42, 41, 38, 39: 250/252 vs 234/252. Tiered was never worse than mini on any call in any round, and it held steady through three prompt revisions that moved mini by up to 4 calls each way. Mini's swings come from its own false nulls (wrong-person and complaint calls), which tiered catches by escalating 0-5% of calls. Cost: about Rs 0.078-0.095 per 3-minute call against mini's Rs 0.073, inside the Rs 0.17 analysis budget. The letter of the old reverse_if (more than 4/42 in one round) was not met; this decision rests on robustness across rounds, which the old rule did not measure.
nodes.reverse_if: Tiered's measured cost exceeds Rs 0.17 per 3-minute call, or a mini-single contract matches tiered on outcome (within 1/42 on the mean of two TEST passes) in two consecutive rounds with no moment or objection loss.

nodes.title: Every voice-stack part declares its languages as measured or stated; a stack serves a language only if every part does, graded by its weakest part
nodes.rationale: Agents for multilingual lists need to know what each stack can hear, understand and speak. shared/components.ts gives each part a LanguageSupport {measured, stated, source}; shared/stacks.ts stackLanguage()/stackLanguages() derive the per-stack matrix. Measured is limited to what our lab and benches ran: Hinglish on Azure ears, the benched brains, Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite voice, MAI voice and Gemini Live, plus Hindi on Azure ears and the two Gemini/MAI voices; a test refuses any other measured entry. Stated lists are the makers' published support as we understood it on 2026-10-24, restricted to VP's 12 codes, and NOT re-read from vendor docs today. Result on the curated stacks: Kannada, Malayalam, Gujarati, Punjabi and Odia are served only by the two beta stacks (Sarvam, Gemini Live), so none can call real people in those languages yet.
nodes.reverse_if: A docs read or a test call shows a stated entry is wrong (fix the list and its source), or a language is run on our calls (then it moves to measured with the run named).

nodes.title: An agent may speak only languages its voice stack serves: draft writes and every version path refuse otherwise, naming the language, the stack and the part
nodes.rationale: The agent's primary plus allowed languages are its languages. saveDraft refuses a write that introduces an unserved language (e.g. adding Kannada on a stack whose voice cannot speak it, or switching a Tamil agent to the MAI voice stack); createVersion refuses any unserved language for published, candidate, variant and restored versions. Message: 'Kannada is not supported by the voice stack <label>: its voice (<part>) does not support Kannada. Choose a stack that supports Kannada, or remove Kannada from the agent's languages.'
nodes.reverse_if: Owners need to draft ahead of a stack that will support a language (then drafts warn and only versions refuse).

nodes.title: Language variants are immutable agent versions (kind 'variant') with the same facts and agenda; campaigns route each contact to a version that speaks their language, else the main one with the reason recorded
nodes.rationale: version.language_variant (A2) copies a published version's config with languages {primary: L, allowed: [L, English if the stack serves it], mirrorCaller: true} and optionally another stack; it is refused when shared/safety has no checked disclosure line for L (disclosure.json has Hinglish, English, Hindi, Tamil and Bengali today; Kannada, Telugu and the rest need the safety team) and runs the hard guard and language validation. Variants never count as the live version. At claim the worker routes after the experiment or deployment choice (campaigns/languages.ts routeAttempt): explicit campaign.draft languageRoutes first, then the agent's newest variant per language; beta-stack versions are skipped because they cannot dial real people; Hindi and Hinglish serve each other, English is served by English or Hinglish; no match calls with the main version and stores precheck.language {preferred, servedBy, versionId, reason}. The R2 launch warning now counts only those fallbacks and points to version.language_variant.
nodes.reverse_if: Fallback calls in the wrong language show worse outcomes than not calling (then fallback becomes skip-with-reason), or owners want variants as separate agents rather than versions.

nodes.title: The brief review never judges persona or brand settings. persona.name, gender, register, energy, humour and honorific, and brand.name and spokenName, are given to the model as one context line ('the agent is the AI assistant of <brand>; its persona is named <name> (<gender>)'), never as numbered fields, so a finding can never cite them. The prompt says a persona's name, gender, voice or tone is not a breach, and drops 'If unsure ... report it with a lower confidence' for 'report a field only when its own words claim, imply or instruct a breach'. Notes and guidance are still judged in full.

nodes.title: Transcript retention and erasure redact the words in place and keep the metrics (job memory.transcript_purge, every 10 minutes). Calls are purged when the person was erased (forget_request scope erase_me, or a contact intake erased in place), whatever the call's age, or when the call ended longer ago than the workspace's transcripts_days. turn.text is set to '' and heard_text to NULL, and the timing, latency and cut-ins stay. conversation.transcript becomes []. analysis loses every free-text key (summary, points, quotes, quote, text, note, claim, reason, message, body, why) and keeps its codes, counts and verdicts. call_moment quote and note are nulled; outcome.evidence loses quote; hand_off.brief loses summary; this call's quotes leave each call_insight theme. The row records transcript_purged_at and transcript_purge_reason. call.get returns transcriptRemoved, and the call page shows it ('Transcript removed: this workspace keeps transcripts for N days.' or 'Transcript removed on the person's erasure request.').
nodes.rationale: Deleting conversation rows would cascade-delete cost_line, breaking billing and settlement, and would orphan the audit's object ids, outcomes and learning's per-call metrics. Deleting turn rows would lose the reply-gap timing the reports read. Redacting removes every place the caller's words or a model's paraphrase of them live, and keeps what is not personal.
nodes.reverse_if: Counsel requires the conversation row itself to go at erasure, in which case cost lines are first moved to a non-cascading settlement record. Or another table starts storing caller text keyed by conversation, in which case add it to purgeOne.

nodes.title: A recording delete that the voice runtime has not confirmed is a visible pending erasure. calls.recording_purge writes recording_purge_tries, recording_purge_tried_at and recording_purge_error on each failure and clears the error on success. call.get's recording reason adds 'Deleting it is pending: the voice runtime has not confirmed after N tries; it is retried every 10 minutes.' The new read tool erasure.pending lists those calls, plus erased people's calls that still hold audio or words.
nodes.rationale: open.2026-10-24.recording-files-retention-purge: a failed delete is retried and is never silent. Before this it was a console.warn only.
nodes.reverse_if: Erasure becomes synchronous with the request (then the pending state lives on the forget_request receipt instead).

nodes.title: Intake's dpdp.request.execute wrote its forget_request without a scope, so an erase_me request was stored as forget_memory, the column default. calls.recording_purge acts only on scope = 'erase_me', so an erasure done through the product never deleted the recordings. The existing purge test missed it because it wrote scope = 'erase_me' itself.
nodes.tried: Erasure through intake, followed by calls.recording_purge.
nodes.broke: The audio of an erased person was never purged. Fixed: intake stores i.scope. Both purges also treat contact.erased_at as an erasure, so a request row with the wrong scope can no longer hide one. tests/memory-retention.test.ts goes through intake; with the one-line fix reverted, it fails at 'intake stores the scope the purges act on'.

nodes.title: Retention and erasure: tests/memory-retention.test.ts 4/4. (1) Analysis redaction keeps codes and verdicts and drops all free text. (2) A call 31 days old in a 30-day workspace: the text is gone from turn, transcript, analysis, moment, outcome evidence, hand-off brief and insight quotes; the turn rows, latency 640 ms, cost line 2400 milli and outcome are kept; call.get says why and its JSON holds no caller word. A 5-day-old call keeps its words. A run scoped to one workspace touches no other; a second run purges 0. (3) An erase_me request through intake: the forget_request stores scope erase_me, the recording link is refused at once, the transcript is purged with reason erased, and the runtime is asked to purge only that call; another person's call is untouched. (4) The runtime is unreachable twice: erasure.pending shows 2 tries with the error, and call.get says the deletion is pending; once the runtime is back, it is purged and nothing is pending. nodes.title: VP_SPECULATE_PARTIAL is off by default on every provider, paced or not (provider-aware pre-warm stays: on where unpaced). The 2026-10-23 gain (998 -> 750 ms) needed partials that carry every word at once. The Azure brain-stage gain on staging (886 vs 1,096 ms, n=24 vs 5) is better explained by the warm connection, which pre-warm keeps.

nodes.broke: experiment.assign's INSERT INTO experiment_assignment waits on the check's FOR UPDATE (its foreign-key check takes a key-share lock) while holding a pool connection. With the pool dry, the check never got its second connection. The suite hung in 2 of 4 runs (integrator) and 1 of 10 here at each of two pool sizes.

nodes.title: Learning never takes a pooled connection while it holds a lock. cross() runs the sibling tool on the caller's own connection under a savepoint, and the sibling's writes commit or roll back with the caller's. Learning's row locks are FOR NO KEY UPDATE, so foreign-key checks (assignments) never wait on them.
nodes.rationale: rejected.2026-10-24.pooled-call-under-row-lock; measure.2026-10-24.loop-under-full-suite.
nodes.reverse_if: The kernel gains a general nested-execute (Registry.execute on a transaction client); then learning uses that instead of its local sameConnection wrapper.

nodes.method: The whole server suite (every product/tests/*.test.ts except the browser-flow wrapper web.test.ts, concurrency 4 as scripts/test.mjs runs it, a fresh database each run), repeated on a pinned worktree. 20 runs at the default pool and 20 at PG_POOL_MAX=4 on the fix (18c8ea3); 10 runs at each pool size on the commit before (a9c58df). A hang is the loop test's 300 s timeout. Separately, the deterministic regression test (pool 4, 6 assigns + 1 check).
nodes.title: After the fix the learning loop test passed 20 of 20 full-suite runs at the default pool and 20 of 20 at a pool of 4: no pool timeout, 8-12 s each. Before it hung in 1 of 10 at each pool size. On its own that comparison is weak (2/20 vs 0/40); the decisive evidence is the regression test, which deadlocked 3 of 3 before the fix and passes after.

money.test's two MA-08 tests fail together in 7 of 60 full-suite runs here, on the commits both before and after the learning fix ('0' !== '700000' at money.test.ts:458; 'already credited' 1 !== 0 at :480). Likely cause, not verified: resolveTopups scans every workspace's unknown top-ups with the process's own gateway, so it settles other test files' top-ups in the shared database. Routed to money.
nodes.closes_when: MA-08 passes 20 full-suite runs in a row, e.g. with resolveTopups scoped to the test's workspace or the test's top-ups isolated.

nodes.title: The base branch is red on three registry guards since calls' outcome.import (99c0924); reproduced on 0b33102 without learning's commits. activity-subject: outcome.import.importId is neither a subject nor listed as internal. describe-labels: the outcome.import card prints an id ('Record verified outcomes from import 6d83f2c5'). sdk: the tool catalog is behind the registry (run scripts/tool-catalog.ts). Routed to calls; learning did not widen its push to fix another module's tool.

nodes.method: The 42 TEST records of research/2026-10-24/benches-r6/analysis-gpt-4.1-mini.r5-outcome-first-p1.json, replayed through calls' real ingest() and analyse() as the bench feeds them (judge off). The reply is rebuilt per record from its outcome, reason code and moment kinds, with quotes from the case's own lines. Then learning.propose reads them. product/tests/learning-r6.test.ts.
nodes.title: Learning's evidence reads the shipped analysis contract (r5-outcome-first) correctly: 42 of 42 calls store the recorded reason code, AI outcome read and moment kinds; every analysis prompt had OUTCOME before KIND; learning's counts equal the recorded ones; AI reads (more than 20 calls) never count as outcomes ({none: 42}). One leak found and fixed: an opt-out caller's line reached learning through the AI outcome read's quote.

Calls whose words never reach the model that writes the brief are crisis calls AND opted-out calls (reason, end reason, flag, or an opt_out moment). No line of theirs is quoted from a moment, a theme or an AI outcome read; the outcome read keeps only its value and calibration.
nodes.rationale: measure.2026-10-24.learning-reads-r6-contract: the outcome read carried an opt-out caller's line. In r6 the model also tags a crisis line as an objection (3 of 3 crisis records), so crisis calls must never be quoted from objections either.
nodes.reverse_if: Never for crisis. For opt-outs, only if the owner decides opted-out callers' words may train the brief.

nodes.title: Blueprint decision 9 is implemented: after every analysed live call, script.harm_check reads harm-class moments from what analysis stored, with no model call: complaint plus a request for a person, an ignored opt-out, a crisis without Tele-MANAS 14416 or 112, or a caller saying she lied. When 2 fall in any 15 consecutive live calls of one agent version, script_throttle slows its campaigns to 25% of their lines (gate G12, at least 1) and a critical Safety issue names the calls and quotes the moments. A crisis is quoted by her reply, never the caller's words. A member restores with one tap (script.pacing.restore, A1, audited); moments before a restore never re-throttle.
nodes.rationale: The must-be audit (research/2026-10-24/must-be-audit) found decision 9 contradicted: the only live fast lane was a 50-call early-hang-up rate monitor, and only experiment arms had a harm stop.
nodes.reverse_if: Real use shows the floor's wantsHuman or the lie pattern flag ordinary calls (measured as throttles a member restores within an hour with no change); then tighten that rule, never the window.

nodes.method: harmMoments over every analysis-bench case (scripts/analysis-bench/cases.ts, 72 Hinglish + 12 regional, synthetic), with each case's keyed moments, reason code, end reason and outcome.
nodes.title: Only the 6 complaint cases flag (complaint_human). None of the agreed, callback, not-interested, wrong-person, opt-out (the call ends on it), question, language-mismatch, crisis (she gives the line), early-hang-up, no-answer or objection-resolved cases flag.
